bilingual_description.en: The mass air flow sensor (MAF) sits between the air filter and the throttle or compressor and measures how much air the engine draws in; fuel quantity, load and ignition are calculated from it. Most are hot-film or hot-wire sensors that output either a voltage or, on GM, Saab and newer Ford systems, a frequency. P0102 means the signal is below its electrical lower limit – a frequency that is too low or a voltage that is too low. Documented limits: GM petrol 450 Hz or less, GM diesel below 276 Hz, Ford digital below 1.5 kHz for 5 s, Ford analogue below 0.244 V. GM and Saab need two trips; the engine runs on a calculated substitute value.

description: The manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor measures the pressure behind the throttle; on vehicles without a separate barometric sensor it also supplies the ambient pressure, read at key-on or wide-open throttle – hence 'MAP/BARO'. It is a three-wire sensor with 5 V reference, ground and signal. P0105 is the general circuit fault and is rarely used today: most petrol engines report low, high and intermittent separately (P0107–P0109). It appears mainly where the fault cannot be broken down further – Ford's 2023 diesels set it when the digital SENT sensor reports a bad status or an out-of-limit value for 5 s (lost communication is a separate U code), and Bosch EDC16 diesels use it with a fault type byte, for example signal below 0.2 V. Saab then substitutes 101.3 kPa, limits torque and switches off EGR and boost control.
possible_causes: Connector or wiring to the sensor open, shorted or loose [HIGH]
MAP sensor faulty (oiled, failed internally, SENT status fault) [MEDIUM]
Sensor hose disconnected, vacuum or boost leak [MEDIUM]
5 V reference pulled down by another sensor on the same circuit [LOW]
Engine control module faulty [LOW]

bilingual_description.de: Der Saugrohrdrucksensor (MAP) misst den Druck hinter der Drosselklappe; bei Fahrzeugen ohne eigenen Luftdrucksensor liefert er auch den Umgebungsdruck, gelesen bei Zündung ein oder Vollgas – daher „MAP/BARO“. Er ist ein Dreileiter-Sensor mit 5-V-Referenz, Masse und Signal. P0105 ist der allgemeine Stromkreisfehler und wird heute selten genutzt: Die meisten Benziner melden zu niedrig, zu hoch und sporadisch getrennt (P0107–P0109). Er erscheint vor allem dort, wo sich der Fehler nicht weiter aufschlüsseln lässt – Fords Diesel von 2023 setzen ihn, wenn der digitale SENT-Sensor 5 s lang einen schlechten Status oder einen Wert außerhalb der Grenzen meldet (ausgefallene Kommunikation ist ein eigener U-Code), und Bosch-EDC16-Diesel nutzen ihn mit Fehlerart-Byte, etwa für ein Signal unter 0,2 V. Saab rechnet dann mit 101,3 kPa, begrenzt das Drehmoment und schaltet Abgasrückführung und Ladedruckregelung ab.

symptoms: Loss of power, limp mode with torque limit (diesel)
Rough idle, hard starting, higher consumption (petrol)

description: The manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor measures the pressure behind the throttle; on vehicles without a separate barometric sensor it also supplies the ambient pressure, read at key-on or wide-open throttle – hence 'MAP/BARO'. It is a three-wire sensor with 5 V reference, ground and signal. P0106 is a plausibility fault: the signal is electrically valid but implausible – stuck, offset or drifting. Two tests are common. With the engine stopped, all pressures equalise, so MAP must match ambient (and boost) pressure; Ford allows 1.5–3 inHg. While running, MAP is compared with a value modelled from air mass, throttle and speed – GM blames the MAP sensor above about 23–30 kPa error, with two trips on petrol and one on diesel. Turbo engines with three sensors find the odd one out by majority. Besides the sensor, intake or boost leaks often cause it.
possible_causes: Vacuum leak at the intake manifold or boost leak (hose, clamp, charge air cooler) [HIGH]
Sensor oiled or sooted, port blocked (EGR soot), characteristic drifted [HIGH]
High resistance in signal, reference or ground wire [MEDIUM]
Comparison sensor wrong, or mechanical cause (dirty throttle, EGR stuck open) [MEDIUM]

bilingual_description.en: Sensor B is a second mass air flow sensor in a second intake path, found on engines with two air filter boxes – for example the Nissan VR30DDTT twin-turbo V6 (where sensor B belongs to bank 2) or GM's 3.0 litre twin-turbo V6. P010B is the plausibility fault of sensor B: the signal is electrically valid but does not fit. GM checks it like sensor A against a model built from the other sensors (manifold pressure, boost, throttle, sensor A) and fails it above 20 g/s deviation, with two trips. For the VR30DDTT Nissan names a loose or leaking left-hand intake pipe as the main cause and warns against touching or dismantling the sensor. Other causes match P0101: a soiled element, a clogged filter on that side or a boost leak.

P010B ist der Plausibilitätsfehler von Sensor B: Das Signal ist elektrisch gültig, passt aber nicht. GM prüft ihn wie Sensor A gegen ein Modell aus den übrigen Sensoren (Saugrohrdruck, Ladedruck, Drosselklappe, Sensor A) und wertet ab 20 g/s Abweichung, mit zwei Fahrzyklen. Beim VR30DDTT nennt Nissan ein lose sitzendes oder undichtes linkes Ansaugrohr als Hauptursache und warnt davor, den Sensor zu berühren oder zu zerlegen. Weitere Ursachen entsprechen P0101: verschmutztes Messelement, verstopfter Luftfilter auf dieser Seite oder ein Ladeluftleck.

description: Engines with two intake paths have two mass air flow sensors, A and B. On a symmetrical V engine both sides should draw about the same amount of air, so the readings can be compared with each other. P010F is set when both signals are electrically valid but differ by more than allowed; the code does not say which side is wrong. No manufacturer document using exactly this code or its threshold was found: GM's twin-turbo V6 and Nissan's VR30DDTT assess each sensor separately against a model (P0101/P010B). The description therefore rests on the CARB requirement for plausibility checks and on component sources for engines with two sensors. Typical causes are a leaking intake pipe or a soiled sensor on one side.

One of the two sensors contaminated or aged [HIGH]
Air filter on one side clogged or wrongly fitted [MEDIUM]
Turbocharger or boost problem on one bank [LOW]
Contact resistance in connector or wiring [LOW]

description: Intake air temperature sensor 1 is the first air temperature sensor in the intake path; depending on the vehicle it is built into the mass air flow sensor, mounted near the air filter or, on some naturally aspirated GM engines, fitted in the intake manifold. Most versions are NTC thermistors in a 5 V divider: the hotter the air, the lower the signal voltage. P0110 is the general circuit fault. With a conventional analogue sensor most manufacturers report low and high signals separately (P0112/P0113), so P0110 mainly appears in two cases: with digital (SENT) sensors that combine air mass and temperature, where it stands for lost communication or an implausible status (Ford diesel 2023, after about 5 s), and in some Bosch systems as a collective code whose fault type byte tells open circuit from short to ground. The control module then uses a substitute temperature; some systems also limit torque.

Sensor or mass air flow sensor with built-in temperature sensor faulty [HIGH]

description: Intake air temperature sensor 1 is the first air temperature sensor in the intake path; depending on the vehicle it is built into the mass air flow sensor, mounted near the air filter or, on some naturally aspirated GM engines, fitted in the intake manifold. Most versions are NTC thermistors in a 5 V divider: the hotter the air, the lower the signal voltage. P0111 is a plausibility fault: the signal is electrically valid but does not fit. The usual test runs at key-on after a long soak (Ford 6 h, GM 8 h): the intake air sensor is compared with other temperature sensors such as coolant, cylinder head, charge air cooler or IAT2, which should all read about the same. GM flags it above about 25 °C deviation, Ford above about 17 °C; Ford first confirms with a drive above 40 mph because sunshine can warm a sensor, and also sets P0111 if the air reads over 66 °C while driving. A detected block heater suspends the test. Two consecutive trips are needed.

Ford zählt kurze Ausreißer außerhalb des Bereichs, die einzeln zu kurz für P0112/P0113 sind, und setzt den Code nach zehn davon in einem Fahrzyklus. GM bewertet das Rauschen im gültigen Bereich: Summieren sich die alle 100 ms gelesenen Werte innerhalb einer Sekunde zu mehr als 80 °C Bewegung, und das in vier von fünf Sekunden, gilt die Probe als fehlerhaft. GM braucht zwei Fahrzyklen. Typischer Auslöser ist ein Wackelkontakt, der bei Motorbewegung öffnet.

description: The engine coolant temperature sensor 1 is an NTC thermistor: the control module feeds 5 V through a resistor, and as the coolant warms the resistance and signal voltage fall. Its value drives cold-start enrichment, idle speed, ignition timing, the radiator fan and the release of closed-loop mixture control. Some Ford engines measure cylinder head temperature instead and calculate a coolant value from it. P0116 is a plausibility fault: the signal is electrically valid but not believable. Most often it checks for a sensor stuck too warm. After a long soak (GM 8 h, Ford 6 h) coolant must be close to intake air temperature; GM fails it above about 19 °C difference without a detected block heater, Ford if it reads over 110 °C or sits at 79–110 °C. Ford diesels instead check whether coolant warms fast enough in frost. A sensor stuck warm suppresses cold-start enrichment and can defeat the thermostat monitor, which is why CARB requires this test. GM uses one or two trips depending on the engine.
possible_causes: Sensor drifting and reading too warm (ageing, coolant ingress) [HIGH]
Corrosion or contact resistance in connector or wiring [MEDIUM]
Block heater or preheater not detected [MEDIUM]
Comparison sensor (intake air, ambient) wrong [LOW]
Control module calibration [LOW]

description: The engine coolant temperature sensor 1 is an NTC thermistor: the control module feeds 5 V through a resistor, and as the coolant warms the resistance and signal voltage fall. Its value drives cold-start enrichment, idle speed, ignition timing, the radiator fan and the release of closed-loop mixture control. Some Ford engines measure cylinder head temperature instead and calculate a coolant value from it. P0117 means the signal voltage is too low, so the sensor would report an implausibly hot engine (around 140–160 °C). Usual causes are a signal wire shorted to ground, coolant or moisture in the connector, or an internally shorted sensor. Limits: GM below 55 ohms, Ford petrol below 0.244 V for 5 s, Ford diesel below 0.10 V, Mitsubishi below 0.1 V for 2 s. Mitsubishi then calculates with 80 °C; GM/Saab switch the radiator fan on and the A/C compressor off. GM needs two trips. On Ford engines with a head temperature sensor the equivalent is P1290.
possible_causes: Signal wire shorted to ground (chafing, pinched harness) [HIGH]
Sensor shorted internally or coolant inside the sensor [HIGH]
Moisture or coolant in the connector [MEDIUM]
Engine control module faulty [LOW]

symptoms: Rich mixture, higher consumption, possibly black smoke or fuel smell

description: The engine coolant temperature sensor 1 is an NTC thermistor: the control module feeds 5 V through a resistor, and as the coolant warms the resistance and signal voltage fall. Its value drives cold-start enrichment, idle speed, ignition timing, the radiator fan and the release of closed-loop mixture control. Some Ford engines measure cylinder head temperature instead and calculate a coolant value from it. Coolant temperature can only change slowly because of the thermal mass involved. P0119 is set when the reading jumps faster than physically possible. GM calculates, every second, a window for the next valid value from the previous reading and a sensor time constant of 13 s; readings outside it in three of four samples count as a fault, monitored continuously over two trips. GM/Saab set it after more than 4 s of abrupt changes and then run the radiator fan. Typical causes are loose contacts or a harness chafing as the engine moves.

Harness chafing that briefly grounds or opens with engine movement [MEDIUM]
Sensor with internal crack or contact fault [MEDIUM]
Air pockets at the sensor (poorly bled cooling system) [LOW]

Occasional rough running or idle fluctuation

description: Some engines have two coolant temperature sensors that check each other. P011A is set when both are electrically fine but their readings differ more than a calibrated amount under conditions where they should agree. Mazda documents the code for the 2013–2016 CX-5 and 2014–2016 Mazda6: sensor 2 sits in the heater hose, and a clogged heater core keeps it noticeably colder, so P011A often comes with weak cabin heat although both sensors are good. Mazda's check is to compare both sensors with ambient temperature after an overnight soak and then the temperature difference across the heater hoses. A block heater used below 0 °C can also trigger it.
possible_causes: Clogged heater core or restricted coolant flow at sensor 2 [HIGH]
One of the two sensors drifting [MEDIUM]
Air in the cooling system or low coolant level [MEDIUM]
Block heater use in frost [LOW]
Contact resistance at one sensor [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 1200€ (0.5h - 6h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

P011A is set when both are electrically fine but their readings differ more than a calibrated amount under conditions where they should agree. Mazda documents the code for the 2013–2016 CX-5 and 2014–2016 Mazda6: sensor 2 sits in the heater hose, and a clogged heater core keeps it noticeably colder, so P011A often comes with weak cabin heat although both sensors are good. A block heater used below 0 °C can also trigger it.
bilingual_description.de: Manche Motoren haben zwei Kühlmitteltemperatursensoren, die sich gegenseitig prüfen. P011A wird gesetzt, wenn beide elektrisch in Ordnung sind, ihre Werte aber stärker als kalibriert voneinander abweichen, obwohl sie übereinstimmen müssten. Mazda dokumentiert den Code beim CX-5 von 2013–2016 und Mazda6 von 2014–2016: Sensor 2 sitzt im Heizungsschlauch, und ein verstopfter Heizungswärmetauscher hält ihn deutlich kälter – P011A kommt dann oft zusammen mit schwacher Heizleistung, obwohl beide Sensoren intakt sind. Mazda prüft, indem beide Sensoren nach einer Nacht Standzeit mit der Außentemperatur verglichen werden und danach der Temperaturunterschied an den Heizungsschläuchen. Auch eine unter 0 °C genutzte Standheizung kann ihn auslösen.

description: After a long standstill the coolant and the intake air should both have settled close to ambient temperature. P011B compares the two sensors at start-up and is set when they disagree without either sensor showing a circuit fault. In the documented GM/Saab version the engine must have been off for more than 10 hours with no preheater detected; the fault counts if coolant reads at least 20 °C above intake air, or intake air at least 30 °C above coolant, and the coolant reading barely moves (2 °C or less) in the first 45 s. The code does not say which sensor is wrong – that has to be found by comparing both with the actual ambient temperature. Toyota resolved false settings on some 2015 V6 engines with new software. Ford and GM report the same idea under the individual sensor codes.
possible_causes: Coolant temperature sensor stuck or drifting [HIGH]
Intake air temperature sensor drifting or heat-soaked [MEDIUM]
Undetected preheater or uneven cooling [MEDIUM]
Contact resistance at a sensor connector or ground [MEDIUM]
Control module software (false setting, update available) [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 40€ - 300€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_title.en: Engine Coolant Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation

bilingual_description.en: After a long standstill the coolant and the intake air should both have settled close to ambient temperature. P011B compares the two sensors at start-up and is set when they disagree without either sensor showing a circuit fault. In the documented GM/Saab version the engine must have been off for more than 10 hours with no preheater detected; the fault counts if coolant reads at least 20 °C above intake air, or intake air at least 30 °C above coolant, and the coolant reading barely moves (2 °C or less) in the first 45 s. The code does not say which sensor is wrong – that has to be found by comparing both with the actual ambient temperature. Toyota resolved false settings on some 2015 V6 engines with new software. Ford and GM report the same idea under the individual sensor codes.
bilingual_description.de: Nach langer Standzeit sollten Kühlmittel und Ansaugluft beide nahe der Umgebungstemperatur liegen. P011B vergleicht die zwei Sensoren beim Start und wird gesetzt, wenn sie nicht zusammenpassen, ohne dass einer einen Stromkreisfehler zeigt. In der dokumentierten GM/Saab-Fassung muss der Motor über 10 Stunden gestanden haben, ohne erkannte Vorwärmung; als Fehler zählt, wenn das Kühlmittel mindestens 20 °C über der Ansaugluft liegt oder umgekehrt die Ansaugluft mindestens 30 °C darüber, und sich die Kühlmittelanzeige in den ersten 45 s kaum (höchstens 2 °C) bewegt. Welcher Sensor falsch liegt, verrät der Code nicht – das klärt der Vergleich beider Werte mit der tatsächlichen Außentemperatur. Toyota hat Fehlauslösungen bei einigen V6 von 2015 per Software behoben. Ford und GM melden dieselbe Prüfidee unter den Einzelcodes der Sensoren.

symptoms: With a wrong coolant reading: poor cold start, higher consumption or odd fan behaviour
Code often returns only after an overnight soak

description: On turbocharged engines a charge air cooler temperature sensor sits downstream of the compressor, usually after the charge air cooler, and intake air temperature sensor 1 sits upstream near the air filter. While driving they differ by design, because compression heats the air. After a long standstill, however, both should read nearly the same, so the check runs at start-up. P011C is set when the two bank 1 sensors disagree there, without naming the faulty one. No manufacturer document using exactly this code was found; Ford performs the same comparison after 6 hours (tolerance about 17 °C on petrol, 16 °C on the 2023 diesel) but reports the outlier as P007B, P0111 or P00CE.
possible_causes: Charge air cooler temperature sensor drifting, oily or stuck [HIGH]
Intake air temperature sensor 1 drifting [MEDIUM]
Contact resistance at connector or shared ground [MEDIUM]
Undetected preheating or uneven cooling (sun, residual heat) [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 300€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

While driving they differ by design, because compression heats the air. After a long standstill, however, both should read nearly the same, so the check runs at start-up. P011C is set when the two bank 1 sensors disagree there, without naming the faulty one. Im Fahrbetrieb unterscheiden sich ihre Werte zwangsläufig, weil die Verdichtung die Luft erwärmt. Nach langer Standzeit sollten aber beide fast gleich anzeigen, deshalb läuft die Prüfung beim Start. P011C wird gesetzt, wenn die beiden Sensoren der Bank 1 dort nicht übereinstimmen, ohne den schuldigen zu benennen. Eine Herstellerunterlage mit genau diesem Code wurde nicht gefunden; Ford macht denselben Vergleich nach 6 Stunden (Toleranz rund 17 °C beim Benziner, 16 °C beim Diesel 2023), meldet den Ausreißer aber als P007B, P0111 oder P00CE.

description: This is the bank 2 counterpart of P011C and only exists on engines with two separate intake paths, each with its own charge air cooler temperature sensor and intake air temperature sensor – for example V engines with twin turbochargers and separate charge air coolers. After a long standstill both bank 2 sensors should read nearly the same; if they disagree at start-up, without either showing a circuit fault, P011D is set. The code does not identify which sensor is wrong. No manufacturer document using exactly this code was found; the check follows the same principle Ford uses for bank 1 after 6 hours, with a preheater suspending it.

description: After a long standstill, typically six to eight hours, the coolant should have cooled to roughly the outside air temperature measured by the ambient sensor in the bumper or mirror. P011E compares coolant temperature sensor 1 with the ambient sensor at start-up and is set when they differ beyond a calibrated limit and no preheater was detected. The code does not say which of the two sensors is wrong. description: Sensor A is, in practice, throttle position sensor 1 at the throttle body; the accelerator pedal has its own codes (P2120 onwards). With a cable-operated throttle there is a single potentiometer (about 0.5 V closed to 4.5 V wide open). Electronic throttles have two sensors sharing a 5 V reference and ground, usually running in opposite directions – on GM throttle sensor 1 falls from 3–4 V at idle to below 1 V at full throttle. description: Closed-loop mixture control using the oxygen sensors is only released once the coolant has reached a minimum temperature. CARB requires that this happens within set times – from 2006 two minutes if the engine starts up to 8 °C below the release temperature, five minutes if 8–19 °C below. P0125 means it took too long. Ford checks once per cold start and fails if coolant is still below 10 °C while its model already expects over 27 °C; Mitsubishi expects about 7 °C within 90–300 s and also fails if coolant drops back below 40 °C. Long idling suspends the test. Usual causes are a thermostat stuck open or a sensor reading too cold. GM does not use this code in the tables checked.

Coolant sensor reading too cold or slow (drift, contact resistance) [HIGH]
Low coolant level or air at the sensor [MEDIUM]
Much idling or coasting in frost [LOW]
Engine control module [LOW]

bilingual_description.de: Die Lambdaregelung über die Sauerstoffsensoren wird erst freigegeben, wenn das Kühlmittel eine Mindesttemperatur erreicht hat. CARB verlangt, dass das in festen Zeiten geschieht – ab 2006 in zwei Minuten, wenn der Motor bis 8 °C unter der Freigabetemperatur startet, in fünf Minuten bei 8–19 °C darunter. P0125 heißt, es hat zu lange gedauert. Ford prüft einmal je Kaltstart und wertet einen Fehler, wenn das Kühlmittel noch unter 10 °C liegt, während das Modell schon über 27 °C erwartet; Mitsubishi erwartet etwa 7 °C in 90–300 s und wertet auch, wenn das Kühlmittel wieder unter 40 °C fällt. Langer Leerlauf setzt die Prüfung aus. Übliche Ursachen sind ein offen hängender Thermostat oder ein zu kalt messender Sensor. GM nutzt den Code in den geprüften Tabellen nicht.

symptoms: Engine warms up slowly, heater stays cold for a long time

description: The generic title refers to a coolant temperature that is not reached for stable operation, i.e. for releasing further functions and diagnostics; how manufacturers implement it differs. The only implementation documented in a manufacturer source is Subaru's (via the Saab 9-2X service information): there P0126 is a stuck-sensor check – if the coolant signal changes by less than 5 mV during 20 s of driving or idling after start, the sensor counts as frozen. It runs once per drive cycle, lights the MIL after two consecutive cycles and has no fail-safe mode. Other interpretations, closer to a thermostat check, could not be verified in a manufacturer document.
possible_causes: Coolant sensor frozen or faulty (resistance does not change) [HIGH]
Thermostat stuck open or low coolant [MEDIUM]
Contact resistance in connector or wiring [LOW]
Engine control module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 30€ - 300€ (0.3h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_description.en: The generic title refers to a coolant temperature that is not reached for stable operation, i.e. for releasing further functions and diagnostics; how manufacturers implement it differs. The only implementation documented in a manufacturer source is Subaru's (via the Saab 9-2X service information): there P0126 is a stuck-sensor check – if the coolant signal changes by less than 5 mV during 20 s of driving or idling after start, the sensor counts as frozen. It runs once per drive cycle, lights the MIL after two consecutive cycles and has no fail-safe mode. Other interpretations, closer to a thermostat check, could not be verified in a manufacturer document.
bilingual_description.de: Der generische Titel meint eine Kühlmitteltemperatur, die für stabilen Betrieb – also die Freigabe weiterer Funktionen und Diagnosen – nicht erreicht wird; die Umsetzung unterscheidet sich je Hersteller. Die einzige in einer Herstellerquelle dokumentierte Umsetzung ist die von Subaru (über die Saab-9-2X-Werkstattinfo): Dort ist P0126 eine Prüfung auf einen hängenden Sensor – ändert sich das Kühlmittelsignal in 20 s Fahrt oder Leerlauf nach dem Start um weniger als 5 mV, gilt der Sensor als eingefroren. Sie läuft einmal je Fahrzyklus, schaltet die Motorkontrollleuchte nach zwei aufeinanderfolgenden Zyklen ein und hat keinen Notlauf. Andere, eher thermostatnahe Deutungen ließen sich in keiner Herstellerunterlage belegen.

symptoms: Engine and heater warm up slowly

description: P0127 is not a circuit fault but a functional check of the air path: the measured intake air temperature is too high for the operating state. The logic is documented for a Bosch EDC16 diesel (Saab 9-3): if the intake air exceeds 130 °C and does not fall below it within 45 s after the exhaust gas recirculation valve is closed, hot exhaust gas is evidently still entering or the sensor is wrong. The engine then disables EGR and runs in limp mode with reduced torque. GM has the code in its diesel software but disabled for US OBD II; Ford reports an overly hot intake air reading as P0111 instead. On other engines a hot reading can also come from warm under-bonnet air being drawn in.
possible_causes: EGR valve stuck open or not sealing (diesel) [HIGH]
EGR cooler clogged or bypass flap stuck in bypass [MEDIUM]
Charge air cooler dirty or airflow through it blocked [MEDIUM]
Sensor reading wrong, or hot engine-bay air drawn in (loose intake duct) [MEDIUM]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 1200€ (0.5h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_title.en: Intake Air Temperature Too High

bilingual_description.en: P0127 is not a circuit fault but a functional check of the air path: the measured intake air temperature is too high for the operating state. The logic is documented for a Bosch EDC16 diesel (Saab 9-3): if the intake air exceeds 130 °C and does not fall below it within 45 s after the exhaust gas recirculation valve is closed, hot exhaust gas is evidently still entering or the sensor is wrong. The engine then disables EGR and runs in limp mode with reduced torque. GM has the code in its diesel software but disabled for US OBD II; Ford reports an overly hot intake air reading as P0111 instead. On other engines a hot reading can also come from warm under-bonnet air being drawn in.
bilingual_description.de: P0127 ist kein Stromkreisfehler, sondern eine Funktionsprüfung der Luftstrecke: Die gemessene Ansauglufttemperatur ist für den Betriebszustand zu hoch. Dokumentiert ist die Logik bei einem Bosch-EDC16-Diesel (Saab 9-3): Liegt die Ansaugluft über 130 °C und fällt sie nach dem Schließen des Abgasrückführventils nicht binnen 45 s darunter, strömt offenbar weiter heißes Abgas ein oder der Sensor zeigt falsch. Der Motor schaltet dann die Abgasrückführung ab und geht mit reduziertem Drehmoment in den Notlauf. GM hat den Code in der Diesel-Software, für US-OBD II aber abgeschaltet; Ford meldet eine zu heiße Ansaugluft stattdessen als P0111. Bei anderen Motoren kann ein hoher Wert auch von angesaugter warmer Motorraumluft stammen.

symptoms: Loss of power, limp mode with torque limit
Knock tendency and retarded ignition on petrol engines

description: After a cold start the thermostat stays closed so the engine warms up quickly. CARB requires the coolant to reach a temperature at most 11 °C below the thermostat's rated value within a set time. GM models the heat put in (fuel energy minus losses to ambient, cabin heater and coasting) and fails if enough energy has gone in without coolant reaching about 65 °C (55 °C in cold weather). Ford compares the measured value with a modelled one, typically failing below 78 °C with an 89 °C thermostat. The test runs once per drive cycle, pauses with much idling or below about −7 °C, and needs two trips. Usually the thermostat is stuck open; a sensor reading too low is the other suspect.

Driving pattern or conditions (much idling, extreme cold, strong heating) [LOW]

bilingual_description.de: Nach einem Kaltstart bleibt der Thermostat geschlossen, damit der Motor schnell warm wird. CARB verlangt, dass das Kühlmittel in einer festen Zeit eine Temperatur höchstens 11 °C unter dem Nennwert des Thermostats erreicht. GM rechnet die zugeführte Wärme mit (Energie des Kraftstoffs abzüglich Verlusten an Umgebung, Innenraumheizung und Schubphasen) und wertet einen Fehler, wenn genug Energie geflossen ist, ohne dass das Kühlmittel etwa 65 °C (bei Kälte 55 °C) erreicht. Ford vergleicht den Messwert mit einem Modellwert, typisch Fehler unter 78 °C bei einem 89-°C-Thermostat. Die Prüfung läuft einmal je Fahrzyklus, pausiert bei viel Leerlauf oder unter etwa −7 °C und braucht zwei Fahrzyklen. Meist hängt der Thermostat offen; zweiter Verdächtiger ist ein zu niedrig messender Sensor.

symptoms: Temperature gauge stays low or drops while driving
Heater does not get properly warm

description: The engine control module needs the ambient air pressure for mixture, altitude correction and boost limits. It comes either from a dedicated barometric sensor or from the MAP sensor, read at key-on with the engine stopped and updated at wide-open throttle. P0129 means this value is lower than physically possible – even on the highest drivable passes air pressure stays around 50 kPa, and GM and Ford use 50 kPa as their lower plausibility limit. Usual causes are a MAP or baro sensor reading too low, a blocked sensor port or high resistance in the wiring. No manufacturer document naming exactly this code was found: GM and Ford file the same finding under P2227.
possible_causes: MAP or baro sensor reading too low (dirty, oiled, drifted) [HIGH]
High resistance or corrosion in signal wire or connector [MEDIUM]
Sensor port or hose blocked [MEDIUM]
Control module (baro sensor often built in) or software [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 20€ - 250€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_description.de: Das Motorsteuergerät braucht den Umgebungsluftdruck für Gemisch, Höhenkorrektur und Ladedruckgrenzen. Er kommt entweder von einem eigenen Luftdrucksensor oder vom Saugrohrdrucksensor, gelesen bei Zündung ein und stehendem Motor und bei Vollgas nachgeführt. P0129 heißt, dieser Wert ist niedriger als physikalisch möglich – selbst auf den höchsten befahrbaren Pässen liegt der Luftdruck um 50 kPa, und GM wie Ford setzen 50 kPa als untere Plausibilitätsgrenze. Übliche Ursachen sind ein zu niedrig messender Saugrohr- oder Luftdrucksensor, eine verstopfte Sensorbohrung oder hoher Übergangswiderstand in der Leitung. Eine Herstellerunterlage mit genau diesem Code wurde nicht gefunden: GM und Ford legen denselben Befund unter P2227 ab.

symptoms: Rich mixture, higher consumption, rough idle

description: The turbocharger/supercharger inlet pressure sensor A sits between the air filter and the compressor. The engine uses it for the compressor pressure ratio, to judge air filter restriction (ambient minus inlet pressure) and to cross-check the other pressure sensors. P012A is the general circuit fault. Ford's 2023 diesels use a digital SENT sensor here and set P012A when its error flag is raised or the value exceeds a limit for 5 s; lost communication is reported separately (U068B). FCA's 2019 Jeep Wrangler 2.0 turbo could set P012A, P012C and P012D falsely and was fixed with new engine software, so the software level is worth checking before replacing parts. GM's supercharged V8 uses only P012B–P012D. A substitute value, usually ambient pressure, is used.
possible_causes: Connector or wiring open, corroded or shorted [HIGH]
Sensor faulty (SENT sensor reports internal error) [MEDIUM]
Control module software (false setting) [MEDIUM]
Engine control module faulty [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 20€ - 250€ (0.3h - 1h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_description.de: Der Eintrittsdrucksensor A des Turboladers bzw. Kompressors sitzt zwischen Luftfilter und Verdichter. Das Steuergerät nutzt ihn für das Druckverhältnis des Verdichters, zur Beurteilung des Luftfilterwiderstands (Umgebungsdruck minus Eintrittsdruck) und zum Abgleich der übrigen Drucksensoren. P012A ist der allgemeine Stromkreisfehler. Fords Diesel von 2023 haben hier einen digitalen SENT-Sensor und setzen P012A, wenn dessen Fehlerbit gesetzt ist oder der Wert 5 s lang eine Grenze überschreitet; ausgefallene Kommunikation wird getrennt gemeldet (U068B). Beim Jeep Wrangler 2.0 Turbo von 2019 konnte FCA-Software P012A, P012C und P012D fälschlich setzen, behoben per Software-Update – vor einem Teiletausch lohnt also der Blick auf den Softwarestand. description: The turbocharger/supercharger inlet pressure sensor A sits between the air filter and the compressor. The engine uses it for the compressor pressure ratio, to judge air filter restriction (ambient minus inlet pressure) and to cross-check the other pressure sensors. P012B is a plausibility fault: the signal is electrically valid but stuck or offset. On GM's supercharged 6.2 V8 the sensor must read 50–115 kPa and agree within 10 kPa with MAP and ambient pressure after the engine has been off for more than 8 s; while running, it is compared with modelled values (fault above about 25–30 kPa). GM normally needs two trips, one in some 2019 applications. In operation inlet pressure is slightly below ambient because of filter losses, so a clogged filter or blocked intake lowers it further.
possible_causes: Sensor oiled (crankcase vent often joins before the compressor) or drifted [HIGH]
Air filter heavily clogged or intake blocked or collapsed [MEDIUM]
Leak in the intake pipe between filter and compressor or at the sensor flange [MEDIUM]
High resistance in the wiring [MEDIUM]
Comparison sensor (MAP, baro, MAF) wrong or software [LOW]

symptoms: Loss of power or boost limitation

description: The turbocharger/supercharger inlet pressure sensor A sits between the air filter and the compressor. The engine uses it for the compressor pressure ratio, to judge air filter restriction (ambient minus inlet pressure) and to cross-check the other pressure sensors. P012C means the signal voltage is below its lower limit – typically a signal wire shorted to ground, an open signal or 5 V reference wire, or a failed sensor. GM's supercharged V8 sets it below 3 % of the 5 V reference (about 0.15 V), with 320 of 400 samples failing, continuously monitored; two trips are normal, one in some 2019 applications. FCA documented false settings on the 2019 Jeep Wrangler 2.0 turbo that were cured by a software update. A substitute value is used and power may be limited.
possible_causes: Connector unplugged or corroded, signal or reference wire open [HIGH]
Signal wire shorted to ground [MEDIUM]
Sensor failed internally [MEDIUM]
Control module software (false setting) [LOW]
5 V reference shorted by another sensor [LOW]

description: The turbocharger/supercharger inlet pressure sensor A sits ahead of the compressor – between air filter and turbocharger, or on GM's supercharged V8 between throttle and supercharger. It is an analogue 5 V pressure sensor used for the compressor pressure ratio, filter restriction and cross-checks with the other pressure sensors. symptoms: Reduced power or limp mode possible

description: The turbocharger/supercharger inlet pressure sensor A sits ahead of the compressor – between air filter and turbocharger, or on GM's supercharged V8 between throttle and supercharger. It is an analogue 5 V pressure sensor used for the compressor pressure ratio, filter restriction and cross-checks with the other pressure sensors. P012E covers a signal that jumps or drops out briefly without staying below or above the circuit limits – typically a loose contact. Such intermittent monitors usually count short limit violations or changes faster than real pressure can move. No manufacturer document using exactly this code was found: GM handles jumps of this sensor through its range check P012B and the counting windows of P012C/P012D, and Ford's 2023 diesels report their digital sensor under P012A. The description therefore rests on CARB's circuit monitoring requirement and component information. A substitute value is used while the fault is present.
possible_causes: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector [HIGH]
Broken or chafed wire making intermittent contact [MEDIUM]
Sensor faulty internally (erratic output) [MEDIUM]
Control module or software [LOW]

symptoms: Occasional power reduction or boost fluctuation

description: P012F compares the coolant temperature sensor with the engine oil temperature sensor. The documented user is Ford's Power Stroke diesel. After a calibration update for the 6.0 litre engine, Ford uses it to monitor oil cooler efficiency: if the oil gets much hotter than the coolant at certain speed and load, the oil-to-coolant heat exchanger is probably clogged, and P012F sets together with the wrench lamp. On the 6.7 litre (2015–2018) several bulletins treat P012F as a false setting – partly below 5 °C ambient – cured by reprogramming the engine module. Ford's 2023 diesels run the cold-start comparison of coolant against oil temperature (35 °C limit after 6 h) under P0196 instead. GM does not use the code, and the code does not say which sensor or which system is at fault.
possible_causes: Oil cooler (oil-to-coolant heat exchanger) clogged – oil much hotter than coolant [HIGH]
Engine module software (false setting, especially in cold weather) [MEDIUM]
Coolant or oil temperature sensor inaccurate, or its wiring faulty [MEDIUM]
Thermostat stuck open or low coolant [LOW]
Block heater in use (only coolant preheated) [LOW]

Nach einem Kalibrier-Update für den 6,0-Liter-Motor überwacht Ford damit den Wirkungsgrad des Ölkühlers: Wird das Öl bei bestimmter Drehzahl und Last deutlich heißer als das Kühlmittel, ist der Öl-Kühlmittel-Wärmetauscher vermutlich zugesetzt, und P012F wird zusammen mit der Schraubenschlüsselleuchte gesetzt. Beim 6,7-Liter (2015–2018) behandeln mehrere Bulletins P012F als Fehlauslösung – teils unter 5 °C Außentemperatur –, behoben durch Neuprogrammieren des Motorsteuergeräts. Fords Diesel von 2023 führen den Kaltstartvergleich Kühlmittel gegen Öl (Grenze 35 °C nach 6 h) stattdessen unter P0196. GM nutzt den Code nicht, und der Code sagt nicht, welcher Sensor oder welches System schuld ist.

symptoms: Check engine light and/or wrench lamp (Ford)
Raised oil temperature with a clogged oil cooler
Often no driving symptoms when software is the cause

description: The oxygen sensor before the catalytic converter on bank 1 (sensor 1) is the main control sensor for the mixture. It is either a switching sensor (about 0.1 V lean to 0.9 V rich) or a wide-band sensor that works with a pump current evaluated by an interface chip. P0130 is the general circuit code, and manufacturers fill it very differently. Ford used it up to 2010 as the collective code for all wiring faults reported by the wide-band interface chip and has split it into specific codes since 2011. Subaru sets it when the interface voltages leave their range for 5 s, with immediate MIL. GM calls it 'closed loop performance': cross-talk from the heater (signal rises above 2 V with the heater off) or disagreement with the downstream sensor, two trips. A stored code usually switches mixture control to open loop and suspends adaptation and converter monitoring.
possible_causes: Wiring or connector of the bank 1 upstream sensor damaged, corroded or wet [HIGH]
Oxygen sensor faulty internally [HIGH]
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor or mixture fault (plausibility versions) [MEDIUM]
Wrong or aftermarket sensor type [LOW]
Control module or sensor interface chip faulty [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 60€ - 350€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_description.de: Die Lambdasonde vor dem Katalysator auf Bank 1 (Sensor 1) ist die Hauptregelsonde für das Gemisch. Sie ist entweder eine Sprungsonde (etwa 0,1 V mager bis 0,9 V fett) oder eine Breitbandsonde, die mit einem Pumpstrom arbeitet, den ein Schnittstellenchip auswertet. P0130 ist der allgemeine Stromkreiscode, und die Hersteller füllen ihn sehr unterschiedlich. Ford nutzte ihn bis 2010 als Sammelcode für alle Leitungsfehler, die der Schnittstellenchip der Breitbandsonde meldet, und hat ihn seit 2011 in Einzelcodes aufgeteilt. Subaru setzt ihn, wenn die Schnittstellenspannungen 5 s lang aus dem Bereich laufen, mit sofortiger Motorkontrollleuchte. GM nennt ihn „Leistung im Regelbetrieb“: Übersprechen der Heizung (Signal steigt bei abgeschalteter Heizung über 2 V) oder Widerspruch zur Nachkatsonde, zwei Fahrzyklen. description: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 (sensor 1) has an electric heater so that it reaches its working temperature of about 300 °C soon after a cold start. The control module switches the heater on the ground side and checks driver voltage and heater current: GM fails it outside 0.3–2.5 A (or 3.1 A) and calls it 'heater performance', Ford outside roughly 0.22–0.465 A minimum to 3 A, Saab Trionic outside 0.5–2.3 A for 5 s. Ford sets it as 'no activity' in a functional check: if the sensor never swings beyond about 0.42/0.48 V despite rich and lean phases – if needed after forced enrichment and leaning – once per drive cycle. description: The downstream oxygen sensor (sensor 2, after the catalytic converter) is used for fine mixture trim and to monitor the converter. 'Delayed response' means the sensor starts reacting too late, or does not reach the target level at all, after the mixture has changed. This code covers the rich-to-lean direction, usually tested during deceleration fuel cut-off. Bulletins often point elsewhere: Audi fixed P013E with software and said not to replace the sensor, VW names exhaust leaks or the converter. CARB requires separate detection of slow and delayed faults in each direction (phased in from 2009 for downstream and 2011 for upstream sensors).

description: The oxygen sensor after the catalytic converter on bank 1 (sensor 2) is a switching sensor (about 0.1–0.9 V) used for converter monitoring and fine mixture trim. P0140 means the sensor produces no voltage of its own and the control module only sees its own reference (bias) voltage. GM's V6 sets it when the signal sits at 401–548 mV or the sensor's internal resistance exceeds 40 kΩ when it should be hot; newer GM systems apply 1900 mV and read above 1700 mV as an open circuit. Two trips. Ford reports 'no activity' under P0136 instead. A cold sensor with a failed heater can also cause it. When it fails, the control module stops the downstream trim and cannot evaluate the converter; there is no limp mode.
possible_causes: Signal or ground wire open, connector off or corroded [HIGH]
Sensor heater failed, sensor never becomes active [MEDIUM]
Sensor worn out (no longer produces voltage) [MEDIUM]
Control module input faulty [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 250€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: The downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 (sensor 2) has an electric heater so it reaches its working temperature quickly. The control module switches the heater on the ground side and checks both the driver voltage against the commanded state and the heater current. GM fails it outside 0.3–2.5 A (two trips; pure circuit faults are P0036–P0038 there); Ford uses P0141 as its general heater circuit code with a current window of roughly 0.22–0.465 A minimum to 3 A maximum depending on sensor supplier. Without heat the sensor signal is useless, so converter monitoring and trim are suspended.

Heater supply (fuse, relay) or control wire open [MEDIUM]
Short in the heater (current too high) [MEDIUM]
Connector corroded, contact resistance [LOW]

description: Sensor 3 is a third oxygen sensor on bank 1, behind a second converter or converter brick. It only exists on some vehicles – documented for Jaguar Land Rover's 3.0 V6 supercharged (2013–2016, where sensor 2 is 'mid-cat' and sensor 3 'post-cat') and Ford systems that monitor part of the converter volume. P0142 is the general circuit code of this sensor. Jaguar Land Rover lists it with P0143, P0144 and P0147 for the post-cat sensor and names software (fixed by reconfiguring the engine module) and water-induced thermal shock as causes. No published thresholds exist for sensor 3; the logic follows the sensor 2 checks (P0136). When it fails, the control module stops the downstream trim and cannot evaluate the converter; there is no limp mode.

description: P0148 is an early, rather unspecific OBD II code: the control module finds that the fuel delivered does not match what was requested. Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel (Isuzu) uses it for leak detection: from the balance of quantity and rail pressure it recognises a leak of 90 mm³ per crankshaft revolution, monitored continuously up to 6,400 rpm, and then shuts the engine off – a restart is only possible in the next drive cycle. Ford lists P0148 in the fuel monitor of its 2020–2023 petrol engines, alongside P0171/P0172, without describing the logic. Newer systems usually report such faults more precisely as P0087/P0088 (rail pressure) or P0093 (large leak).

Fuel filter clogged or lift pump weak [MEDIUM]

Air in the fuel system (tank run dry) [LOW]

description: P0149 is a diesel code for a deviation of the actual from the target start of injection. On distributor pumps such as the Bosch VP44, a timing device sets the delivery start, and the pump control unit compares the actual position with the target. On the 2003 Saab 9-3 2.2 TiD (GM/Opel engine) P0149 means injection too early – too late is the manufacturer code P1149; it is monitored continuously above 600 rpm and leads to limp mode with limited fuel quantity. CARB has required injection timing monitoring for all diesels since model year 2010. On common-rail systems timing is mostly covered by injector-related codes, so P0149 is rare there.

Crankshaft or camshaft signal disturbed [LOW]

description: The downstream oxygen sensor (sensor 2, after the catalytic converter) is used for fine mixture trim and to monitor the converter. 'Delayed response' means the sensor starts reacting too late, or does not reach the target level at all, after the mixture has changed. This code covers the rich-to-lean direction, usually tested during deceleration fuel cut-off. Bank 2 only exists on V and boxer engines. GM checks whether the signal falls below 450 mV before about 45 g of air have passed after the forced change; failing needs two trips. Ford uses the same stuck-in-range test for bank 2, failing after three bad results in a row. CARB requires separate detection of slow and delayed faults in each direction (phased in from 2009 for downstream and 2011 for upstream sensors).
possible_causes: Downstream oxygen sensor aged or contaminated (soot, oil, silicone, coolant) [HIGH]
Exhaust leak between manifold/turbo and the sensor [MEDIUM]
Converter faulty or non-original with different oxygen storage [MEDIUM]
Control module software too sensitive (update available) [LOW]
Sensor connector or wiring with contact resistance [LOW]

description: The upstream oxygen sensor (sensor 1, before the catalytic converter) is the main control sensor for the air-fuel mixture. CARB requires separate detection of slow and delayed faults in each direction (phased in from 2009 for downstream and 2011 for upstream sensors).

bilingual_description.en: The upstream oxygen sensor (sensor 1, before the catalytic converter) is the main control sensor for the air-fuel mixture. 'Slow response' means the signal transition itself is too sluggish – it takes too long to pass between two voltage levels. This code covers the rich-to-lean direction, usually tested during deceleration fuel cut-off. Manufacturer documentation was found only for diesels: GM evaluates the oxygen signal of the NOx sensor when the engine goes from load to overrun and fails it above about 1.1 s (two trips); Ram lists it as soot-related. GM petrol engines use P015A/P015B instead, and Ford reported upstream response faults as P0133 in 2012. CARB requires separate detection of slow and delayed faults in each direction (phased in from 2009 for downstream and 2011 for upstream sensors).
bilingual_description.de: Die Lambdasonde vor dem Katalysator (Sensor 1) ist die Hauptregelsonde für das Gemisch. „Langsame Reaktion“ heißt: Der Signalwechsel selbst ist zu träge – das Signal braucht zu lange zwischen zwei Spannungsschwellen. Dieser Code betrifft die Richtung fett nach mager, meist geprüft während der Schubabschaltung. Herstellerunterlagen fanden sich nur für Diesel: GM wertet das Sauerstoffsignal der NOx-Sonde beim Übergang von Last in den Schub aus und setzt den Fehler ab etwa 1,1 s (zwei Fahrzyklen); Ram führt ihn als rußbedingt. GM-Benziner nutzen stattdessen P015A/P015B, und Ford meldete Ansprechfehler der Sonde vor Kat 2012 als P0133. CARB verlangt, langsame und verzögerte Fehler je Richtung getrennt zu erkennen (eingeführt ab 2009 für Sonden nach und ab 2011 für Sonden vor dem Katalysator).

description: The oxygen sensor before the catalytic converter on bank 2 (sensor 1) is the main control sensor for the mixture. It is either a switching sensor (about 0.1 V lean to 0.9 V rich) or a wide-band sensor that works with a pump current evaluated by an interface chip. Bank 2 exists only on engines with two exhaust manifolds. P0150 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0130. Ford used it up to 2010 as the collective code for wiring faults of the bank 2 wide-band sensor reported by the interface chip and has used specific codes since 2011 (P0151, P0152, P2240/P2247/P2254). Other makers fill it as for bank 1 – an interface voltage check, a collective code or a plausibility test. No bank 2-specific manufacturer thresholds were found. If P0130 and P0150 appear together, look for a shared cause such as supply, ground or the control module. A stored code usually switches mixture control to open loop and suspends adaptation and converter monitoring.
possible_causes: Wiring or connector of the bank 2 upstream sensor damaged, corroded or wet [HIGH]
Oxygen sensor faulty internally [HIGH]
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor or mixture fault (plausibility versions) [MEDIUM]
Control module or sensor interface chip faulty [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 60€ - 350€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

Sie ist entweder eine Sprungsonde (etwa 0,1 V mager bis 0,9 V fett) oder eine Breitbandsonde, die mit einem Pumpstrom arbeitet, den ein Schnittstellenchip auswertet. Treten P0130 und P0150 zusammen auf, auf eine gemeinsame Ursache wie Versorgung, Masse oder Steuergerät achten. Ein gespeicherter Code schaltet die Lambdaregelung meist ab, Adaption und Katalysatorprüfung ruhen.

description: The oxygen sensor before the catalytic converter on bank 2 (sensor 1) is the main control sensor for the mixture. It is either a switching sensor (about 0.1 V lean to 0.9 V rich) or a wide-band sensor that works with a pump current evaluated by an interface chip. Bank 2 exists only on engines with two exhaust manifolds. P0151 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0131. On switching sensors the signal stays below about 40–50 mV in closed loop with a stoichiometric target (GM LT4: 285 of 350 samples; GM 3.0/3.6 V6 within 50 s); on wide-band sensors the interface chip reports a sensor wire shorted to ground. Two trips. A genuinely lean bank 2 shows up as P0174 rather than this code. A stored code usually switches mixture control to open loop and suspends adaptation and converter monitoring.

Sensor faulty or poisoned (permanently lean signal) [HIGH]
Large exhaust leak ahead of the sensor or misfires [MEDIUM]
Connector wet or corroded [MEDIUM]

description: The oxygen sensor before the catalytic converter on bank 2 (sensor 1) is the main control sensor for the mixture. It is either a switching sensor (about 0.1 V lean to 0.9 V rich) or a wide-band sensor that works with a pump current evaluated by an interface chip. description: The oxygen sensor before the catalytic converter on bank 2 (sensor 1) is the main control sensor for the mixture. It is either a switching sensor (about 0.1 V lean to 0.9 V rich) or a wide-band sensor that works with a pump current evaluated by an interface chip. Bank 2 exists only on engines with two exhaust manifolds. P0153 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0133: the sensor reacts too slowly to mixture changes. description: The oxygen sensor before the catalytic converter on bank 2 (sensor 1) is the main control sensor for the mixture. It is either a switching sensor (about 0.1 V lean to 0.9 V rich) or a wide-band sensor that works with a pump current evaluated by an interface chip. Bank 2 exists only on engines with two exhaust manifolds. P0154 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0134: the sensor delivers no moving signal and the control module only sees its own bias voltage. On GM's 3.0/3.6 V6 the code is set when the signal stays at 350–550 mV after heater warm-up, within about 15 s, in closed loop after 150 s of running; two trips. A stored code usually switches mixture control to open loop and suspends adaptation and converter monitoring.

description: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 2 (sensor 1) has its own electric heater. P0155 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0135: the heater current is outside its window or the driver voltage does not follow the command. GM fails it outside 0.3–3.1 A (8 s or 8 of 10 samples, two trips); Ford outside roughly 0.22–0.465 A minimum to 3 A, with related codes for heater temperature control (P0050) and resistance (P0059). Closed loop on bank 2 then starts late after a cold start, and the sensor checks are suspended. P0135 together with P0155 points to a shared supply or fuse.
possible_causes: Heater element of the sensor burnt out (sensor must be replaced) [HIGH]
Fuse or relay of the heater supply faulty [MEDIUM]
Heater wiring or connector open, corroded or shorted [MEDIUM]
Heater driver in the control module faulty [LOW]

description: The upstream oxygen sensor (sensor 1, before the catalytic converter) is the main control sensor for the air-fuel mixture. 'Delayed response' means the sensor starts reacting too late, or does not reach the target level at all, after the mixture has changed. This code covers the rich-to-lean direction, usually tested during deceleration fuel cut-off. GM uses this on switching (narrow-band) sensors: while the fuel cut-off for the downstream tests is running, it measures how long the upstream sensor takes to start dropping from above 680 mV and fails a filtered delay above about 0.58 s after one trip. Conditions include warm engine, 40–78 mph and a hot converter. CARB requires separate detection of slow and delayed faults in each direction (phased in from 2009 for downstream and 2011 for upstream sensors).
possible_causes: Upstream oxygen sensor aged or poisoned (silicone, oil, coolant, soot) [HIGH]
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor (manifold, flange) [MEDIUM]
Mixture fault: intake air leak, injectors, fuel pressure, air flow sensor [LOW]
Sensor heater weak, sensor too cold [LOW]
Connector, wiring or control module software [LOW]

description: Diesel fuel systems correct injection timing and quantity in closed loop, often with learning routines that run during suitable overrun phases. CARB requires a fault when such feedback control does not start within a manufacturer-defined time. P015E is the code of this kind for injection timing control: the closed-loop correction does not become active in time, or does not learn. It belongs to a family of similar codes – Ford's 2023 diesels, for example, set the sister code P016D when rail pressure adaptation has learned nothing after 300 s. No manufacturer document describing P015E itself, or its threshold, was found; the description rests on CARB and the sister code. Frequent causes are learning conditions that occur too rarely, software, or injectors outside tolerance.
possible_causes: Learning conditions (overrun phases, temperatures) met too rarely [HIGH]
Control module software [MEDIUM]
Injectors outside tolerance or unstable fuel pressure [MEDIUM]
Injector wiring or sensors faulty [LOW]
Engine control module faulty [LOW]

description: Cylinder balance control evens out the contribution of individual cylinders – on diesels by adjusting each injector's quantity based on crankshaft speed fluctuations. P015F, by its title, is set when this closed-loop control does not become active within the expected time after starting, for example because the crankshaft wheel has not been learned or the conditions are missing. No manufacturer using P015F was found: Ford's 2023 diesels run cylinder balancing (maximum correction 3.5–15 mg per stroke) but report problems as P0263–P0284. The description therefore rests on CARB's requirement for feedback controls and that comparable function; causes are derived, not documented.

Control module software [LOW]

bilingual_description.en: Cylinder balance control evens out the contribution of individual cylinders – on diesels by adjusting each injector's quantity based on crankshaft speed fluctuations. P015F, by its title, is set when this closed-loop control does not become active within the expected time after starting, for example because the crankshaft wheel has not been learned or the conditions are missing. No manufacturer using P015F was found: Ford's 2023 diesels run cylinder balancing (maximum correction 3.5–15 mg per stroke) but report problems as P0263–P0284. The description therefore rests on CARB's requirement for feedback controls and that comparable function; causes are derived, not documented.
bilingual_description.de: Die Zylindergleichstellung gleicht den Beitrag der einzelnen Zylinder aus – beim Diesel, indem sie die Menge jedes Injektors anhand der Drehzahlschwankungen der Kurbelwelle anpasst. P015F wird laut Titel gesetzt, wenn diese Regelung nach dem Start nicht in der erwarteten Zeit aktiv wird, etwa weil das Kurbelwellen-Geberrad nicht gelernt ist oder die Bedingungen fehlen. Ein Hersteller, der P015F nutzt, wurde nicht gefunden: Fords Diesel von 2023 betreiben eine Zylindergleichstellung (maximale Korrektur 3,5–15 mg je Hub), melden Probleme aber als P0263–P0284. Die Beschreibung stützt sich deshalb auf die CARB-Vorgabe zu Regelkreisen und diese vergleichbare Funktion; die Ursachen sind abgeleitet, nicht belegt.

description: The oxygen sensor after the catalytic converter on bank 2 (sensor 2) is a switching sensor used for converter monitoring and downstream mixture trim; it exists only on V and boxer engines with a separate downstream sensor per bank. P0160 means the sensor shows no change in voltage although it is heated and the engine is in closed loop; the control module only sees its own bias voltage, so the circuit is open or high-resistance or the sensor is dead. On GM's 3.0/3.6 V6 the code sets within 15 s after more than 150 s of running; newer GM systems apply 1900 mV and treat above 1700 mV as open; two trips. Ford does not use P0160 and reports 'no activity' as P0156. A failed heater (P0161) can also cause it. The previous obdex title mixed in 'Slow Response', which is P0159. When it fails, the downstream evaluation of that converter is suspended; there is no limp mode.
possible_causes: Signal or ground wire open or high-resistance, connector corroded [HIGH]
Sensor dead, poisoned or damaged by thermal shock [HIGH]
Heater failed or fuse blown by a heater short [MEDIUM]
Signal wire shorted to voltage [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 60€ - 250€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_description.de: Die Lambdasonde nach dem Katalysator auf Bank 2 (Sensor 2) ist eine Sprungsonde für Katalysatorüberwachung und Nachregelung; es gibt sie nur bei V- und Boxermotoren mit eigener Nachkatsonde je Bank. P0160 heißt, die Sonde zeigt keine Spannungsänderung, obwohl sie beheizt ist und der Motor in der Lambdaregelung läuft; das Steuergerät sieht nur seine eigene Vorspannung, der Kreis ist also offen oder hochohmig oder die Sonde tot. Fällt sie aus, entfällt die Bewertung dieses Katalysators; einen Notlauf gibt es nicht.

description: The downstream oxygen sensor on bank 2 (sensor 2) has an electric heater so that it reaches working temperature quickly. P0161 concerns this heater circuit and its performance. GM measures the current through its low-side driver and fails it outside 0.3–2.9 A on the supercharged V8 (8 of 10 samples, two trips). Ford checks the driver voltage continuously and the current once per drive cycle once the sensor is estimated above about 120 °C; the lower limit is 0.22–0.55 A depending on sensor type, the upper 3 A. Without heat the sensor becomes active late or not at all, so P0159/P0160 can follow; there is no limp mode.
possible_causes: Heater element of the sensor burnt out [HIGH]
Heater wiring, connector or fuse open or corroded [MEDIUM]
Short in the heater circuit (current too high) [LOW]
Driver in the engine module faulty [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 60€ - 250€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: Sensor 3 on bank 2 is a switching oxygen sensor behind a second converter or converter brick. It is rare – documented for Jaguar Land Rover's supercharged V6 and V8 (2013–2016), where it is the 'post-cat' sensor of the second bank, and for Ford systems that monitor part of the converter volume. P0162 is the general circuit code of this sensor, the counterpart of P0142. Jaguar Land Rover assigns the code to that sensor and names software (fixed by reconfiguring the engine module) and water-induced thermal shock as causes; no thresholds are published for sensor 3, so the logic follows the sensor 2 checks. The previous obdex titles from P0162 to P0165 were shifted by one position; P0162 had carried the heater title of P0161. When it fails, the downstream evaluation of that converter is suspended; there is no limp mode.
possible_causes: Sensor faulty or damaged by thermal shock [HIGH]
Wiring or connector under the car damaged [MEDIUM]
Engine module software (Jaguar Land Rover) [MEDIUM]
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 60€ - 300€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: P0168 is not a sensor fault but an operating condition, almost only on diesels: the fuel temperature sensor reports fuel hotter than a protective limit. The fuel heats up through the return flow from the high-pressure pump and injectors, especially with little fuel in the tank, at idle after full load, in hot weather or with a failed fuel cooler; one manufacturer patent names about 80 °C as the upper limit to protect seals, against a normal range of roughly 5–60 °C. On Saab's Bosch EDC16 diesels the code means an engine protection function is active and injection quantity is reduced. No manufacturer threshold was found, and GM's and Ford's diesel summaries do not use P0168. Whether the warning light comes on depends on the manufacturer.
possible_causes: Fuel cooler (air or water cooler in the return) dirty or faulty, coolant circuit disturbed [HIGH]
Very little fuel in the tank at high load or heat [MEDIUM]
Excessive return flow from worn high-pressure pump or injectors, or faulty overflow valve [MEDIUM]
Fuel temperature sensor drifting and reading too high [MEDIUM]
Engine overheating or overload (trailer, gradient) [LOW]

On Saab's Bosch EDC16 diesels the code means an engine protection function is active and injection quantity is reduced. No manufacturer threshold was found, and GM's and Ford's diesel summaries do not use P0168. Whether the warning light comes on depends on the manufacturer.
bilingual_description.de: P0168 ist kein Sensorfehler, sondern ein Betriebszustand, fast nur bei Dieseln: Der Kraftstofftemperatursensor meldet Kraftstoff, der heißer ist als eine Schutzgrenze. Der Kraftstoff erwärmt sich durch den Rücklauf aus Hochdruckpumpe und Injektoren, besonders bei wenig Tankinhalt, im Leerlauf nach Volllast, bei Hitze oder mit ausgefallenem Kraftstoffkühler; ein Herstellerpatent nennt etwa 80 °C als Obergrenze zum Schutz der Dichtungen, bei einem Normalbereich von rund 5–60 °C. Bei Saabs Bosch-EDC16-Dieseln heißt der Code, dass eine Motorschutzfunktion aktiv ist und die Einspritzmenge reduziert wird. Eine Herstellerschwelle wurde nicht gefunden, und die Diesel-Übersichten von GM und Ford nutzen P0168 nicht. Ob die Warnleuchte angeht, hängt vom Hersteller ab.

symptoms: Loss of power, limp mode (reduced injection quantity)
Occurs in heat, at full load, with little fuel in the tank

description: According to its title, P0169 means the control module has detected a fuel composition outside what is expected – wrong fuel or an impermissible ethanol or water content – while the composition sensor itself works. None of the manufacturer OBD documents checked (GM, Ford) uses the code: GM reports water or conductive fuel via the ethanol sensor frequency as P2269, and Ford has had no composition sensor since 2000. Claims that diesel makers use it for misfuelling or water could not be verified. The description therefore rests on CARB, which lists the fuel composition sensor as a monitored component, and on component information. Unrecognised fuel usually also shows up as mixture adaptation codes.
possible_causes: Wrong fuel (E85 in a non-flex-fuel vehicle, ethanol content outside calibration) [HIGH]
Water or contamination in the fuel [MEDIUM]
Fuel composition sensor drifting (value in range but wrong) [MEDIUM]
Control module software [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 500€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

symptoms: Poor cold start, stumbling, loss of power

description: With closed-loop control the engine module corrects the injected fuel using the oxygen sensor: short-term fuel trim reacts within fractions of a second, long-term trim stores a learned base correction per load and speed range. Positive values mean fuel is being added because the mixture was lean, negative values mean fuel is being removed; around ±10 % is normal. Closed loop needs a heated, working oxygen sensor and plausible engine data. P016A means the mixture control did not switch to closed loop within the calibrated time after starting; the engine then runs on map values with higher emissions but no actual limp mode. CARB requires this check, and since 2019 also after every automatic restart in start-stop systems. Bentley and other VW group petrol engines set it together with oxygen sensor heater codes when the heater fuse holder was damaged; Ram's 3.0 EcoDiesel listed it in bulletins fixed with new software and sensors. Time limits are not public.
possible_causes: Oxygen sensor heater not working (fuse, fuse holder, wiring, heater element) [HIGH]
Oxygen sensor sluggish or aged [MEDIUM]
Control module software (false setting) [MEDIUM]
Engine not warming up (thermostat open, coolant sensor) [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 10€ - 400€ (0.3h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

Für den Regelbetrieb braucht es eine beheizte, funktionierende Lambdasonde und plausible Motordaten. P016A heißt, die Gemischregelung ist nach dem Start nicht in der kalibrierten Zeit in den Regelbetrieb gewechselt; der Motor läuft dann mit Kennfeldwerten und höheren Emissionen, aber ohne eigentlichen Notlauf. CARB verlangt diese Prüfung, seit 2019 auch nach jedem automatischen Neustart bei Start-Stopp. Bentley und andere Benziner des VW-Konzerns setzen ihn zusammen mit Codes der Sondenheizung, wenn der Sicherungshalter der Heizung beschädigt war; beim Ram 3.0 EcoDiesel stand er in Bulletins, die mit neuer Software und Sensoren behoben wurden. Zeitgrenzen sind nicht öffentlich.

symptoms: Often with oxygen sensor or heater codes

description: With closed-loop control the engine module corrects the injected fuel using the oxygen sensor: short-term fuel trim reacts within fractions of a second, long-term trim stores a learned base correction per load and speed range. Positive values mean fuel is being added because the mixture was lean, negative values mean fuel is being removed; around ±10 % is normal. P016B means the mixture control as a whole has reached its lower limit: it already removes as much fuel as allowed and the mixture is still rich. In substance it matches P0172, but without a bank reference – for manufacturers whose strategy evaluates the control loop as a whole. CARB requires a fault once the adaptation has used up its range. No manufacturer document using exactly this code was found; Hyundai documents the lean counterpart P016C. Typical causes are those of a rich mixture: excessive fuel pressure, leaking injectors or an open purge valve.
possible_causes: Fuel pressure too high / high-pressure pump or regulator fault (direct injection) [MEDIUM]
Leaking injectors [MEDIUM]
Purge valve open [MEDIUM]
Oxygen sensor or air flow/pressure sensor offset, control module software [LOW]

symptoms: Check engine light on (after two drive cycles)

description: With closed-loop control the engine module corrects the injected fuel using the oxygen sensor: short-term fuel trim reacts within fractions of a second, long-term trim stores a learned base correction per load and speed range. Positive values mean fuel is being added because the mixture was lean, negative values mean fuel is being removed; around ±10 % is normal. Fuel pressure or delivery too low [MEDIUM]
Wrongly learned adaptation / control module software [MEDIUM]
Air flow or pressure sensor reading low, injectors clogged [LOW]

symptoms: Check engine light on (after two drive cycles)
Stalling when stopping or at idle

description: Common-rail diesels regulate rail pressure in closed loop: the control module compares the rail pressure sensor with the target and adjusts a volume or pressure control valve, learning correction factors as it goes. CARB requires faults to be flagged when this feedback control does not start in time or runs out of authority. P016D means the pressure control has not settled into closed loop, or has not learned, in the time allowed. Ford's 2023 diesels (6.7 and 3.0 litre) set it when, within the learning conditions – target rail pressure 600–1300 bar, fuel at most 40 °C – no new adaptation factor has been learned after 300 s; the check only runs while the rail pressure sensor and its supply are fault-free. Ford reports adaptation at its limit separately as P228E/P228F. Use on petrol engines was not found. Often there are no noticeable symptoms.
possible_causes: Rail pressure sensor drifting (wrong slope) [HIGH]
Volume or pressure control valve sticking or worn [MEDIUM]
Unstable low-pressure supply (filter, lift pump, air in system) [MEDIUM]
Fuel leak or high injector return flow [LOW]
Control module software [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 100€ - 1500€ (1h - 5h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_description.de: Common-Rail-Diesel regeln den Raildruck geschlossen: Das Steuergerät vergleicht den Raildrucksensor mit dem Sollwert, verstellt ein Mengen- oder Druckregelventil und lernt dabei Korrekturfaktoren. CARB verlangt einen Fehler, wenn diese Regelung nicht rechtzeitig beginnt oder ihren Stellbereich ausschöpft. P016D heißt, die Druckregelung ist nicht in der erlaubten Zeit in den Regelbetrieb gekommen oder hat nicht gelernt. Fords Diesel von 2023 (6,7 und 3,0 Liter) setzen ihn, wenn unter den Lernbedingungen – Soll-Raildruck 600–1300 bar, Kraftstoff höchstens 40 °C – nach 300 s kein neuer Adaptionsfaktor gelernt wurde; die Prüfung läuft nur, solange Raildrucksensor und dessen Versorgung fehlerfrei sind. Eine Adaption am Anschlag meldet Ford getrennt als P228E/P228F. Eine Nutzung bei Benzinern wurde nicht gefunden. Oft gibt es keine spürbaren Symptome.

symptoms: Occasional power reduction or rough idle

description: Common-rail diesels regulate rail pressure in closed loop: the control module compares the rail pressure sensor with the target and adjusts a volume or pressure control valve, learning correction factors as it goes. CARB requires faults to be flagged when this feedback control does not start in time or runs out of authority. P016E means the controller is already at its limit in the 'reduce pressure' direction and the measured pressure is still above target. That can be real overpressure – a control valve that lets too much through or a blocked return – or a falsely high reading. Volvo and Mack document P016E on their 11 and 13 litre truck diesels together with P0194, caused by corroded contacts at the rail pressure sensor; the fix is a new sensor and internal harness. No public thresholds exist; Ford reports the comparable condition as P228F. Use on passenger-car diesels or petrol engines was not documented.
possible_causes: Rail pressure sensor or its contacts/wiring (corrosion) giving a falsely high signal [HIGH]
Pressure or volume control valve sticking (lets too much through) [MEDIUM]
Return line from control valve or rail blocked or kinked [MEDIUM]
Control module software or calibration [LOW]

description: Common-rail diesels regulate rail pressure in closed loop: the control module compares the rail pressure sensor with the target and adjusts a volume or pressure control valve, learning correction factors as it goes. CARB requires faults to be flagged when this feedback control does not start in time or runs out of authority. Which circuit is meant depends on the manufacturer: Volvo and Mack use it for rail pressure, for example as a follow-up when their electronic pressure relief valve stays open (P009B); on FCA's 3.0 EcoDiesel it concerns the regulated low-pressure supply via the fuel pump control module and appears with P025C and P01C6, partly fixed by new engine software. Connector or ground problems (corrosion, water) at pump module, low-pressure sensor or ground point [HIGH]
Pressure relief valve open or its control circuit interrupted [MEDIUM]
Worn high-pressure pump or internal leak [MEDIUM]
Engine control module software [LOW]

symptoms: Check engine light on (after two drive cycles)

description: With closed-loop control the engine module corrects the injected fuel using the oxygen sensor: short-term fuel trim reacts within fractions of a second, long-term trim stores a learned base correction per load and speed range. Positive values mean fuel is being added because the mixture was lean, negative values mean fuel is being removed; around ±10 % is normal. P0171 means long-term trim on bank 1 is at its upper limit: the module already adds the maximum fuel and the mixture still stays lean. GM sets it at a long-term factor of about 1.30–1.36 (+30–36 %, engine-specific), Ford above +25 % with short-term trim above +1 %; it needs two trips and is suspended during heavy purge flow or intrusive tests. GM bulletins repeatedly trace it to leaking crankcase ventilation hoses or pipes on V6 and V8 engines; Ford found leaking direct injectors. P0171 together with P0174 points to a shared cause. Diagnosis hint: trims very high only at idle and normal under load point to an air leak; trims rising with load point to fuel shortage or an air flow sensor reading low. The oxygen sensor only reports what is in the exhaust and is rarely the cause.

specific_definitions.AUDI: Control module software needs to be updated, Vacuum leaks (intake manifold gaskets, vacuum hoses, PCV hoses, etc.), Mass air flow sensor, Plugged fuel filter or weak fuel pump, Plugged or dirty fuel injectors
specific_definitions.BUICK: System Lean Bank 1

bilingual_title.en: System Too Lean Bank 1

bilingual_description.en: With closed-loop control the engine module corrects the injected fuel using the oxygen sensor: short-term fuel trim reacts within fractions of a second, long-term trim stores a learned base correction per load and speed range. Positive values mean fuel is being added because the mixture was lean, negative values mean fuel is being removed; around ±10 % is normal. P0171 means long-term trim on bank 1 is at its upper limit: the module already adds the maximum fuel and the mixture still stays lean. GM sets it at a long-term factor of about 1.30–1.36 (+30–36 %, engine-specific), Ford above +25 % with short-term trim above +1 %; it needs two trips and is suspended during heavy purge flow or intrusive tests. GM bulletins repeatedly trace it to leaking crankcase ventilation hoses or pipes on V6 and V8 engines; Ford found leaking direct injectors. P0171 together with P0174 points to a shared cause. Diagnosis hint: trims very high only at idle and normal under load point to an air leak; trims rising with load point to fuel shortage or an air flow sensor reading low. The oxygen sensor only reports what is in the exhaust and is rarely the cause.
bilingual_description.de: Im geschlossenen Regelkreis korrigiert das Motorsteuergerät die Einspritzmenge anhand der Lambdasonde: Die Kurzzeitkorrektur reagiert in Sekundenbruchteilen, die Langzeitkorrektur speichert je Last- und Drehzahlbereich eine gelernte Grundkorrektur. Positive Werte heißen, es wird Kraftstoff zugegeben, weil das Gemisch mager war, negative, es wird Kraftstoff weggenommen; rund ±10 % sind normal. P0171 heißt, die Langzeitkorrektur auf Bank 1 steht am oberen Anschlag: Das Steuergerät gibt bereits maximal Kraftstoff zu, und das Gemisch bleibt trotzdem mager. GM setzt ihn ab einem Langzeitfaktor von etwa 1,30–1,36 (+30–36 %, motorabhängig), Ford über +25 % bei Kurzzeitkorrektur über +1 %; er braucht zwei Fahrzyklen und ruht bei starkem Tankentlüftungsfluss oder Eingriffstests. GM-Bulletins führen ihn bei V6- und V8-Motoren immer wieder auf undichte Schläuche oder Rohre der Kurbelgehäuseentlüftung zurück; Ford fand undichte Direkteinspritzventile. P0171 zusammen mit P0174 deutet auf eine gemeinsame Ursache. Die Lambdasonde meldet nur, was im Abgas ist, und ist selten die Ursache.
