Engine software (false setting) [MEDIUM]
Poor combustion (misfire, fuel or air shortage, low compression) [MEDIUM]
Increased internal friction (wrong oil, seizing parts) [LOW]

description: By its J2012 name P0337 means the crankshaft position signal stays at a low level without changing state – signal wire shorted to ground, missing supply on a Hall sensor or a sensor stuck low. Few manufacturers use the code. GM 2014–2019 and Ford report all crank sensor faults under P0335/P0336 or P0320/P0339. GM's Global A engines (Saab 9-5 1.6 LLU, 2011) define P0337 as a low duty cycle: fewer than 200 reference pulses in 10 consecutive revolutions, caused among other things by an open or high resistance in the signal or ground wire, set after two trips. Older Bosch diesels (Saab 9-5 EDC16) use it differently for crank pulses missing while cam pulses are present, and shut the engine down. The consequence is as for P0335: stalling or no start.

description: By its J2012 name P0338 means the crankshaft position signal stays at a high level – signal wire shorted to supply, or an open signal output that the module's pull-up holds high on a Hall sensor. GM 2014–2019 and Ford do not use the code. GM's Global A engines in the Saab 9-5 (2010/11) and 9-4X define it as a high duty cycle, i.e. too many pulses or teeth between the reference gaps: on the 2.8 turbo V6 (LAU) a deviation of more than 8 teeth, checked once per revolution and set in the first trip; on the 1.6 (LLU) more than 200 reference pulses in 10 revolutions, and on the 2.0 turbo (LDK) a large tooth deviation over 4 revolutions, both after two trips. Behind this are usually interference pulses or a gap that is not recognised. Result: misfire, stalling, limp mode.

description: P0339 means the crankshaft position signal drops out or is disturbed for moments and then recovers. description: To know which stroke each cylinder is in, the engine module matches the crank angle with the camshaft phase. P033F means this synchronisation is lost while running or cannot be established. It is documented by code only at Ford (2020–2023): P033F, as an alternative to Ford's older own code, stands for a disturbed crank signal without crank/cam synchronisation, and then misfire detection is also impossible. Ford's 2012 description shows the reaction: on a crank sensor fault the module cuts fuel and spark and resynchronises – one revolution to find the gap, one more to confirm cylinder 1 via the camshaft sensor. FCA evaluates the same function in its own cam/crank synchronisation monitor under other codes. Besides the sensors, a jumped timing chain or belt can be behind it.

P033F heißt, diese Synchronisation geht im Lauf verloren oder kommt nicht zustande. description: The camshaft position sensor, almost always a Hall sensor, tells the engine module which stroke cylinder 1 is in – one crank revolution alone is ambiguous – and measures the actual cam phase with variable timing. Sensor A is the intake camshaft, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. P0340 means no or too few cam pulses arrive while the crankshaft turns in sync. GM sets it after 5.5 s (or 4 s) of cranking without a cam pulse or fewer than 4 pulses in 3 s running, petrol engines after two trips. Ford checks the ratio of cam to crank events from 200 rpm. The engine usually keeps running but starts longer and loses power as cam timing is held. Bulletins: corroded connectors on GM V8s (PIP5335C), moisture in the oil on short trips in Ford hybrids (SSM 48598).

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

description: P0341 means the intake camshaft sensor of bank 1 (or the only cam sensor) delivers pulses, but their number or pattern does not fit the crankshaft. GM counts the pulses while the crank is in sync: 4 to 6 in the first 12 reference events and 398 to 402 per 100 engine cycles on the 4X wheel of the cam phaser; outside that in 8 of 10 checks the code is set after two trips. Ford's 2023 diesel compares the detected segment profile of the cam wheel with the expected one (1.2 s); the Saab 9-4X V6 checks pulses per crank revolution and correlation with crank position. Ford petrol engines use P0344 instead. Result: cam phase uncertain, cam timing switched off, possibly hard starting. GM names corroded connectors at the timing cover as a sporadic cause (PIP5335C).

Tone wheel on the phaser damaged or wrongly fitted [MEDIUM]

description: P0342 means the signal of the intake camshaft sensor of bank 1 (or the only cam sensor) stays at ground level without edges – signal wire shorted to ground, sensor supply missing or the Hall sensor faulty. description: P0344 means the signal of the intake camshaft sensor of bank 1 (or the only cam sensor) is disturbed for moments: edges are missing or appear at an unexpected angle. description: P0349 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0344: the signal of the intake camshaft sensor on the side without cylinder 1 is disturbed for moments – edges are missing or appear at an unexpected angle. Ford checks this on the five-tooth wheel used with variable cam timing; if edges appear where none are expected, Ford sets P0349 and switches cam timing on bank 2 off, from 200 rpm, detected within 5 s. FCA also uses the code and asks for the cam/crank synchronisation event data to be saved before the sensor is replaced, because a disturbed crank reference can look like a cam fault. GM does not use P0349. Typical causes are a loose contact at the bank 2 connector, a sensor dropping out when hot or soaked with oil moisture, and a damaged tone wheel.

description: Engines with start-stop or hybrid autostart store the crankshaft rest position when the engine stops, so that they can inject and fire correctly at once on restart. This needs a direction-sensing crank sensor, because a cylinder under compression can push the crankshaft backwards after shut-off. On restart the module compares the stored position with the one actually measured after the reference gap. GM sets P034A when they differ by more than 2 teeth in 2 of 3 autostarts or by at least 1 tooth in 4 of 5, after two trips; the diesel already at more than 1 tooth in 1 of 3. The check is suspended while a crank sensor fault is present. Result: start-stop is restricted, restarts take longer with conventional synchronisation, and the autostart may be rough.
possible_causes: Direction-sensing crankshaft position sensor faulty or aged [HIGH]
Interference pulses in the sensor circuit during shut-off [MEDIUM]
Air gap or tone wheel – teeth not detected at low speed [MEDIUM]
Engine module software [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 80€ - 500€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_description.de: Motoren mit Start-Stopp oder Hybrid-Autostart speichern beim Abstellen die Ruhelage der Kurbelwelle, damit sie beim Neustart sofort richtig einspritzen und zünden können. Dazu braucht es einen richtungserkennenden Kurbelwellengeber, denn ein Zylinder in der Verdichtung kann die Kurbelwelle nach dem Abstellen zurückdrücken. Beim Wiederanlauf vergleicht das Steuergerät die gespeicherte mit der nach der Bezugslücke tatsächlich gemessenen Lage. GM setzt P034A, wenn beide um mehr als 2 Zähne in 2 von 3 Autostarts oder um mindestens 1 Zahn in 4 von 5 abweichen, nach zwei Fahrzyklen; der Diesel schon bei mehr als 1 Zahn in 1 von 3. Bei einem Kurbelgeberfehler ruht die Prüfung. Folge: Start-Stopp wird eingeschränkt, der Neustart dauert mit herkömmlicher Synchronisation länger, der Autostart kann ruppig sein.

description: Direction-sensing (bidirectional) crank sensors count the rest position for start-stop even when the crankshaft rocks back after shut-off. In normal running the sensor must never report reverse rotation – if it does, the signal is disturbed. GM sets P034B after at least 3 direction reversals within 10 s at 400 to 2,000 rpm and an airflow of at least 1.5 g/s, after two trips; the diesel uses the same thresholds. GM bulletin 17-NA-317 describes the 3.6 V6 (LFY) in the 2018 Buick Enclave and Chevrolet Traverse: interference in the sensor circuit caused P034B with P0506, low idle or stalling after an autostart, transmission slip above 65 km/h and cruise control dropping out; the remedy was a revised sensor wiring. Result: start-stop disabled, possibly reduced power.
possible_causes: Interference in the sensor circuit (wiring routed next to switching lines) [HIGH]
Direction-sensing crankshaft position sensor faulty [MEDIUM]
Ground or connector fault [MEDIUM]
Tone wheel or air gap [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 80€ - 600€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

symptoms: Low idle or stalling after an autostart

description: With ion current sensing the spark plug serves as a sensor after the spark: a measuring voltage across the gap drives a current through the ions in the flame, from which the module detects combustion, misfire and knock – a Delphi patent describes coils with built-in ion sensing, and Saab's Trionic engines detected misfire this way. P034C means this measuring system works implausibly, so misfire and knock detection are no longer reliable. It is documented on the Alfa Romeo Giulia and Stelvio 2.9 V6 biturbo, where three bulletins fix it mainly with engine software; limp mode is possible. Sooted plugs or a faulty coil with ion circuit are further causes.
possible_causes: Engine software or calibration [HIGH]
Spark plugs sooted, oily or wrong type or gap [MEDIUM]
Ignition coil or cassette with ion circuit faulty [MEDIUM]
Wiring or connector of the ion current return line [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 100€ - 600€ (0.5h - 2h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

symptoms: Limp mode or reduced power possible

description: P0350 is the general ignition coil circuit code without assignment to a coil: the engine module detects a fault in the primary or secondary circuit of a coil but does not report which one. This typically concerns older systems with a shared output stage or ignition module, or a shared feedback line for all coils. The monitoring works as for P0351 ff – primary-current feedback for each ignition command, or the voltage at the driver. GM and Ford report coil faults individually (P0351 ff, P2300 ff) and do not use P0350; the description follows CARB's output monitoring requirement, which allows one collective code.
possible_causes: Ignition coil, coil pack or ignition module faulty [HIGH]
Shared supply (fuse, relay, ignition feed) or ground open [MEDIUM]
Harness, connector or feedback line to the coils faulty [MEDIUM]
Ignition lead or plug connector damaged (secondary side) [LOW]
Engine module or driver [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 400€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

GM and Ford report coil faults individually (P0351 ff, P2300 ff) and do not use P0350; the description follows CARB's output monitoring requirement, which allows one collective code.
bilingual_description.de: P0350 ist der allgemeine Zündspulen-Kreiscode ohne Zuordnung zu einer Spule: Das Motorsteuergerät erkennt einen Fehler im Primär- oder Sekundärkreis einer Spule, meldet aber nicht, welcher. Das betrifft typisch ältere Systeme mit gemeinsamer Endstufe oder gemeinsamem Zündmodul oder einer gemeinsamen Rückmeldeleitung für alle Spulen. Die Überwachung arbeitet wie bei P0351 ff – Primärstrom-Rückmeldung je Zündbefehl oder Spannung am Treiber. GM und Ford melden Spulenfehler einzeln (P0351 ff, P2300 ff) und nutzen P0350 nicht; die Beschreibung folgt der CARB-Vorgabe zur Ausgangsüberwachung, die einen Sammelcode erlaubt.

symptoms: Starting problems or stalling if a shared output stage fails

description: Modern engines have one coil-on-plug ignition coil per cylinder, with the output stage either in the engine module or in the coil itself. P0351 monitors the primary control circuit of coil A – the line from the engine module to the coil or its built-in output stage – for an open circuit or high resistance. GM's module measures the voltage with its low-side driver off and flags an open circuit above 30 kΩ in 50 of 63 samples (2018 engines in the first trip, older ones after two); Ford checks continuously within 1 s, expecting a primary-current feedback for every ignition command, and shuts off injection to that cylinder for 30 s at a time. Short circuits and the secondary side have their own codes (P2300 ff). Coil A usually serves cylinder 1, but the assignment is up to the manufacturer.
possible_causes: Ignition coil A faulty (output stage in the coil or primary winding open) [HIGH]
Connector at the coil corroded, loose or with a spread pin [HIGH]
Control, supply or ground wire open or chafed [MEDIUM]
Fuse or relay of the coil supply (then usually several codes) [LOW]
Driver in the engine module faulty [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 40€ - 250€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_description.de: Moderne Motoren haben je Zylinder eine Stabzündspule, mit der Endstufe entweder im Motorsteuergerät oder in der Spule selbst. P0351 überwacht den Primär-Steuerkreis von Spule A – die Leitung vom Motorsteuergerät zur Spule bzw. zu ihrer eingebauten Endstufe – auf Unterbrechung oder hohen Widerstand. GMs Steuergerät misst bei abgeschaltetem Low-Side-Treiber die Spannung und erkennt eine Unterbrechung über 30 kΩ in 50 von 63 Messungen (Motoren von 2018 im ersten Fahrzyklus, ältere nach zwei); Ford prüft ständig binnen 1 s, erwartet zu jedem Zündbefehl eine Primärstrom-Rückmeldung und schaltet die Einspritzung dieses Zylinders jeweils 30 s ab. Kurzschlüsse und die Sekundärseite haben eigene Codes (P2300 ff). Spule A gehört meist zu Zylinder 1, die Zuordnung legt aber der Hersteller fest.

symptoms: Misfire and rough running on cylinder 1, often also P0301
Loss of power, jerking under load
Cylinder shut off (injection off), risk to the catalyst if driven on

GM's module measures the voltage with its low-side driver off and flags an open circuit above 30 kΩ in 50 of 63 samples (2018 engines in the first trip, older ones after two); Ford checks continuously within 1 s, expecting a primary-current feedback for every ignition command, and shuts off injection to that cylinder for 30 s at a time. Short circuits and the secondary side have their own codes (P2300 ff). Coil D usually serves cylinder 4, but the assignment is up to the manufacturer.
possible_causes: Ignition coil D faulty (output stage in the coil or primary winding open) [HIGH]
Connector at the coil corroded, loose or with a spread pin [HIGH]
Control, supply or ground wire open or chafed [MEDIUM]
Fuse or relay of the coil supply (then usually several codes) [LOW]
Driver in the engine module faulty [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 40€ - 250€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: Ignition E is one of the control signal lines from the engine module to an ignition module, ignition output stage or group of coils; which cylinders it serves is defined by the manufacturer, not by the code standard. The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff). P035A means the control line is open – the module sees a voltage with its driver off that indicates high resistance. No manufacturer using these codes was found – neither GM nor Ford use the Ignition E to H codes; GM reports coil control faults as P0351 ff (open above 30 kΩ) – so the description follows CARB and that analogy. The affected coils fire wrongly or not at all, causing misfire; many modules then shut off injection to those cylinders to protect the catalyst.
possible_causes: Control line or connector pin open (corrosion, pushed-back pin) [HIGH]
Ignition module or coil with integrated driver of this group faulty [MEDIUM]
Supply or ground of the ignition module faulty [MEDIUM]
Driver stage in the engine module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 500€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

Der Code betrifft das Steuersignal, nicht den Primärstrom der Spule (dafür gibt es eigene Codes, P0351 ff und P2300 ff). Die betroffenen Spulen zünden falsch oder gar nicht, was Aussetzer verursacht; viele Steuergeräte schalten dann die Einspritzung dieser Zylinder zum Schutz des Katalysators ab.

bilingual_title.en: Ignition F Control Signal Circuit/Open

bilingual_description.en: Ignition F is one of the control signal lines from the engine module to an ignition module, ignition output stage or group of coils; which cylinders it serves is defined by the manufacturer, not by the code standard. The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff). P035D means the control line is open – the module sees a voltage with its driver off that indicates high resistance. No manufacturer using these codes was found – neither GM nor Ford use the Ignition E to H codes; GM reports coil control faults as P0351 ff (open above 30 kΩ) – so the description follows CARB and that analogy. The affected coils fire wrongly or not at all, causing misfire; many modules then shut off injection to those cylinders to protect the catalyst.

P035D heißt, die Steuerleitung ist unterbrochen – das Steuergerät sieht bei abgeschaltetem Treiber eine Spannung, die auf hohen Widerstand hindeutet. Ein Hersteller, der diese Codes nutzt, wurde nicht gefunden – weder GM noch Ford verwenden die Codes für Zündung E bis H; GM meldet Fehler der Spulenansteuerung als P0351 ff –, die Beschreibung folgt deshalb CARB und dieser Analogie. Die betroffenen Spulen zünden falsch oder gar nicht, was Aussetzer verursacht; viele Steuergeräte schalten dann die Einspritzung dieser Zylinder zum Schutz des Katalysators ab.

description: P0360 monitors the primary control circuit of ignition coil J – the line from the engine module to the coil or to its built-in output stage – for an open circuit or high resistance. Coil J usually serves cylinder 10, so the code only occurs on engines with at least 10 cylinders. GM does not use the code (at most eight cylinders). Ford uses coils I and J on its 6.8-litre V10 in vans, pickups and motorhome chassis. Ford checks continuously from 200 rpm within 1 s, expecting a primary-current feedback for every ignition command, and then shuts off injection to that cylinder for 30 s at a time to protect the catalyst. Ford's PCM code list (Roush workshop manual for the V10) shows the code with check engine light. Short circuits have their own codes (P2327 ff).
possible_causes: Ignition coil J faulty (output stage in the coil or primary winding open) [HIGH]
Connector at the coil corroded, wet or with a loose pin [HIGH]
Control, supply or ground wire open or chafed [MEDIUM]
Driver in the engine module faulty or software (permanent dwell) [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 60€ - 350€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: P0363 is a reaction code: the engine module has detected misfire severe enough to damage the catalyst – through its crankshaft-based misfire monitor – and has therefore shut off injection to the affected cylinder or cylinders. CARB allows exactly this: a vehicle that cuts fuel immediately on catalyst-damaging misfire may turn the check engine light on steadily instead of flashing it, and may switch fuel back on to re-check at most every 30 s. The code names no cylinder; that comes from the accompanying P0301 ff. It is documented by code only at FCA: two reprogramming bulletins for the 2017–2018 Alfa Romeo Giulia 2.0 turbo list P0363 alongside misfire and mixture codes. Ford reacts in the same way without its own code, VW uses a manufacturer code (P130A) for the hidden cylinder, and GM does not list P0363.
possible_causes: Ignition coil or spark plug of the affected cylinder faulty [HIGH]
Injector sticking or leaking, or fuel pressure too low [MEDIUM]
Engine module software (misfire detection, cold-start mixture) [MEDIUM]
Mechanical cause: loss of compression, valve or carbon deposits, vacuum leak [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 800€ (0.5h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

CARB erlaubt genau das: Ein Fahrzeug, das bei katschädigenden Aussetzern sofort den Kraftstoff abschaltet, darf die Motorkontrollleuchte dauerhaft statt blinkend leuchten lassen und höchstens alle 30 s zur Prüfung wieder einspritzen. description: By its J2012 name P0364 means the control circuit to the control module of a DC/AC converter (inverter) behaves implausibly – the command or enable line is present but its signal does not fit what the engine module expects. The code is a late assignment in the P03xx block: older code lists show the slot as reserved, and the other DC/AC converter codes sit in the P2DAx range (P2DA8–P2DAB). Which converter is meant – a traction inverter in a hybrid or a 120/230 V socket inverter – the name does not say, and no manufacturer document available to us uses P0364. The description is therefore limited to the code name and CARB's general requirement to monitor electronic powertrain components. Whether the check engine light comes on and what the vehicle restricts depends on the manufacturer.
possible_causes: Control or enable line to the converter module disturbed (connector, wiring) [MEDIUM]
Converter control module faulty internally [MEDIUM]
Software of the modules involved [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 150€ - 2000€ (1h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor (bank 1 = side with cylinder 1), usually a Hall sensor on the exhaust cam phaser. P0365 means no or too few exhaust cam pulses arrive while the crankshaft turns in sync. GM sets it after 4 s of cranking or 5.5 s without a cam pulse, or fewer than 4 pulses in 3 s running, 8 of 10 samples, after two trips; on GM's 3.6-litre V6 (Saab 9-4X) also with no pulse in 800 of 1,000 engine cycles. Ford checks the ratio of crank to cam events from 200 rpm, detected within 5 s, and collects all electrical faults here. The exhaust phaser then goes to its park position; the engine keeps running but cranks longer and loses some power. FCA advises saving the cam/crank synchronisation data before replacing the sensor, as the fault is often elsewhere.
possible_causes: Exhaust camshaft position sensor faulty [HIGH]
Connector or wiring open or corroded, 5 V reference missing [HIGH]
Oil in the connector from a leaking sensor O-ring [MEDIUM]
Tone wheel on the exhaust phaser damaged or loose [LOW]
Engine module (5 V supply) [LOW]

description: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor (bank 1 = side with cylinder 1), usually a Hall sensor on the exhaust cam phaser. P0366 means its pulses arrive, but their number or position does not fit the crankshaft. GM expects 400 pulses per 100 engine cycles and sets the code outside 398–402, or with fewer than 4 or more than 6 pulses in the first 12 reference events at start, 8 of 10 samples, after two trips. On GM's 3.6-litre V6 in the Saab 9-4X the exhaust phaser then goes to its park position and ignition runs from the crankshaft alone; on the 2.8 turbo V6 (LAU) the fault must last 1 s, or 10 s cumulatively, below 2,520 rpm. Saab's workshop information names a damaged tone wheel, play, foreign matter and too large an air gap. Ford uses the code too but publishes no thresholds.

description: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor (bank 1 = side with cylinder 1), usually a Hall sensor on the exhaust cam phaser. P0369 means its signal is basically present, but now and then a cam pulse arrives at a crank angle where none is expected, or pulses drop out. Ford checks this in its camshaft ignition system test from 200 rpm and decides within 5 s; with this and the other cam timing codes active, Ford also suspends its oxygen sensor monitor. FCA lists P0369 among the cam sensor codes for which the cam/crank synchronisation event data should be read before replacing the sensor. GM does not use the code (2014–2019 only P0365/P0366). Typical causes are a loose contact, interference from ignition wiring and a sensor with metal debris or a borderline air gap.

Interference from the ignition (routing, shielding) [MEDIUM]
Sensor with metal debris or borderline air gap [MEDIUM]

description: Ignition G is one of the control signal lines from the engine module to an ignition module, ignition output stage or group of coils; which cylinders it serves is defined by the manufacturer, not by the code standard. The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff). P036A means the control line is open – the module sees a voltage with its driver off that indicates high resistance. No manufacturer using these codes was found – neither GM nor Ford use the Ignition E to H codes; GM reports coil control faults as P0351 ff (open above 30 kΩ) – so the description follows CARB and that analogy. The affected coils fire wrongly or not at all, causing misfire; many modules then shut off injection to those cylinders to protect the catalyst.
possible_causes: Control line or connector pin open (corrosion, pushed-back pin) [HIGH]
Ignition module or coil with integrated driver of this group faulty [MEDIUM]
Supply or ground of the ignition module faulty [MEDIUM]
Driver stage in the engine module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 500€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_description.de: Zündung G ist eine der Steuersignalleitungen vom Motorsteuergerät zu einem Zündmodul, einer Zündendstufe oder einer Spulengruppe; welche Zylinder sie bedient, legt der Hersteller fest, nicht die Code-Norm. Der Code betrifft das Steuersignal, nicht den Primärstrom der Spule (dafür gibt es eigene Codes, P0351 ff und P2300 ff). P036A heißt, die Steuerleitung ist unterbrochen – das Steuergerät sieht bei abgeschaltetem Treiber eine Spannung, die auf hohen Widerstand hindeutet. Ein Hersteller, der diese Codes nutzt, wurde nicht gefunden – weder GM noch Ford verwenden die Codes für Zündung E bis H; GM meldet Fehler der Spulenansteuerung als P0351 ff –, die Beschreibung folgt deshalb CARB und dieser Analogie. Die betroffenen Spulen zünden falsch oder gar nicht, was Aussetzer verursacht; viele Steuergeräte schalten dann die Einspritzung dieser Zylinder zum Schutz des Katalysators ab.

description: Some diesel systems give the injection control a finely divided angle signal in addition to the normal reference signal, to time and meter injection precisely – the high resolution signal. GM's 6.5-litre diesel (1997) had an optical sensor in the injection pump that delivers a high resolution track and one cam reference pulse per cylinder; P0370 is set if more than 8 consecutive cam pulses pass without progress on the high resolution counter, in the first trip. The engine then runs on backup fuelling with reduced power, and injection timing control is suspended. On the 2004 Duramax LB7 the injector driver module evaluates the 57X crank signal and reports 'no crank signal' over CAN; from 60 rpm, 100 of 120 samples sets P0370, also in the first trip. Petrol engines practically do not use the code.
possible_causes: Optical sensor in the injection pump faulty (6.5-litre) [HIGH]
Wiring or connector between pump or sensor and module [MEDIUM]
Crankshaft sensor or tone wheel (LB7: 57X signal) [MEDIUM]
Injector driver module, engine module or CAN communication [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 150€ - 1500€ (1h - 6h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

GMs 6,5-Liter-Diesel (1997) hatte einen optischen Geber in der Einspritzpumpe, der eine hochauflösende Spur und je Zylinder einen Nocken-Bezugsimpuls liefert; P0370 wird gesetzt, wenn mehr als 8 Nockenimpulse in Folge ohne Fortschritt des hochauflösenden Zählers vergehen, im ersten Fahrzyklus. description: Some diesel systems give the injection control a finely divided angle signal in addition to the normal reference signal – the high resolution signal. By its J2012 name P0374 means signal A delivers no pulses at all although the engine turns. GM's 2004 Duramax LB7 uses the code differently, for a plausibility fault: the injector driver module evaluates the 57X crank signal and reports it as implausible over CAN; from 60 rpm, 100 of 120 samples of 31.6 ms set the code, in the first trip. GM's 6.5-litre diesel with the optical sensor in the injection pump reports all faults of its high resolution track under P0370. Without the fine signal the module falls back to coarser timing, so the engine loses power and may run roughly or start poorly.

description: Diesel engines show the driver a wait-to-start lamp while the glow plugs preheat; the engine module switches it with a high-side driver. P037A means the lamp control circuit is too low – in practice a short to ground on the line to the instrument cluster. GM's diesels detect it in the driver itself: about 0.5 Ω to ground with the lamp commanded, only with a lamp configured, ignition on, more than 11 V and not while cranking. The 2015 engines need 3 s of fault, the 2016/2018 engines 10 of 15 samples; the check engine light follows after two trips. The glow plugs keep working; only the indication is missing, so the driver may start too early. CARB requires monitoring of the wait-to-start lamp circuit. Ford reports lamp faults under P0381 and does not use P037A.
possible_causes: Lamp control wire chafed through to ground between engine module and cluster [HIGH]
Lamp or LED driver in the instrument cluster shorted internally [MEDIUM]
Moisture or corrosion in the module or cluster connector [MEDIUM]
Driver in the engine module faulty [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 60€ - 400€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_description.de: Dieselmotoren zeigen dem Fahrer während des Vorglühens eine Vorglühleuchte; das Motorsteuergerät schaltet sie über einen High-Side-Treiber. P037A heißt, der Steuerkreis der Leuchte ist zu niedrig – praktisch ein Masseschluss der Leitung zum Kombiinstrument. GMs Diesel erkennen ihn im Treiber selbst: etwa 0,5 Ω gegen Masse bei angesteuerter Leuchte, nur mit konfigurierter Leuchte, Zündung an, über 11 V und nicht beim Anlassen. Die Motoren von 2015 brauchen 3 s Fehler, die von 2016/2018 10 von 15 Proben; die Motorkontrollleuchte folgt nach zwei Fahrzyklen. Die Glühkerzen arbeiten weiter; nur die Anzeige fehlt, sodass der Fahrer womöglich zu früh startet. CARB verlangt die Überwachung des Vorglühleuchten-Kreises. Ford meldet Leuchtenfehler unter P0381 und nutzt P037A nicht.

symptoms: Glow plug light does not come on or stays dim
Check engine light on (GM after two trips)
Driver starts too early, possibly poor cold start

description: P037B is the counterpart of P037A: the control circuit of the wait-to-start lamp is too high, i.e. the line carries voltage although the engine module's driver is off, or the driver sees a short to battery voltage. Fault in the instrument cluster feeding voltage back [MEDIUM]
Water damage in a connector bridging to a neighbouring pin [MEDIUM]
Driver in the engine module faulty [LOW]

GMs Diesel von 2015 prüfen im ausgeschalteten Zustand und setzen den Fehler nach 1 s bei über 11 V; die Motoren von 2016/2018 werten im Treiber einen Kurzschluss von etwa 0,5 Ω zu einer Spannungsquelle aus, 10 von 20 Proben à 100 ms. symptoms: Glow plug light stays on or flickers
Check engine light on (after two trips)

description: To heat the catalyst quickly after a cold start, some engines select a particular camshaft profile; CARB counts altered valve timing among these cold-start measures and requires components of the cold-start strategy to have their own diagnostics. P037C checks whether the requested profile is actually engaged during this phase. It is documented by code only at GM, on the 2.7-litre turbo four-cylinder (L3B) with a three-step sliding camshaft: while catalyst heating is active, the measured lift state is compared with the cold-start target, and if it is wrong in 100 of 120 cylinder events the code is set in the first trip. Two GM bulletins (19-NA-145 for 2019 Silverado/Sierra 1500 with stalling on remote start below −6 °C, 20-NA-174 for the 2020 Cadillac CT4) trace P037C to a software fault and reprogram the engine module.
possible_causes: Engine module software (GM L3B, reprogramming) [HIGH]
Profile actuator (sliding cam pin) sticking or not switching [MEDIUM]
Actuator circuit (connector, wiring) [MEDIUM]
Wrong oil viscosity or low oil level, mechanism stiff when cold [LOW]

description: To check the glow plugs, the engine module reads back the voltage or current of the glow plug supply through a sense circuit – CARB requires glow plug circuits to be monitored for correct current and voltage drop, and from model year 2010 the failure of a single plug to be detected. In the J2012 scheme P037D is the general code for this sense circuit, P037E and P037F its low and high counterparts. None of the manufacturer documents available to us uses P037D: GM's 2016/2018 diesels use only P037E/P037F, Ford 2023 its own glow plug codes (P0671 ff, P064C) and Saab reports the feedback of its glow plug control module as P0380/P0382. The description therefore follows CARB and the GM sister codes. Typically glow plug monitoring is inactive; glowing itself can work normally.
possible_causes: Sense wire open or high resistance, connector corroded [HIGH]
Glow relay or glow plug control module giving an implausible feedback [MEDIUM]
Fuse or fusible link of the glow plug supply blown [MEDIUM]
Engine module internal [LOW]

bilingual_description.de: Um die Glühkerzen zu prüfen, liest das Motorsteuergerät über einen Rückmeldekreis Spannung oder Strom der Glühversorgung zurück – CARB verlangt, die Glühkreise auf richtigen Strom und Spannungsabfall zu überwachen und ab Modelljahr 2010 den Ausfall einer einzelnen Kerze zu erkennen. In der J2012-Systematik ist P037D der allgemeine Code für diesen Rückmeldekreis, P037E und P037F sein niedriges und hohes Gegenstück. Keine der uns vorliegenden Herstellerunterlagen nutzt P037D: GMs Diesel von 2016/2018 verwenden nur P037E/P037F, Ford 2023 eigene Glühcodes (P0671 ff, P064C), und Saab meldet die Rückmeldung seines Glühzeitsteuergeräts als P0380/P0382. symptoms: Check engine light or glow plug light on
Possibly poor cold start if the cause also affects the glow plug supply

description: P037E means the voltage read back from the glow plug supply is too low. GM's 2016/2018 diesels, whose glow plug output stages sit in the engine module, compare the feedback with the battery voltage while glowing: if it is lower by more than a calibrated, current-dependent threshold – excessive voltage drop or a short to ground of the sense line – a sample counts as faulty, and 60 of 120 samples in a 50 ms grid set the code, roughly 3 of 6 s. The check only runs with the engine running (afterglow), not while cranking, and is suspended if a single plug or the supply already has an electrical fault. GM classes the cause as internal to the module (measuring circuit) and turns on the check engine light after two trips. There is no limp mode; glow plug monitoring is restricted.
possible_causes: High contact resistance in the glow plug supply (connector, ground, fusible link) [HIGH]
Measuring circuit or output stage in the engine module [MEDIUM]
Sense or supply wire shorted to ground [MEDIUM]
Weak battery or vehicle voltage at the edge of the enable range [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 80€ - 1200€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_description.de: P037E heißt: Die von der Glühversorgung zurückgelesene Spannung ist zu niedrig. GMs Diesel von 2016/2018, deren Glühendstufen im Motorsteuergerät sitzen, vergleichen die Rückmeldung beim Glühen mit der Batteriespannung: Liegt sie um mehr als eine kalibrierte, stromabhängige Schwelle darunter – übermäßiger Spannungsabfall oder Masseschluss der Rückmeldeleitung –, zählt eine Probe als fehlerhaft, und 60 von 120 Proben im 50-ms-Raster setzen den Code, also etwa 3 von 6 s. Die Prüfung läuft nur bei laufendem Motor (Nachglühen), nicht beim Anlassen, und ruht, wenn eine einzelne Kerze oder die Versorgung schon einen elektrischen Fehler hat. GM ordnet die Ursache dem Steuergerät zu (Messkreis) und schaltet die Motorkontrollleuchte nach zwei Fahrzyklen ein. Einen Notlauf gibt es nicht; die Glühüberwachung ist eingeschränkt.

symptoms: Possibly hard starting or knocking when cold

description: P037F means the voltage read back from the glow plug supply is too high. GM's 2016/2018 diesels set it when the feedback lies above a threshold derived from the run/crank relay voltage, with a feedback above 5.0 V – for example voltage is reported although the plugs are not energised, or the sense line is shorted to positive. The code needs 40 of 80 samples at 50 ms, about 2 of 4 s, only with the engine running, and turns on the check engine light after two trips; GM classes the cause as internal to the module. If there is a real short to positive or a stuck relay or output stage, the plugs can stay energised permanently, overheating them and draining the battery – then also check the single plug codes P0671 ff and P066x. CARB requires glow plug circuits to be monitored for correct current and voltage drop.
possible_causes: Sense wire chafed against positive or bridged in the connector [HIGH]
Glow relay sticking or output stage shorted (supply stays on) [MEDIUM]
Measuring circuit in the engine module [MEDIUM]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 80€ - 1200€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

symptoms: Glow plugs possibly energised permanently (flat battery, plug damage)

description: P0380 concerns glow plug circuit A – depending on the manufacturer the first group of plugs, glow relay 1 or feedback line A of the glow plug control module. Saab's 3.0 TiD (9-5, 2002) has two feedback lines from the control module; if line A at the engine module stays above 4.0 V for more than 3 s while glowing, the module is reporting a plug or circuit fault, checked once per drive cycle with the warning lamp on. In Saab's 1.9 TiD (EDC16) the glow plug control module drives two pairs of plugs, monitors them itself and reports faults over a diagnostic line that should switch inversely to the activation line. The 2010/11 Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD sets P0380 for implausible feedback or a missing supply of the module, there without check engine light. Newer GM and Ford diesels report single plugs under P0671 ff instead.
possible_causes: Glow plug(s) in circuit A burnt out [HIGH]
Glow plug control module or glow relay faulty [MEDIUM]
Wiring or connector fault (feedback line, plug connector, supply) [MEDIUM]
Missing battery or ignition supply of the control module (fuse) [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 80€ - 600€ (0.5h - 4h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: P0381 monitors the circuit of the wait-to-start lamp for an open circuit or, more generally, for faults that keep the lamp dark when commanded – CARB names a burnt-out bulb as the example, with exemptions for LCD clusters and for engines that only release the starter after preheating. GM's 2015–2018 diesels detect an open circuit in the driver by a high load impedance (about 200 kΩ in 2015), in 0.2 s or 10 of 15 samples, with the check engine light after two trips; on the 2014 Duramax LML P0381 still covered all lamp circuit faults including a short to ground. Ford's 2023 diesels check via the instrument cluster: if it reports the lamp off although on is commanded, P0381 is set within about 1 s at key-on. There is no limp mode; the risk is starting too early in the cold.
possible_causes: Control wire open or connector fault between engine module and cluster [HIGH]
Lamp or LED in the instrument cluster burnt out [MEDIUM]
Instrument cluster faulty or communication problem (Ford) [LOW]
Driver in the engine module [LOW]

symptoms: Glow plug light does not come on at key-on
Check engine light on (GM after two trips)
Driver starts too early in the cold

description: P0382 is the counterpart of P0380 for glow plug circuit B – depending on the manufacturer the second group of plugs, glow relay 2 or feedback line B of the glow plug control module. A code-specific manufacturer description exists from Saab: the 3.0 TiD V6 diesel in the 9-5 (2002) reads two feedback lines from its glow plug control module, and if line B stays above 4.0 V for more than 3 s while glowing, the module is reporting a fault in the second group of plugs; the check runs once per drive cycle, the warning lamp comes on and there is no further system reaction. The typical consequence is a poor cold start with smoke.

Glow plug control module or glow relay 2 faulty [MEDIUM]
Feedback line B, plug connector or busbar faulty [MEDIUM]

symptoms: Hard starting when cold, long cranking
White or blue smoke and rough running after a cold start
Glow plug light or check engine light on or flashing

description: Many diesels have a separate glow plug control module that the engine module commands over a control line. P0383 means this line is too low. In GM's logic for the 2010/11 Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD the engine module drives the module with a PWM signal and holds about 10 V on the line at rest (9.5–10.5 V at the signal terminal); if it reads too little voltage for more than 0.5 s – short to ground, or an open circuit or high resistance – it sets P0383, with ignition on, 9–16 V, once per ignition cycle. In that European version the code does not turn on the check engine light. Without a valid command the module does not glow, so the engine starts poorly when cold. Ford uses P0384 differently and not P0383; GM's 2016/2018 diesels have their output stages in the engine module and no such line. For US vehicles there is no code-specific source.
possible_causes: Control line between engine module and glow plug module shorted to ground or open [HIGH]
Corroded connector at the glow plug module in the engine bay [MEDIUM]
Glow plug control module faulty (input pulls the line down) [MEDIUM]
Driver in the engine module [LOW]

In GMs Logik für den Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD von 2010/11 steuert das Motorsteuergerät das Glühsteuergerät mit einem PWM-Signal und hält in Ruhe etwa 10 V auf der Leitung (9,5–10,5 V an der Signalklemme); liest es länger als 0,5 s zu wenig Spannung – Masseschluss oder Unterbrechung bzw. hoher Widerstand –, setzt es P0383, bei Zündung an, 9–16 V, einmal je Zündzyklus. symptoms: Warning lamp depending on the manufacturer

description: P0384 is the counterpart of P0383: the control line from the engine module to the glow plug control module is too high, i.e. shorted to positive. In GM's logic for the 2010/11 Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD the signal terminal should show 9.5–10.5 V; a higher voltage for more than 0.5 s, with ignition on and 9–16 V, sets the code, there without check engine light. Ford's 2023 diesels (6.7 and 3.0 litre) use P0384 differently from the J2012 name, for the supply voltage of the glow plug module: below 6.5 V, above 16.5 V or open, detected in about 1 s – today J2012 has P052F for that. So with Ford, check battery, alternator and the module's supply first. The consequence is missing or irregular preheating or a protective shutdown of the module, with a poor cold start.
possible_causes: Control line chafed against positive or bridged in the connector [HIGH]
Glow plug control module faulty internally (feeding back) [MEDIUM]
Ford: supply of the module outside 6.5–16.5 V or open (battery, alternator, fuse) [MEDIUM]
Engine module [LOW]

bilingual_description.en: P0384 is the counterpart of P0383: the control line from the engine module to the glow plug control module is too high, i.e. shorted to positive. In GM's logic for the 2010/11 Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD the signal terminal should show 9.5–10.5 V; a higher voltage for more than 0.5 s, with ignition on and 9–16 V, sets the code, there without check engine light. Ford's 2023 diesels (6.7 and 3.0 litre) use P0384 differently from the J2012 name, for the supply voltage of the glow plug module: below 6.5 V, above 16.5 V or open, detected in about 1 s – today J2012 has P052F for that. So with Ford, check battery, alternator and the module's supply first. The consequence is missing or irregular preheating or a protective shutdown of the module, with a poor cold start.
bilingual_description.de: P0384 ist das Gegenstück zu P0383: Die Steuerleitung vom Motorsteuergerät zum Glühzeitsteuergerät ist zu hoch, hat also Kurzschluss nach Plus. In GMs Logik für den Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD von 2010/11 soll die Signalklemme 9,5–10,5 V zeigen; eine höhere Spannung länger als 0,5 s, bei Zündung an und 9–16 V, setzt den Code, dort ohne Motorkontrollleuchte. Fords Diesel 2023 (6,7 und 3,0 Liter) nutzen P0384 abweichend vom J2012-Namen für die Versorgungsspannung des Glühsteuergeräts: unter 6,5 V, über 16,5 V oder offen, erkannt in etwa 1 s – dafür gibt es in J2012 heute P052F. Bei Ford also zuerst Batterie, Lichtmaschine und Versorgung des Steuergeräts prüfen. Die Folge ist fehlendes oder unregelmäßiges Vorglühen bzw. eine Schutzabschaltung des Steuergeräts, mit schlechtem Kaltstart.

symptoms: No or irregular preheating, hard starting when cold
Warning lamp depending on the manufacturer

description: Some engines have a second crankshaft sensor or a second track on the tone wheel, which the engine module checks against sensor A or the camshaft. P0385 means its signal is missing or does not match. GM's 2004 Northstar 4.6 V8 counts the crank pulses per cam pulse (target 48 ± 1, fault in 8 of 10 tests) and also flags 2 s while cranking or 0.4 s running without a match, after two trips; an active P0385 suspends the cam sensor check. GM's 3.8-litre V6 (2006) sets it when its low resolution track stays silent while the medium resolution track delivers 36 pulses, 40 of 50 samples. The Honda 3.5-litre in the 2004 Saturn Vue Redline sets it when the second crank signal is missing while the first runs, judged after 17 revolutions, in the first trip. The engine usually keeps running on sensor A.
possible_causes: Crankshaft position sensor B faulty [HIGH]
Connector or wiring open or corroded [HIGH]
Tone wheel or second track damaged [LOW]
Engine module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 60€ - 350€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_description.de: Manche Motoren haben einen zweiten Kurbelwellengeber oder eine zweite Spur auf dem Geberrad, die das Motorsteuergerät gegen Geber A oder die Nockenwelle prüft. P0385 heißt, ihr Signal fehlt oder passt nicht. GMs Northstar-4,6-V8 von 2004 zählt die Kurbelimpulse je Nockenimpuls (Soll 48 ± 1, Fehler in 8 von 10 Tests) und erkennt zusätzlich 2 s Anlassen bzw. 0,4 s Lauf ohne Übereinstimmung, nach zwei Fahrzyklen; ein aktiver P0385 sperrt die Nockenwellengeber-Prüfung. GMs 3,8-Liter-V6 (2006) setzt ihn, wenn seine niedrig auflösende Spur stumm bleibt, während die mittlere 36 Impulse liefert, 40 von 50 Proben. Der Honda-3,5-Liter im Saturn Vue Redline von 2004 setzt ihn, wenn das zweite Kurbelsignal bei laufendem ersten fehlt, beurteilt nach 17 Umdrehungen, im ersten Fahrzyklus. Der Motor läuft meist mit Geber A weiter.

description: P0386 means the signal of the second crankshaft sensor or second tone wheel track is present but implausible. GM's 2004 Northstar 4.6 V8 sets it after 5 resynchronisations within 10 s, after two trips. GM's 3.8-litre V6 (2006) expects exactly 0 or 6 low resolution pulses per 36 medium resolution pulses and one cam pulse; any other count in 40 of 50 samples sets the code, also after two trips. The Honda 3.5-litre in the 2004 Saturn Vue Redline counts implausible signals of its second crank sensor (target 44 crank pulses per 3 cam pulses, checked every half revolution, the counter dropping by one every 10 s) and sets the code at 30, about 2.2 s at idle, in the first trip. Typical causes are interference pulses, a dirty sensor or a wrong air gap; the result is jerking, misfire or longer cranking.
possible_causes: Interference pulses (wiring near the ignition, shielding) [HIGH]
Sensor dirty or air gap wrong [MEDIUM]
Tone wheel damaged [MEDIUM]
Sensor faulty [MEDIUM]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 60€ - 350€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: By its J2012 name P0387 means the signal of the second crankshaft sensor stays at a low level – typically a short to ground of the signal wire, a missing or shorted sensor supply, or with an inductive sensor an amplitude that is too small. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0387: the engines with a sensor B that we found (GM Northstar 4.6 and 3.8-litre V6, the Honda 3.5-litre in the Saturn Vue Redline) report its electrical faults under P0385 and implausible signals under P0386. The description therefore follows the J2012 name, the function of sensor B and CARB's monitoring requirement for crank angle sensors. As long as sensor A works, the engine usually keeps running; together with a sensor A fault it may not start.
possible_causes: Signal wire shorted to ground [HIGH]
Sensor faulty [MEDIUM]
Sensor supply too low or shorted [MEDIUM]
Engine module [LOW]

description: Some engines have a second crankshaft sensor or a second track on the tone wheel – GM's 3.4/3.5/3.8-litre V6 use the low resolution track of a dual Hall sensor, the Honda 3.5-litre in the Saturn Vue Redline a second sensor – which the engine module checks against sensor A or the camshaft. symptoms: Check engine light on, possibly only after several trips

description: Ignition I is one of the control signal lines from the engine module to an ignition module, ignition output stage or group of coils; which cylinders it serves is defined by the manufacturer, not by the code standard. The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff). P038A means the control line is open – the module sees a voltage with its driver off that indicates high resistance. No manufacturer using these codes was found – neither GM nor Ford use the Ignition A to J codes; GM reports coil control faults as P0351 ff – so the description follows CARB and that analogy. The affected coils fire wrongly or not at all, causing misfire; many modules then shut off injection to those cylinders to protect the catalyst.
possible_causes: Control line or connector pin open (corrosion, pushed-back pin) [HIGH]
Ignition module or coil with integrated driver of this group faulty [MEDIUM]
Supply or ground of the ignition module faulty [MEDIUM]
Driver stage in the engine module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 500€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_description.de: Zündung I ist eine der Steuersignalleitungen vom Motorsteuergerät zu einem Zündmodul, einer Zündendstufe oder einer Spulengruppe; welche Zylinder sie bedient, legt der Hersteller fest, nicht die Code-Norm. Der Code betrifft das Steuersignal, nicht den Primärstrom der Spule (dafür gibt es eigene Codes, P0351 ff und P2300 ff). P038A heißt, die Steuerleitung ist unterbrochen – das Steuergerät sieht bei abgeschaltetem Treiber eine Spannung, die auf hohen Widerstand hindeutet. Ein Hersteller, der diese Codes nutzt, wurde nicht gefunden – weder GM noch Ford verwenden die Codes für Zündung A bis J; GM meldet Fehler der Spulenansteuerung als P0351 ff –, die Beschreibung folgt deshalb CARB und dieser Analogie. Die betroffenen Spulen zünden falsch oder gar nicht, was Aussetzer verursacht; viele Steuergeräte schalten dann die Einspritzung dieser Zylinder zum Schutz des Katalysators ab.

No manufacturer using these codes was found – neither GM nor Ford use the Ignition A to J codes; GM reports coil control faults as P0351 ff – so the description follows CARB and that analogy. The affected coils fire wrongly or not at all, causing misfire; many modules then shut off injection to those cylinders to protect the catalyst.
possible_causes: Control line shorted to ground (chafing) [HIGH]
Input of the ignition module or coil shorted [MEDIUM]
Moisture or corrosion in the connector [MEDIUM]
Driver stage in the engine module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 500€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0390 means no or too few exhaust cam pulses arrive from bank 2 while the crankshaft turns. GM's 3.0 twin-turbo V6 (LGW) sets it after 5.5 s without a cam pulse, 4 s of cranking or fewer than 4 pulses in 3 s, after two trips; for GM it collects all circuit faults. GM's 3.6-litre V6 in the Saab 9-4X also counts 800 of 1,000 engine cycles without a pulse. Ford checks the crank-to-cam ratio from 200 rpm within 5 s, and the 2004 Northstar counts missing signal changes up to 16. The bank 2 exhaust phaser then locks in its base position; the engine keeps running on the crank and intake cam sensors. FCA advises saving the synchronisation data before replacing the sensor.
possible_causes: Connector or wiring of the bank 2 exhaust sensor open or corroded (signal, 5 V, ground) [HIGH]
Camshaft position sensor faulty [HIGH]
Oil contamination or leak at the sensor, sensor loose [MEDIUM]
Tone wheel on the phaser damaged or wrongly fitted after timing chain work [MEDIUM]
Engine module, or 5 V reference shorted by another sensor [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 60€ - 300€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_description.de: Nockenwellengeber B ist der Auslass-Nockenwellengeber; Bank 2 ist die Seite ohne Zylinder 1, der Code kommt also nur bei V- und Boxermotoren mit je einem Auslassgeber pro Bank vor. P0390 heißt, es kommen bei drehender Kurbelwelle keine oder zu wenige Auslass-Nockenimpulse von Bank 2. Der Auslassversteller der Bank 2 verriegelt dann in Grundstellung; der Motor läuft mit Kurbel- und Einlassgeber weiter. FCA rät, vor dem Gebertausch die Synchronisationsdaten zu sichern.

symptoms: Loss of power (bank 2 exhaust cam timing in its base position)

description: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0391 means the bank 2 exhaust cam signal is present, but the number or position of its pulses does not fit the crankshaft. GM's 3.0 twin-turbo V6 (LGW) expects 4 to 6 pulses in the first 12 reference events and 398 to 402 per 100 engine cycles on the four-tooth wheel, after two trips; the Saab 9-4X 2.8 turbo V6 (LAU) checks pulses per crank revolution below 2,520 rpm. The 2004 Northstar requires each edge within a window of crank teeth, and GM's 2004 3.6-litre V6 (LY7) counts implausible signals over two drive cycles. The phaser then goes to its base position and the engine cranks longer. Mechanical causes – damaged tone wheel, jumped chain – matter more here than with P0390.
possible_causes: Tone wheel on the bank 2 exhaust phaser damaged, loose or wrongly fitted [HIGH]
Interference or loose contact producing extra edges [MEDIUM]
Sensor loose, wrong O-ring or gap, chips on the magnet [MEDIUM]
Timing chain stretched or jumped [MEDIUM]
Sensor faulty [MEDIUM]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 60€ - 1200€ (0.5h - 8h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

symptoms: Loss of power (bank 2 exhaust cam timing in its base position)

description: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0392 means the bank 2 exhaust cam signal stays low without edges – typically a short to ground of the signal wire, a sensor output stuck low or a missing 5 V reference. Only manufacturers with separate low and high codes use it: on the Saab 9-4X 2.8 turbo V6 (GM LAU) the signal must stay low without pulses for more than 1 s, or 10 s cumulatively, after more than 10 crank revolutions and below 2,520 rpm, after two trips; GM's 2004/2005 3.6-litre V6 (LY7, LP1) counts the fault over two drive cycles. Newer GM petrol engines (2015–2020) and Ford report the same fault as P0390. The consequence is as for P0390: cam timing on bank 2 in its base position, loss of power, longer cranking.
possible_causes: Signal wire shorted to ground [HIGH]
Sensor faulty internally (output stuck low) [MEDIUM]
5 V reference missing (shorted by another sensor on the same circuit) [MEDIUM]
Engine module [LOW]

description: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0394 means the bank 2 exhaust cam signal now and then appears at a position where it is not expected relative to the crank reference – sporadic extra or missing edges. Ford checks this in its camshaft ignition system test from 200 rpm and decides within 5 s. Tone wheel or phaser damaged, or sensor loose [MEDIUM]

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1. P0395 is the general circuit code for this pressure sensor, meant for modules that do not separate open circuits and shorts into low and high. The only manufacturer we found using this code family – GM's European 2.0 CDTI diesel, documented in Saab 9-5 workshop information – splits the faults into low and high (P0397, P0398) and does not use P0395; VW's US 2.0 TDI engines with pressure-sensing glow plugs report such faults with their own codes (P13CE ff). The description therefore follows CARB's requirement to monitor input sensors for circuit faults. The sensor has three wires (5 V reference, ground, signal); without it the module drops combustion control for that cylinder.
possible_causes: Connector at the pressure-sensing glow plug loose or corroded [HIGH]
Reference, signal or ground wire open or shorted [MEDIUM]
Sensor electronics in the glow plug faulty [MEDIUM]
Engine module (reference voltage or input) [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 400€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_description.de: Manche Diesel haben einen Brennraumdrucksensor in der Glühkerze; damit regelt das Motorsteuergerät die Einspritzung je Zylinder. Dieser Code betrifft Zylinder 1. P0395 ist der allgemeine Kreiscode für diesen Drucksensor, gedacht für Steuergeräte, die Unterbrechung und Kurzschluss nicht nach niedrig und hoch trennen. Der einzige gefundene Nutzer dieser Codefamilie – GMs europäischer 2.0-CDTI-Diesel, beschrieben in der Saab-9-5-Werkstattinformation – trennt nach niedrig und hoch (P0397, P0398) und nutzt P0395 nicht; VWs US-2.0-TDI mit Druckglühkerzen melden solche Fehler mit eigenen Codes (P13CE ff). Der Sensor hat drei Leitungen (5-V-Referenz, Masse, Signal); ohne ihn verzichtet das Steuergerät auf die Verbrennungsregelung dieses Zylinders.

symptoms: Check engine light on (often after two trips)
Usually barely noticeable – combustion control for the cylinder is switched off
Possibly rougher running, more noise or slightly higher consumption

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1. P0396 means the sensor signal is electrically fine but does not fit the expected value. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code; a GM patent shows how such a check works: in overrun the measured peak pressure is compared with a compression pressure calculated from manifold pressure and compression ratio, and the pressure values are also compared with limits and with crankshaft speed fluctuation. GM's European diesel in the Saab 9-5 uses the peak pressure in overrun anyway to find top dead centre. Typical causes are sensor drift from combustion deposits or a glow plug that leaks or is wrongly torqued. CARB requires a two-sided plausibility check of input sensors where feasible.
possible_causes: Sensor in the glow plug drifting (deposits, ageing) [HIGH]
Glow plug leaking or wrongly torqued (pressure transmitted wrongly) [MEDIUM]
Contact resistance in connector or ground [MEDIUM]
Actual compression pressure differs (valve, rings) [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 120€ - 500€ (1h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

symptoms: Combustion control for the cylinder off – slightly rough running, more noise

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1. P0397 means the sensor signal stays below its lower limit. GM's European 2.0 CDTI diesel (Saab 9-5, 2010) sets it when the signal is below the threshold for more than 2 s with the engine running, checked once per drive cycle, with the check engine light after two trips; the displayed maximum combustion pressure then reads 0 kPa instead of the normal 0–9,000 kPa. Saab names an open or grounded 5 V reference and a signal wire shorted to ground as causes; the glow plug should measure 3–12 Ω between reference and ground. Without the signal, combustion control for this cylinder is switched off, which is usually barely noticeable.
possible_causes: 5 V reference wire open or shorted to ground [HIGH]
Signal wire shorted to ground [MEDIUM]

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code; GM patents show how such an evaluation works: peak and minimum pressure are compared with limits and with a motoring pressure calculated from manifold pressure and compression ratio, and the ratio of measured to motoring pressure is compared between cylinders. A low value can mean weak combustion or compression – leaking valve, worn rings, leaking glow plug seat, an injector delivering too little – or a sensor drifting downwards. description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1. It is documented by code at Audi, surprisingly on a petrol engine: on the 2015 S3 (2.0 TFSI, engine CYFB) the four 'pressure too high' codes came on with the EPC lamp, usually together with misfire codes P0300–P0304 and the manufacturer code for hiding a cylinder; the cause was a software fault that mis-detected misfire, and a software update fixed it. description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1. Typical causes are a coked or leaking injector, compression loss or poor fuel; the engine runs roughly and smokes more.

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 2. P03A1 means the sensor signal stays below its lower limit. GM's European 2.0 CDTI diesel (Saab 9-5, 2010) sets it when the signal is below the threshold for more than 2 s with the engine running, checked once per drive cycle, with the check engine light after two trips; the displayed maximum combustion pressure then reads 0 kPa instead of the normal 0–9,000 kPa. Saab names an open or grounded 5 V reference and a signal wire shorted to ground as causes; the glow plug should measure 3–12 Ω between reference and ground. Without the signal, combustion control for this cylinder is switched off, which is usually barely noticeable.
possible_causes: 5 V reference wire open or shorted to ground [HIGH]
Signal wire shorted to ground [MEDIUM]
Sensor electronics of the glow plug faulty [MEDIUM]
Engine module supplies no reference [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 400€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 2. P03A4 means the pressure measured in the cylinder is lower than expected while the sensor itself is electrically fine. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code; GM patents show how such an evaluation works: peak and minimum pressure are compared with limits and with a motoring pressure calculated from manifold pressure and compression ratio, and the ratio of measured to motoring pressure is compared between cylinders. A low value can mean weak combustion or compression – leaking valve, worn rings, leaking glow plug seat, an injector delivering too little – or a sensor drifting downwards. The usual consequence is rough running and more smoke.

Injector delivering too little or coked [MEDIUM]
Sensor drifting downwards (deposits) [MEDIUM]
Misfire or partial combustion [LOW]

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 2. P03A5 means the pressure measured or calculated for the cylinder is higher than expected. It is documented by code at Audi, surprisingly on a petrol engine: on the 2015 S3 (2.0 TFSI, engine CYFB) the four 'pressure too high' codes came on with the EPC lamp, usually together with misfire codes P0300–P0304 and the manufacturer code for hiding a cylinder; the cause was a software fault that mis-detected misfire, and a software update fixed it. How Audi determines the pressure, the bulletin does not say. On diesels with pressure-sensing glow plugs GM patents describe a peak pressure above its limit – too much or too early injection, or a sensor drifting upwards. If the cylinder is shut off, power drops noticeably.

Injector delivering too much or dripping [MEDIUM]
Sensor drifting upwards (diesel pressure-sensing glow plug) [MEDIUM]
Knock or pre-ignition on a petrol engine [LOW]

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 2. GM's European 2.0 CDTI diesel (Saab 9-5, 2010) uses P03A6 as 'pressure variation too low', with three sub-checks, and sets it when the signal is outside its range for more than 0.2 s with the engine running; its fault table counts it among the signal performance faults together with the erratic code. Usually there are no noticeable symptoms.

Contact resistance in connector or ground [MEDIUM]
Actual compression loss or misfire in the cylinder [LOW]

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 2. P03A8 means the combustion quality in the cylinder, evaluated from the combustion pressure, is abnormal. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code; a GM patent shows the method: the ratio of measured to motoring pressure is turned into a measure of combustion energy, an inequality index against the neighbouring cylinders in firing order is formed, and a two-sided threshold detects partial combustion, misfire, injector and compression faults. CARB requires engines with a combustion or combustion quality sensor to detect misfire more sharply (5 % in 1,000 revolutions). Typical causes are a coked or leaking injector, compression loss or poor fuel; the engine runs roughly and smokes more.
possible_causes: Injector coked, leaking or delivering the wrong quantity [HIGH]
Compression loss (valve, rings) [MEDIUM]
Partial combustion or misfire (fuel quality, EGR distribution) [MEDIUM]
Pressure sensor drifting [LOW]

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 3. P03A9 is the general circuit code for this pressure sensor, meant for modules that do not separate open circuits and shorts into low and high. The only manufacturer we found using this code family – GM's European 2.0 CDTI diesel, documented in Saab 9-5 workshop information – splits the faults into low and high (P03AB, P03AC) and does not use P03A9; VW's US 2.0 TDI engines with pressure-sensing glow plugs report such faults with their own codes (P13CE ff). The description therefore follows CARB's requirement to monitor input sensors for circuit faults. The sensor has three wires (5 V reference, ground, signal); without it the module drops combustion control for that cylinder.
possible_causes: Connector at the pressure-sensing glow plug loose or corroded [HIGH]
Reference, signal or ground wire open or shorted [MEDIUM]
Sensor electronics in the glow plug faulty [MEDIUM]
Engine module (reference voltage or input) [LOW]

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 3. P03AA means the sensor signal is electrically fine but does not fit the expected value. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code; a GM patent shows how such a check works: in overrun the measured peak pressure is compared with a compression pressure calculated from manifold pressure and compression ratio, and the pressure values are also compared with limits and with crankshaft speed fluctuation. GM's European diesel in the Saab 9-5 uses the peak pressure in overrun anyway to find top dead centre. Typical causes are sensor drift from combustion deposits or a glow plug that leaks or is wrongly torqued. CARB requires a two-sided plausibility check of input sensors where feasible.

Glow plug leaking or wrongly torqued (pressure transmitted wrongly) [MEDIUM]
Contact resistance in connector or ground [MEDIUM]
Actual compression pressure differs (valve, rings) [LOW]

Keine uns vorliegende Herstellerunterlage beschreibt den Code; ein GM-Patent zeigt, wie eine solche Prüfung arbeitet: Im Schub wird der gemessene Spitzendruck mit einem aus Saugrohrdruck und Verdichtung berechneten Kompressionsdruck verglichen, zudem werden die Druckwerte mit Grenzen und mit der Drehungleichförmigkeit der Kurbelwelle verglichen. GMs europäischer Diesel im Saab 9-5 nutzt das Druckmaximum im Schub ohnehin zur OT-Bestimmung. Typisch sind Sensordrift durch Verbrennungsablagerungen oder eine undichte bzw. falsch angezogene Glühkerze. CARB verlangt, wo machbar, eine zweiseitige Plausibilitätsprüfung von Eingangssensoren.

symptoms: Combustion control for the cylinder off – slightly rough running, more noise

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 3. P03AB means the sensor signal stays below its lower limit. GM's European 2.0 CDTI diesel (Saab 9-5, 2010) sets it when the signal is below the threshold for more than 2 s with the engine running, checked once per drive cycle, with the check engine light after two trips; the displayed maximum combustion pressure then reads 0 kPa instead of the normal 0–9,000 kPa. Saab names an open or grounded 5 V reference and a signal wire shorted to ground as causes; the glow plug should measure 3–12 Ω between reference and ground. Without the signal, combustion control for this cylinder is switched off, which is usually barely noticeable.
possible_causes: 5 V reference wire open or shorted to ground [HIGH]
Signal wire shorted to ground [MEDIUM]
Sensor electronics of the glow plug faulty [MEDIUM]
Engine module supplies no reference [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 400€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 3. P03AD means the sensor signal is erratic or drops out for moments. GM's European 2.0 CDTI diesel (Saab 9-5, 2010) calls it 'circuit erratic' and sets it when the signal is outside its range for more than 0.2 s with the engine running; its fault table groups the erratic and pressure variation codes together as signal performance faults. The test plan checks a reference of 4.8–5.2 V and a ground below 5 Ω before the glow plug is replaced. Typical causes are a loose contact at the glow plug connector, a chafed engine harness or sensor electronics that become unstable with temperature. The code often comes and goes; combustion control for the cylinder is suspended while it is active.
possible_causes: Loose contact at the glow plug connector [HIGH]
Chafing or broken wire in the engine harness [MEDIUM]
Sensor electronics of the glow plug unstable with temperature [MEDIUM]
Interference from ground problems [LOW]

symptoms: Often no symptoms, the code comes and goes

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 3. P03AE means the pressure measured in the cylinder is lower than expected while the sensor itself is electrically fine. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code; GM patents show how such an evaluation works: peak and minimum pressure are compared with limits and with a motoring pressure calculated from manifold pressure and compression ratio, and the ratio of measured to motoring pressure is compared between cylinders. A low value can mean weak combustion or compression – leaking valve, worn rings, leaking glow plug seat, an injector delivering too little – or a sensor drifting downwards. The usual consequence is rough running and more smoke.
possible_causes: Compression loss (valve, piston rings, leaking glow plug seat) [MEDIUM]
Injector delivering too little or coked [MEDIUM]
Sensor drifting downwards (deposits) [MEDIUM]
Misfire or partial combustion [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 100€ - 1500€ (1h - 6h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

symptoms: Lack of power, rough running, possibly misfire on this cylinder

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 3. P03AF means the pressure measured or calculated for the cylinder is higher than expected. It is documented by code at Audi, surprisingly on a petrol engine: on the 2015 S3 (2.0 TFSI, engine CYFB) the four 'pressure too high' codes came on with the EPC lamp, usually together with misfire codes P0300–P0304 and the manufacturer code for hiding a cylinder; the cause was a software fault that mis-detected misfire, and a software update fixed it. How Audi determines the pressure, the bulletin does not say. On diesels with pressure-sensing glow plugs GM patents describe a peak pressure above its limit – too much or too early injection, or a sensor drifting upwards. If the cylinder is shut off, power drops noticeably.
possible_causes: Engine module software (Audi S3 2015, engine CYFB) [HIGH]
Injector delivering too much or dripping [MEDIUM]
Sensor drifting upwards (diesel pressure-sensing glow plug) [MEDIUM]
Knock or pre-ignition on a petrol engine [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 80€ - 800€ (0.5h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

symptoms: EPC or check engine light on
Misfire codes, possibly a cylinder shut off with noticeable loss of power

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 3. GM's European 2.0 CDTI diesel (Saab 9-5, 2010) uses P03B0 as 'pressure variation too low', with three sub-checks, and sets it when the signal is outside its range for more than 0.2 s with the engine running; its fault table counts it among the signal performance faults together with the erratic code. What exactly is measured, Saab does not explain; presumably it is the swing of the pressure signal within an engine cycle – too small a swing means the signal barely responds, for example because the glow rod is stuck by carbon and no longer transmits the pressure, or because pressure build-up is missing. Usually there are no noticeable symptoms.
possible_causes: Pressure-sensing glow plug faulty or coked (glow rod stuck) [HIGH]
Contact resistance in connector or ground [MEDIUM]
Actual compression loss or misfire in the cylinder [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 100€ - 450€ (1h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 3. P03B2 means the combustion quality in the cylinder, evaluated from the combustion pressure, is abnormal. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code; a GM patent shows the method: the ratio of measured to motoring pressure is turned into a measure of combustion energy, an inequality index against the neighbouring cylinders in firing order is formed, and a two-sided threshold detects partial combustion, misfire, injector and compression faults. CARB requires engines with a combustion or combustion quality sensor to detect misfire more sharply (5 % in 1,000 revolutions). Typical causes are a coked or leaking injector, compression loss or poor fuel; the engine runs roughly and smokes more.
possible_causes: Injector coked, leaking or delivering the wrong quantity [HIGH]
Compression loss (valve, rings) [MEDIUM]
Partial combustion or misfire (fuel quality, EGR distribution) [MEDIUM]
Pressure sensor drifting [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 150€ - 1500€ (1h - 6h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

symptoms: Loss of power, more smoke and consumption

description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 4. P03B3 is the general circuit code for this pressure sensor, meant for modules that do not separate open circuits and shorts into low and high. The only manufacturer we found using this code family – GM's European 2.0 CDTI diesel, documented in Saab 9-5 workshop information – splits the faults into low and high (P03B5, P03B6) and does not use P03B3; VW's US 2.0 TDI engines with pressure-sensing glow plugs report such faults with their own codes (P13CE ff). The description therefore follows CARB's requirement to monitor input sensors for circuit faults. The sensor has three wires (5 V reference, ground, signal); without it the module drops combustion control for that cylinder.
possible_causes: Connector at the pressure-sensing glow plug loose or corroded [HIGH]
Reference, signal or ground wire open or shorted [MEDIUM]
Sensor electronics in the glow plug faulty [MEDIUM]
Engine module (reference voltage or input) [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 400€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.
