description: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 4. P03B4 means the sensor signal is electrically fine but does not fit the expected value. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code; a GM patent shows how such a check works: in overrun the measured peak pressure is compared with a compression pressure calculated from manifold pressure and compression ratio, and the pressure values are also compared with limits and with crankshaft speed fluctuation. GM's European diesel in the Saab 9-5 uses the peak pressure in overrun anyway to find top dead centre. Typical causes are sensor drift from combustion deposits or a glow plug that leaks or is wrongly torqued. CARB requires a two-sided plausibility check of input sensors where feasible.
possible_causes: Sensor in the glow plug drifting (deposits, ageing) [HIGH]
Glow plug leaking or wrongly torqued (pressure transmitted wrongly) [MEDIUM]
Contact resistance in connector or ground [MEDIUM]

bilingual_description.en: On some engines the intake cam phaser (camshaft position actuator A) has its own position sensors, which tell the engine module where the phaser actually is; sensor C is the third of them, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. P03E5 is the general circuit code for this sensor: the module sees an open circuit or a signal outside its valid window on the supply, signal or ground line. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. GM's 2.7-litre engine monitors comparable position sensors on its sliding camshaft under other codes (P2C05 ff), with an open circuit above 200 kΩ and a short below 0.5 Ω in 4 of 5 samples – only as a comparison. The phaser is then usually held in its base position. CARB requires electronic parts of variable valve timing systems to be monitored as comprehensive components.

description: Engines with cam profile switching move the intake camshaft between lift profiles with actuators – for example pins that shift a sliding cam – and position sensors report which profile is engaged. The engine module learns reference values of position sensor A, such as its end-position levels or the expected pulse position relative to the crankshaft and camshaft sensors; a Ford patent describes correcting this position for the cam phase. P03E9 means the learned value lies outside the permitted adaptation limit, so profile detection is no longer reliable and the module usually stays in a safe profile. No manufacturer document available to us describes the code or its limits; GM's 2.7-litre sliding cam has no learning-limit code. CARB lists a pin that does not reach its position among the faults to be detected.
possible_causes: Position sensor A or actuator with integrated sensor worn or faulty (signal drift) [HIGH]
Actuator pin or sliding piece stiff, guide worn, dirty oil [MEDIUM]
Actuator not relearned or wrongly fitted after replacement [MEDIUM]
Connector or wiring with contact resistance [LOW]
Engine module software (learning algorithm) [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 150€ - 900€ (1h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_description.de: Motoren mit Nockenprofil-Umschaltung schalten die Einlassnockenwelle mit Stellern zwischen Hubprofilen um – etwa mit Stiften, die einen Schiebenocken verschieben –, und Positionssensoren melden, welches Profil eingelegt ist. Das Motorsteuergerät lernt Referenzwerte von Positionssensor A, etwa seine Endlagenpegel oder die erwartete Pulslage relativ zu Kurbel- und Nockenwellengeber; ein Ford-Patent beschreibt, diese Lage um die Nockenwellenphase zu korrigieren. P03E9 heißt, der gelernte Wert liegt außerhalb der zulässigen Adaptionsgrenze, die Profilerkennung ist nicht mehr verlässlich, und das Steuergerät bleibt meist in einem sicheren Profil. Keine uns vorliegende Herstellerunterlage beschreibt den Code oder seine Grenzen; GMs 2,7-Liter-Schiebenocken hat keinen Lerngrenzen-Code. CARB zählt einen Stift, der seine Position nicht erreicht, zu den zu erkennenden Fehlern.

description: With a sliding camshaft, the intake camshaft (camshaft A) carries movable cam pieces with several lift profiles; solenoid actuators shoot a pin into a groove in the piece and shift it axially. Actuator C is the third of these actuators – not a profile position. The only known user is GM's 2.7-litre turbo four (L3B, three-step sliding cam, from model year 2019). P03EC means the actuator's control circuit is open: GM checks the circuit with the driver on and sets the code at an impedance of 200 kΩ or more (4 of 5 samples, above 11 V, MIL on the first trip). The actuator can then not shift its cam piece, and lift switching and cylinder deactivation are blocked.
possible_causes: Actuator connector loose, corroded or pin pushed back (often after valve cover work) [HIGH]
Actuator solenoid open [MEDIUM]
Wire broken in the engine harness [MEDIUM]
Driver in the engine module [LOW]

P03EE heißt, der Steuerkreis hat Schluss nach Versorgungsspannung: GM prüft bei ausgeschaltetem Treiber und setzt den Code ab 0,5 Ω oder weniger zwischen Signal und Versorgung (4 von 5 Proben, über 11 V, Kontrollleuchte in der ersten Fahrt). Der Steller kann sein Nockenstück dann nicht schieben, Hubumschaltung und Zylinderabschaltung sind gesperrt.

symptoms: Lift switching and cylinder deactivation blocked, higher consumption
Possibly rough running if a cam piece stays in the wrong position

description: With a sliding camshaft, the intake camshaft (camshaft A) carries movable cam pieces with several lift profiles; solenoid actuators shoot a pin into a groove in the piece and shift it axially. Actuator C is the third of these actuators – not a profile position. The only known user is GM's 2.7-litre turbo four (L3B, three-step sliding cam, from model year 2019). P03EF is the function check: in the standard's wording the actuator does not do what is commanded. A Hall sensor in the actuator reports the pin position. GM uses this code for a pin that extends without being commanded (4 of 5 cylinder events, MIL on the first trip); a pin that does not extend on command shows up there through the cam piece position sensors (GM-specific codes P30BE ff). GM bulletins name swapped actuator connectors and actuators fitted to the wrong camshaft after repairs.
possible_causes: Actuator faulty inside: pin extends uncommanded (weak return spring) [HIGH]
Actuator connectors swapped, or intake and exhaust actuators fitted to the wrong camshaft [MEDIUM]
Interference in the Hall feedback signal (ground, connector) [MEDIUM]
Cam piece sticking or shift groove worn [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 150€ - 1500€ (0.5h - 6h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: On some engines the exhaust cam phaser (camshaft position actuator B) has its own position sensors, which tell the engine module where the phaser actually is; sensor C is the third of them, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. P03F6 is the general circuit code for this sensor: the module sees an open circuit or a signal outside its valid window on the supply, signal or ground line. Engine module [LOW]

Keine uns vorliegende Herstellerunterlage nutzt diesen Code (Tabellen von GM, Ford und FCA geprüft); das Einlass-Gegenstück P03E5 ff ebenso wenig. Der Versteller wird dann meist in Grundstellung gehalten.

bilingual_description.en: On some engines the exhaust cam phaser (camshaft position actuator B) has its own position sensors, which tell the engine module where the phaser actually is; sensor C is the third of them, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. This is a different family from the sliding-cam position sensors (P2C05 ff). P03F8 means the signal stays below its lower limit – signal wire shorted to ground, 5 V supply open, or the sensor shorted internally. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code (GM, Ford and FCA tables checked); the intake counterpart P03E5 ff is equally unused. The phaser is then usually held in its base position.

description: Ignition K is one of up to twelve control signal lines (A to L) from the engine module to an ignition coil with integrated output stage or to an ignition module – plausibly the 11th channel, but the code standard leaves the assignment to the manufacturer. The code concerns this logic-level signal, not the coil's primary circuit (coil K has its own codes, P0361 and P2330 ff). P03FA means the control line is open or high-resistance: with its driver switched off the module sees a voltage that indicates a missing load (GM uses more than 30 kΩ for comparable coil drivers). The coil fires wrongly or not at all; the misfire usually also sets P0300 ff, and many modules shut off injection to that cylinder to protect the catalyst. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – it would only concern twelve-cylinder engines, whose makers publish no OBD summaries; GM and Ford tables stop at eight and ten cylinders.
possible_causes: Control line or connector pin open (corrosion, pushed-back pin) [HIGH]
Coil with integrated output stage or ignition module faulty [MEDIUM]
Supply or ground of the coil or module missing [MEDIUM]
Driver in the engine module [LOW]

bilingual_description.de: Zündung K ist eine von bis zu zwölf Steuersignalleitungen (A bis L) vom Motorsteuergerät zu einer Zündspule mit integrierter Endstufe oder zu einem Zündmodul – naheliegend der elfte Kanal, die Zuordnung legt aber der Hersteller fest, nicht die Code-Norm. Der Code betrifft dieses Steuersignal, nicht den Primärkreis der Spule (Spule K hat eigene Codes, P0361 und P2330 ff). description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0400 is the general flow fault of EGR system A, used where the module does not classify the error as too little (P0401) or too much (P0402). Ford petrol engines with a stepper-motor valve open and close the valve at steady part load and compare intake manifold pressure with and without EGR; too small a normalised difference (below 1.0) sets P0400, MIL after two trips. GM diesels use the code differently, for air-mass checks with excessive EGR rate. EGR is then usually switched off.
possible_causes: EGR passages or valve carboned up [HIGH]
EGR valve stiff or faulty [MEDIUM]
Leak in the intake or EGR pipe [MEDIUM]
MAP or MAF sensor inaccurate [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 80€ - 600€ (1h - 3h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_description.en: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0400 is the general flow fault of EGR system A, used where the module does not classify the error as too little (P0401) or too much (P0402). Ford petrol engines with a stepper-motor valve open and close the valve at steady part load and compare intake manifold pressure with and without EGR; too small a normalised difference (below 1.0) sets P0400, MIL after two trips. GM diesels use the code differently, for air-mass checks with excessive EGR rate. EGR is then usually switched off.
bilingual_description.de: Die Abgasrückführung (AGR) leitet einen Teil des Abgases zurück in den Ansaugtrakt, um Verbrennungstemperatur und Stickoxide zu senken. P0400 ist der allgemeine Durchflussfehler des AGR-Systems A, genutzt, wenn das Steuergerät den Fehler nicht als zu wenig (P0401) oder zu viel (P0402) einordnet. Ford-Benziner mit Schrittmotorventil öffnen und schließen das Ventil bei gleichmäßiger Teillast und vergleichen den Saugrohrdruck mit und ohne AGR; eine zu kleine normierte Differenz (unter 1,0) setzt P0400, Kontrollleuchte nach zwei Fahrten. GM-Diesel nutzen den Code anders, für Luftmassenprüfungen mit zu hoher AGR-Rate. Die AGR wird dann meist abgeschaltet.

symptoms: Pinging under load or rough idle, depending on direction

description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0401 means too little exhaust is recirculated. Petrol engines open the valve briefly and expect a rise in manifold pressure (GM 2004 V6, MIL on the first trip); older Ford systems measure the pressure drop across an orifice (DPFE sensor). Diesels balance the air mass: if the meter sees more fresh air than the target EGR rate allows, too little exhaust flows (GM, Ford, Saab, usually MIL after two trips). Diesel causes are mostly a coked valve or cooler, petrol causes blocked passages.

specific_definitions.AUDI: Restriction in the EGR passages usually caused by carbon buildup, The EGR Valve is defective, Lack of proper vacuum or electrical signal to the EGR valve, Malfunctioning EGR Vacuum supply solenoid, Lack of proper EGR system feedback to the computer from the: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor (MAP), Differential EGR Pressure Feedback Sensor (DPFE), EGR Valve Position Sensor (EVP), EGR Temperature Sensor

possible_causes: EGR passages, valve or cooler carboned up [HIGH]
EGR valve faulty or stuck closed [HIGH]
Ford: DPFE sensor or its hoses blocked, cracked or swapped [MEDIUM]
Diesel: air mass meter drifting or air leak after the turbo [MEDIUM]
Vacuum control of the valve faulty [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 100€ - 900€ (1h - 4h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_description.en: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0401 means too little exhaust is recirculated. Petrol engines open the valve briefly and expect a rise in manifold pressure (GM 2004 V6, MIL on the first trip); older Ford systems measure the pressure drop across an orifice (DPFE sensor). Diesels balance the air mass: if the meter sees more fresh air than the target EGR rate allows, too little exhaust flows (GM, Ford, Saab, usually MIL after two trips). Diesel causes are mostly a coked valve or cooler, petrol causes blocked passages.
bilingual_description.de: Die Abgasrückführung (AGR) leitet einen Teil des Abgases zurück in den Ansaugtrakt, um Verbrennungstemperatur und Stickoxide zu senken. P0401 heißt, es wird zu wenig Abgas zurückgeführt. Benziner öffnen das Ventil kurz und erwarten einen Anstieg des Saugrohrdrucks (GM 2004 V6, Kontrollleuchte in der ersten Fahrt); ältere Ford-Systeme messen den Druckabfall an einer Blende (DPFE-Sensor). Diesel bilanzieren die Luftmasse: Misst der Luftmassenmesser mehr Frischluft, als die Soll-AGR-Rate zulässt, fließt zu wenig Abgas (GM, Ford, Saab, meist Kontrollleuchte nach zwei Fahrten). Beim Diesel sind meist Ventil oder Kühler verkokt, beim Benziner die Kanäle zugesetzt.

description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0402 means too much exhaust is recirculated, or exhaust flows although the valve should be closed – CARB explicitly requires a leaking valve to be detected. Ford's DPFE check at idle with EGR off expects no pressure difference above the engine-off value; Ford diesels compare the measured EGR rate with the expected one, GM diesels the fresh-air deviation in the opposite direction. Petrol engines idle roughly or stall, diesels smoke and may lose power.
possible_causes: EGR valve stuck open, dirt under the seat [HIGH]
Ford: DPFE sensor drifting or hose wrong [MEDIUM]
Diesel: air leak between air mass meter and turbo, MAF drift [MEDIUM]
Valve control opens unintentionally [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 100€ - 800€ (1h - 3h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0403 concerns the electrical drive of the EGR valve – solenoid, stepper motor, DC motor or vacuum regulator. The module checks the output and sets the code for an open circuit (GM: above 200 kΩ, MIL after two trips; Ford after 4 s, MIL after two trips). Newer systems report shorts separately as P0489 (low) and P0490 (high); Ford and older GM systems include them in P0403. EGR is then switched off for the rest of the trip.

Broken control or supply wire [MEDIUM]

Driver in the engine module [LOW]

description: EGR temperature sensor A measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – GM and Ford report this sensor as P040B to P040E – so the description follows CARB's requirement to check input circuits for continuity and range. A substitute value is used and the EGR cooler check is suspended.

description: EGR temperature sensor A measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it. Like a coolant sensor it is an NTC, so a low voltage means hot. P040B is its plausibility check: after a cold start the sensor must warm up once hot exhaust flows. Ford diesels set the code if it rises by less than 10 °C after load; GM diesels if it barely changes after at least 8 hours off and a defined EGR flow (MIL after two trips). A sooted sensor tip or a lack of EGR flow are typical causes.
possible_causes: Sensor sluggish, tip sooted [HIGH]
Sensor drifting or faulty [MEDIUM]
No EGR flow (valve or cooler blocked), sensor sees no heat [MEDIUM]

description: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. P0412 is the general electrical fault in the control circuit of valve A, detected by comparing the driver's feedback with its commanded state. GM nutzt P0418 für eine Unterbrechung (ab 200 kΩ, 20 von 25 Proben, Kontrollleuchte nach zwei Fahrten) und P2257/P2258 für Kurzschlüsse; Saab und Toyota beschreiben denselben Kreis. Läuft die Pumpe nicht, kann P0411 folgen. Ein Relais mit verschweißten Kontakten lässt die Pumpe dauernd laufen – Subaru rief deshalb Fahrzeuge zurück, weil die Pumpe überhitzen konnte.

description: After a cold start the secondary air (AIR) pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; a shut-off valve opens the path and stops exhaust from flowing back. It is checked like P0418 by comparing the driver's feedback with its commanded state. No manufacturer document available to us describes P0419 specifically; Pierburg's fault table lists it as relay B with the same remedies as relay A.
possible_causes: Pump relay B faulty [HIGH]
Wire or connector to relay B faulty [HIGH]
Fuse or supply [MEDIUM]
Pump B blocked (consequential damage) [LOW]
Engine module [LOW]

description: EGR temperature sensor B measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it. Like a coolant sensor it is an NTC, so a low voltage means hot. P041A is its general circuit code. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – GM and Ford report sensor B as P041B to P041D – so the description follows CARB's requirement to check input circuits for continuity and range. A substitute value is used and the EGR cooler check is suspended.

description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR temperature sensor B is the second temperature sensor in the EGR path; on GM diesels it sits before the cooler, on Ford diesels after it. P041E means its signal jumps. GM's diesels of 2016–18, the only documented users, set it when the measured resistance changes by more than 25 Ω between two samples 100 ms apart – faster than any real temperature change, so a loose contact or cracked sensor is the cause (40 of 50 samples, MIL after two trips). Dependent checks such as EGR cooler efficiency are then suspended.
possible_causes: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector [HIGH]
Harness chafed or broken (heat at the EGR pipe) [MEDIUM]
Sensor cracked internally (thermal cycling) [MEDIUM]
Engine module or ground connection [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 30€ - 250€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

AGR-Temperatursensor B ist der zweite Temperatursensor im AGR-Pfad; bei GM-Dieseln sitzt er vor dem Kühler, bei Ford-Dieseln danach. P041E heißt, sein Signal springt. GMs Diesel von 2016–18, die einzigen belegten Nutzer, setzen ihn, wenn sich der gemessene Widerstand zwischen zwei Abtastungen im Abstand von 100 ms um mehr als 25 Ω ändert – schneller als jede echte Temperaturänderung, Ursache ist also ein Wackelkontakt oder ein gerissener Sensor (40 von 50 Proben, Kontrollleuchte nach zwei Fahrten). Abhängige Prüfungen wie der AGR-Kühlerwirkungsgrad ruhen dann.

description: After a cold start the secondary air pump blows fresh air into the exhaust; switching valve A is the electrically driven valve that opens this path. GM checks the valve circuit in three codes – P0412 open, P041F shorted to ground, P044F shorted to positive – while other makers use P0413/P0414 or P0412 for everything. P041F means the control circuit is shorted to ground: GM checks with the driver switched off and sets the code at 0.5 Ω or less to ground (20 of 25 samples of 250 ms, above 11 V, MIL after two trips). The valve is then energised and open although not commanded; P0411 or P2440 may follow.
possible_causes: Control wire chafed against ground [HIGH]
Water or corrosion in the valve connector [MEDIUM]
Valve coil shorted to its housing [MEDIUM]
Driver in the engine module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 30€ - 300€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

Das Ventil ist dann bestromt und offen, obwohl es nicht angesteuert wird; P0411 oder P2440 können folgen.

description: The engine module checks whether the catalyst of bank 1 still converts enough. On petrol engines it estimates the oxygen storage capacity by comparing the sensors before and after the catalyst – a good catalyst smooths the rear signal. GM uses a test on overrun (ratio below 0.35 sets the code on the first trip), Ford an index ratio above 0.75 or fuel integration after fuel cut-off. On diesels P0420 concerns the oxidation catalyst, checked by its heat release during filter regeneration (GM Duramax LML, Ford below 45 % of the expected heat). Ford names oil-borne poisoning as the most common cause.

Diesel: oxidation catalyst sooted or poisoned, post-injection faulty [MEDIUM]

description: Catalyst 1 is the first catalyst in the flow direction of bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1) – the close-coupled or warm-up catalyst that lights off first after a cold start; the older wording was Warm Up Catalyst. description: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of a support catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start (Emitec EMICAT, 12–48 V); it was tried on Californian petrol cars in the 1990s and is used today mainly on diesels, for example Audi's 3.0 TDI from 2014 and 48-volt diesel vans. P0423 means the heated catalyst of bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1) no longer converts enough; CARB requires it to be assessed like any other catalyst. The only manufacturer reference is two Ram software bulletins for the 6.7-litre Cummins HO (model years 2025/26), which list P0423 without saying which part is meant.

description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P042E means the position-controlled EGR valve A is more open than commanded and cannot be closed. GM's diesels of 2016/17 set it when the valve stays too far open despite maximum closing duty (about 1–8 s); the 2018 tables check after switch-off whether it is below 5 % within 2 s – both with MIL on the first trip. Ford petrol engines compare the position with limits for 4 s, Ford diesels a deviation above 15 % for 25 s. Too much EGR causes rough idle, stalling and smoke; EGR control is switched off.

bilingual_title.en: EGR A Control Stuck Open

bilingual_description.en: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P042E means the position-controlled EGR valve A is more open than commanded and cannot be closed. GM's diesels of 2016/17 set it when the valve stays too far open despite maximum closing duty (about 1–8 s); the 2018 tables check after switch-off whether it is below 5 % within 2 s – both with MIL on the first trip. Ford petrol engines compare the position with limits for 4 s, Ford diesels a deviation above 15 % for 25 s. Too much EGR causes rough idle, stalling and smoke; EGR control is switched off.

GMs Diesel von 2016/17 setzen ihn, wenn das Ventil trotz maximalem Schließtastgrad zu weit offen bleibt (etwa 1–8 s); die Tabellen von 2018 prüfen nach dem Abstellen, ob es binnen 2 s unter 5 % fällt – beide mit Kontrollleuchte in der ersten Fahrt. Ford-Benziner vergleichen die Lage 4 s lang mit Grenzen, Ford-Diesel eine Abweichung über 15 % für 25 s. Zu viel AGR verursacht unrunden Leerlauf, Absterben und Rauch; die AGR-Regelung wird abgeschaltet.

No manufacturer document available to us uses this code.

description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Systems with a leak detection pump (Bosch DM-TL at VW, Audi, BMW and Maserati, Denso's canister pump module at Toyota/Lexus) first measure a reference value with the pump working only through a built-in 0.5 mm (0.020 in) orifice; it is the yardstick for the small-leak test that CARB requires. P043E means the reference measurement shows too little flow – the vacuum (or with DM-TL the pressure and pump current) becomes stronger than expected, so the orifice or reference path is partly blocked, often by dirt or liquid after overfilling. Leak detection pump faulty (weak or blocking pump, changeover valve stuck) [MEDIUM]
Engine module software (false detection) [LOW]
Pump connector or supply (voltage dip) [LOW]

description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P043F means the reference measurement shows too much flow – the reference vacuum or pressure does not reach the expected value, because the reference path or changeover valve leaks, the pump is weak, or air enters through leaking valves in the test path. The leak test can then not be judged, since a weak yardstick would hide leaks. GM and Ford do not use the code.

bilingual_description.en: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0443 is the electrical check of purge valve A, which the module switches to ground in pulses; it compares the driver's feedback voltage with the commanded state. GM uses it for an open circuit (200 kΩ or more, 20 of 25 samples, MIL after two trips) and reports shorts as P0458/P0459; Ford covers open and short in P0443 (5 s). description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor C is depends on the maker: on Ford petrol engines from 2020 it is the DPFE sensor, which measures the pressure drop across an orifice in the EGR pipe (sensor A there is the valve position sensor); GM diesels assign it to the position sensor of a low-pressure EGR valve, but only within fault groups. P044A is the general circuit fault of this sensor. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – Ford splits it into P044C/P044D – so the description follows CARB's requirement to check input circuits for continuity and range. Without the sensor, EGR flow and cooler checks are suspended.
possible_causes: Connector or wire to sensor C open or corroded [HIGH]
Sensor faulty [MEDIUM]
5 V reference or ground disturbed (with other sensor codes) [MEDIUM]
Engine module [LOW]

Was AGR-Sensor C ist, legt der Hersteller fest: Bei Ford-Benzinern ab 2020 ist es der DPFE-Sensor, der den Druckabfall an einer Blende im AGR-Rohr misst (Sensor A ist dort der Lagesensor des Ventils); GM-Diesel ordnen ihn dem Lagesensor eines Niederdruck-AGR-Ventils zu, allerdings nur in Fehlergruppen. description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. symptoms: Check engine light on, may come and go

description: After a cold start the secondary air pump blows fresh air into the exhaust; switching valve A is the electrically driven valve that opens this path. GM checks the valve circuit in three codes – P0412 open, P041F shorted to ground, P044F shorted to positive – while other makers use P0413/P0414 or P0412 for everything. P044F means the control circuit is shorted to positive or the coil is low-resistance: when the driver switches on, the line stays high. GM sets the code at 0.5 Ω or less to the supply (20 of 25 samples of 250 ms, above 11 V, MIL after two trips). The valve then does not open, secondary air is missing and P0411 may follow.

Control wire chafed against a supply wire [MEDIUM]
Water in the connector bridging to the supply [MEDIUM]
Driver in the engine module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 30€ - 300€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The tank pressure sensor measures small pressures around ambient for the leak tests. Its direction differs by maker – on GM vacuum raises the voltage, on Ford and Bosch pressure does – so low and high refer to the signal voltage only. P0450 is the general circuit fault of tank pressure sensor A; makers that separate the fault use P0452 or P0453. Only Audi (2022/23) is documented with the code, as an electrical fault of the tank ventilation pressure sensor; GM, Ford and Saab do not use it. The leak tests are then suspended.

Engine module software [LOW]

description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR B is a second EGR valve next to valve A – on diesels with two EGR circuits the low-pressure valve, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor. GM's diesels of 2016–18 and FCA's 2.2-litre diesel in the Jeep Wrangler use it. P045A is the general electrical fault in the drive circuit of valve B, typically an open circuit (for valve A GM uses 200 kΩ or more). GM lists this code among those that switch off the low-pressure EGR position control, but publishes no thresholds for it; the description follows the comparable valve A checks and CARB, which requires output circuits to be monitored. Low-pressure EGR is then switched off.

Driver in the engine module [LOW]

description: The fuel level sensor is a float on a resistor track in the tank unit. It is no emission part, but other monitors depend on it – the EVAP leak tests, for example, need at least 15 % fuel – so CARB requires it to be monitored and the usual exemption from the warning lamp does not apply. P0460 is the general circuit code for sensor A, the main or only fuel level sensor. Ford sets it instead of P0462/P0463 below 5 Ω or above 200 Ω for 30 s and until about 2012 also used it for a stuck sensor (fuel use compared over 100–120 miles); Saab's Trionic T8 uses it for a sensor that does not change. GM does not use P0460. The gauge then shows wrong values or a substitute, and level-dependent monitors do not run.
possible_causes: Resistor track worn or float arm sticking [HIGH]
Wire or connector at the tank unit open or shorted (corrosion) [MEDIUM]
Instrument cluster or gateway sends a wrong value (if the level comes via the bus) [LOW]
Frequent topping up or overfilling (plausibility test fails without a defect) [LOW]

bilingual_description.en: The fuel level sensor is a float on a resistor track in the tank unit. It is no emission part, but other monitors depend on it – the EVAP leak tests, for example, need at least 15 % fuel – so CARB requires it to be monitored and the usual exemption from the warning lamp does not apply. P0461 is the plausibility check of sensor A within its valid signal range. GM compares the level change with calculated fuel use: less than 3 l change after 22 l (2018) or 38.2 l (2016) consumed sets the code, MIL after two trips. Ford reads it differently, as a noisy signal with jumps above 40 %. On the Saab 9-4X the gauge then drops to empty and the low-fuel lamp comes on. A GM bulletin names overfilling and frequent topping up as a false trigger.
bilingual_description.de: Der Tankgeber ist ein Schwimmer auf einer Widerstandsbahn in der Tankeinheit. Er ist kein Abgasbauteil, aber andere Monitore hängen von ihm ab – die EVAP-Lecktests brauchen zum Beispiel mindestens 15 % Füllstand –, deshalb verlangt CARB seine Überwachung, und die übliche Ausnahme von der Kontrollleuchte greift nicht. P0461 ist die Plausibilitätsprüfung von Geber A im gültigen Signalbereich. GM vergleicht die Füllstandsänderung mit dem berechneten Verbrauch: Weniger als 3 l Änderung nach 22 l (2018) bzw. 38,2 l (2016) Verbrauch setzen den Code, Kontrollleuchte nach zwei Fahrten. Ford deutet ihn anders, als verrauschtes Signal mit Sprüngen über 40 %. Beim Saab 9-4X fällt die Anzeige dann auf leer, und die Reserveleuchte geht an. Ein GM-Bulletin nennt Überfüllen und häufiges Nachtanken als Fehlauslöser.

symptoms: Fuel gauge wrong, stuck or jumping
Range display and low-fuel warning wrong
Check engine light (depending on the maker)

description: The fuel level sensor is a float on a resistor track in the tank unit. It is no emission part, but other monitors depend on it – the EVAP leak tests, for example, need at least 15 % fuel – so CARB requires it to be monitored and the usual exemption from the warning lamp does not apply. Low and high refer to the signal, not the fuel level: on GM a full tank is about 40 Ω and a low voltage, while Ford judges the resistance directly. P0462 means the signal is below its lower limit: GM below 10 % of the 5 V reference (100 of 125 samples, MIL after two trips), Saab 9-4X below 0.25 V for 5 s, Ford a resistance below 5 Ω for 30 s. Typical is a signal wire shorted to ground or a shorted sensor. The gauge sticks at one end and a substitute value is used.
possible_causes: Signal wire shorted to ground (chafed at tank or underbody) [HIGH]
Sensor shorted or damaged internally [MEDIUM]
Water or corrosion in the tank connector [MEDIUM]
Evaluating module faulty [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 600€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: The fuel level sensor is a float on a resistor track in the tank unit. It is no emission part, but other monitors depend on it – the EVAP leak tests, for example, need at least 15 % fuel – so CARB requires it to be monitored and the usual exemption from the warning lamp does not apply. At GM, P0464 is a by-product of the engine-off EVAP leak test: a jump in fuel level with the vent valve closed counts as possible refuelling and aborts the test; if a following check finds no real refuelling, the jump is counted as an intermittent sensor signal (change above 10 % not stable for 30 s, 2 of 3 samples). GM sets the code with MIL on the first trip, because otherwise the leak monitor would be defeated permanently. Ford does not use P0464 and reports jumps as P0461.
possible_causes: Loose contact or corrosion at the tank connector or sensor terminal [HIGH]
Worn spots on the resistor track (wiper skipping) [HIGH]
Chafed wire with intermittent contact [MEDIUM]
Car parked on a steep slope or fuel sloshing after switch-off [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 600€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

symptoms: Check engine light on (GM after one trip)

description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. A purge flow sensor – a heated thermistor in the purge line between purge valve and intake manifold, as described in a Ford patent – measures purge flow directly for the CARB purge monitor. Today indirect methods (fuel trim, tank vacuum) have largely replaced it; no manufacturer document available to us uses these codes. P0465 is the general circuit fault of the sensor (heater supply, signal or ground), which CARB requires to be checked continuously. The purge flow monitor can then not be evaluated.
possible_causes: Connector or wire at the purge flow sensor [HIGH]
Sensor (heater or thermistor) faulty [MEDIUM]
Engine module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 30€ - 250€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_title.en: EVAP Purge Flow Sensor Circuit

bilingual_description.en: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. A purge flow sensor – a heated thermistor in the purge line between purge valve and intake manifold, as described in a Ford patent – measures purge flow directly for the CARB purge monitor. Today indirect methods (fuel trim, tank vacuum) have largely replaced it; no manufacturer document available to us uses these codes. P0465 is the general circuit fault of the sensor (heater supply, signal or ground), which CARB requires to be checked continuously. The purge flow monitor can then not be evaluated.
bilingual_description.de: Die Tankentlüftung (EVAP) speichert Kraftstoffdampf aus dem Tank in einem Aktivkohlebehälter; ein Spülventil lässt den Motor ihn absaugen, und ein Belüftungsventil öffnet den Behälter zur Frischluft. Ein Spülstromsensor – ein beheizter Thermistor in der Spülleitung zwischen Spülventil und Saugrohr, wie ein Ford-Patent ihn beschreibt – misst den Spülstrom für den CARB-Spülmonitor direkt. Heute haben indirekte Verfahren (Gemischadaption, Tankunterdruck) ihn weitgehend ersetzt; keine uns vorliegende Herstellerunterlage nutzt diese Codes. P0465 ist der allgemeine Kreisfehler des Sensors (Heizversorgung, Signal oder Masse), den CARB fortlaufend zu prüfen verlangt. Der Spülstrommonitor lässt sich dann nicht auswerten.

symptoms: EVAP readiness not set, emission inspection not passed

description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. A purge flow sensor – a heated thermistor in the purge line between purge valve and intake manifold, as described in a Ford patent – measures purge flow directly for the CARB purge monitor. Today indirect methods (fuel trim, tank vacuum) have largely replaced it; no manufacturer document available to us uses these codes. P0466 means the signal does not fit the purge valve state – the Ford patent judges the voltage difference between 100 % and 0 % purge duty against a calibrated value. The purge flow monitor can then not be evaluated.
possible_causes: Sensor dirty or sluggish (charcoal dust, fuel deposits) [HIGH]
Purge line blocked or purge valve sticking [MEDIUM]
Hose leaking ahead of the sensor [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 30€ - 250€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: Some engines measure the catalyst temperature with sensors instead of only modelling it. P046A compares catalyst temperature sensors 1 and 2 of bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1): both are electrically valid, but their readings do not match – for example they differ after a long stop, or the difference does not fit the operating state. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; FCA's EcoDiesel has only one such sensor per bank, and most makers handle exhaust temperature sensors and their correlation under EGT codes such as P0544 ff or P24C2. The description follows CARB's plausibility requirement for input components.
possible_causes: One of the two sensors drifting (soot on the tip, ageing) [HIGH]
Sensors fitted or connected the wrong way round [MEDIUM]
Contact resistance at one sensor's connector [MEDIUM]
Exhaust leak between the sensors [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 80€ - 400€ (0.5h - 2h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

Die Beschreibung folgt der CARB-Vorgabe zur Plausibilität von Eingangsbauteilen.

description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Which part EGR sensors A and B are depends on the maker: sensor A is usually the position sensor of EGR valve A; GM's Duramax diesels of 2017/18 use sensor B for the coolant temperature sensor at the inlet of the high-pressure EGR cooler, FCA for the position sensor of the low-pressure valve. P046C means the signal of sensor A is electrically valid but implausible. GM's diesels (6.6-litre Duramax LML and others from 2014) set it when the actual valve position deviates from the target by 5 % or more for 8 s, with offset learning completed and at least 11 V (MIL after two trips). Ford uses P0405/P0406/P046D for sensor A instead. EGR is then switched off or limited.
possible_causes: EGR valve coked and stiff, actual position does not follow [HIGH]
Position sensor worn or offset shifted [MEDIUM]
Contact resistance at connector or 5 V supply [MEDIUM]
Values not relearned after valve replacement [LOW]

description: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure. P0470 is the general circuit fault of sensor A. Ford's 6.7-litre diesel with a digital SENT sensor sets it when the sensor reports an error status or its raw data leave their limits for 5 s; a loss of communication is U0691 instead. description: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure. P0471 is the plausibility check of sensor A. Ford diesels compare it with ambient pressure with the engine off (at least 10 s stopped); a deviation above 15 kPa sets the code, including a sensor stuck mid-range. Ford petrol engines check it during the EGR monitor. FCA notes for Cummins diesels that P0471 often comes from real back pressure of a clogged particulate filter – then the sensor must not be replaced. Ford bulletins cover a sensor replacement on the 2.7 EcoBoost and coked sensing tubes on the 6.0 diesel.

Sensing tube or hose blocked or coked [HIGH]
Real high back pressure from a clogged particulate filter or catalyst [MEDIUM]
Leaking sensing tube or exhaust leak ahead of the sensor [LOW]

description: The exhaust pressure control valve is a flap in the exhaust: on older Navistar/Ford diesels a warm-up flap that raises back pressure when cold, on Ram and others an exhaust brake, on VW's 2.0 TDI a flap that drives the low-pressure EGR, and on Audi and Bentley a sound flap. On the Navistar warm-up flap, a patent describes control to a target back pressure with the exhaust pressure sensor as feedback.

Bei der Navistar-Warmlaufklappe regelt das Steuergerät mit dem Sensor als Rückmeldung auf einen Sollgegendruck, ausbleibender Druck trotz Ansteuerung ist also ein Funktionsfehler. Einziger codegenauer Beleg ist Ducatis Motorrad Diavel V4 (2023): fehlerhafte Bewegung des Klappenmotors durch eine falsch sitzende Zughalterung, mit Kontrollleuchte und Drehmomentbegrenzung bis Zündung aus.

symptoms: Flap without function: sound unchanged, rattling
Diesel: longer warm-up, exhaust brake weak or EGR faults

description: The exhaust pressure control valve is a flap in the exhaust: on older Navistar/Ford diesels a warm-up flap that raises back pressure when cold, on Ram and others an exhaust brake, on VW's 2.0 TDI a flap that drives the low-pressure EGR, and on Audi and Bentley a sound flap. P0477 means the control circuit of valve A is low. Audi uses it for a short to ground of the exhaust flap. VW's 2.0 TDI of 2009–12 sets it together with P047F, P048A–P048C and P0401 when salt has corroded the flap shaft and the flap sticks – a blocked motor can cause overcurrent or a voltage drop; on the 2015 engine it appears with P0478/P0475 and the actuator is replaced.
possible_causes: Control wire shorted to ground [HIGH]
Flap actuator faulty internally [HIGH]
Flap seized by corrosion (motor blocked) [MEDIUM]
Chafed wire at the underbody [MEDIUM]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 150€ - 900€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure. No manufacturer document available to us uses sensor B – it would be a second sensor, for example on bank 2 of a twin-turbo engine; the description mirrors sensor A. P047A is the general circuit fault of sensor B, comparable to P0470 for sensor A (a sensor error status or raw values out of limits).
possible_causes: Sensor faulty internally [HIGH]
Connector corroded or heat-damaged near the manifold [MEDIUM]

description: The engine module switches the radiator fan either through a relay, whose coil it pulls to ground, or with a PWM signal to a fan control module. The circuit is an output that CARB requires to be checked continuously. P0480 concerns the control circuit of fan 1. GM sets it for an open circuit – 200 kΩ or more with the driver off, 50 of 63 samples, above 11 V, MIL after two trips – and reports a short to ground or positive as P0691/P0692; Saab models on GM technology set it after 5 s (relay) or 1 s (PWM). FCA bulletins also name it with the warning lamp. Ford's OBD summaries do not contain the code. If the fan stops, the engine can overheat in traffic and the air conditioning weakens at standstill.
possible_causes: Fan relay (coil open) or fan control module faulty [HIGH]
Connector at fan or relay corroded, water ingress or pin pushed out [HIGH]
Control wire open or shorted to ground [MEDIUM]
Fan motor or fan assembly faulty [MEDIUM]
Driver in the engine module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 20€ - 600€ (0.3h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

symptoms: One fan stage or fan not working, or running constantly

description: The engine module switches cooling fan stages through relays, pulling each relay coil to ground. P0482 concerns the control circuit of the third stage or relay: with the driver off the line should sit at battery voltage through the coil, and the internal pull-up level means an open circuit (Saab ME9: more than 1 s, 10–18 V, engine running). On the GM-based Saab 9-5 of 2011 it is relay 3 (medium stage) of a two-fan network, with shorts reported as P0695/P0696. GM tables list P0482 only in fault groups; Ford's OBD summaries do not contain it. One fan stage then fails.

Control wire open or high-resistance, corroded or backed-out pins [HIGH]
Relay coil supply missing (fuse, supply wire) [MEDIUM]
Driver in the engine module [LOW]

symptoms: One fan stage fails – temperature rises in traffic or when towing

description: Two kinds of cooling fan carry these codes: electric fans switched by relays or driven by a PWM/LIN fan module with speed feedback, and engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch, whose speed a Hall sensor reports – GM calls them EV fans, meaning electro-viscous, not electric vehicle. P0483 checks the fan's function, not its circuit. With a speed sensor (GM viscous fans) commanded and actual speed are compared: GM's Duramax diesels of 2014–18 set it at more than ±500 rpm for at least 120 s, GM petrol SUVs and pick-ups of 2004–06 at more than 1000 rpm – MIL after two trips. Without a sensor Subaru (and the Saab 9-2X) judges indirectly: if coolant at 100 °C or more does not fall within 5 minutes at idle with the fan on, the code sets after two trips. Ford's OBD summaries do not contain it.

Electric fan motor stiff or worn, or fan blocked [MEDIUM]
Fan speed sensor or wiring giving a wrong value [MEDIUM]
Radiator or condenser clogged, coolant low (Subaru logic) [LOW]
Drive belt slipping (belt-driven viscous fan) [LOW]

Air conditioning weak at low speed

description: P0484 monitors the current drawn in the fan's load circuit: if it exceeds a threshold – blocked or stiff motor, shorted turns, a short in the load circuit – the code sets. This is only possible where the fan runs on a current-measuring semiconductor driver or fan module; plain relay circuits do not measure load current. Supplier patents (Bosch and others) describe current limiting or switch-off after a few seconds of overcurrent, ignoring the inrush current. No manufacturer table available to us lists P0484, so thresholds and warning-lamp behaviour remain open; CARB requires output components to be monitored.
possible_causes: Fan motor stiff (bearing damage) or blocked (foreign object, ice, bent blade) [HIGH]
Shorted turns or worn brushes in the fan motor [MEDIUM]
Short in the load circuit (pinched or chafed wire) [MEDIUM]
Fan control module faulty (wrong current measurement) [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 120€ - 700€ (0.8h - 3h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

symptoms: Fan does not run, runs only briefly or at reduced power
Humming or grinding at the fan, possibly blown fan fuse

description: P0485 monitors the supply or ground path of the fan or its control module – not the control line. It is typical of fans with their own module (PWM or LIN), which can report undervoltage or a missing ground. The high currents involved, often 20–60 A, make contact resistance at ground and supply connections and fuse holders the main cause. No manufacturer table available to us lists P0485, so thresholds and warning-lamp behaviour remain open; CARB requires output components to be monitored. The fan then runs intermittently or not at all.
possible_causes: Fan or fan module ground loose, corroded or broken [HIGH]
Fan fuse blown or fuse holder overheated or corroded [HIGH]
Relay power contact burnt – voltage drop under load [MEDIUM]
Connector at the fan scorched, water ingress [MEDIUM]
Fan control module faulty [LOW]

symptoms: Fan does not run or only intermittently
Overheating at standstill, weak air conditioning
Possibly burnt smell or discoloured connector

description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Which part EGR sensor B is depends on the maker: FCA uses it for the position sensor of the low-pressure EGR valve, GM's Duramax diesels for the coolant temperature sensor at the EGR cooler inlet. P0486 is its general circuit fault without a low or high assignment. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – makers report sensor B as P0407/P0408, P046E and P046F – so the description follows CARB's input component rules. EGR is then switched off or uses a substitute value.
possible_causes: Connector or harness to sensor B corroded or open (heat at the exhaust) [HIGH]
Sensor B faulty [MEDIUM]
5 V reference or ground disturbed [LOW]
Engine module or software [LOW]

Welches Bauteil AGR-Sensor B ist, legt der Hersteller fest: FCA nutzt ihn für den Lagesensor des Niederdruck-AGR-Ventils, GMs Duramax-Diesel für den Kühlmittel-Temperatursensor am Eintritt des AGR-Kühlers. Die AGR wird dann abgeschaltet oder nutzt einen Ersatzwert.

symptoms: EGR switched off, usually no noticeable change

description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. The EGR throttle is a regulating flap ahead of the intake manifold on diesels: by closing partly it lowers manifold pressure below exhaust back pressure so that enough exhaust is recirculated, and it also helps filter regeneration and shuts off air at engine stop. It is usually a DC motor with position sensor. GM and Ford report this flap under P02E0 ff; no manufacturer document available to us uses this code. P0487 means its drive circuit is open or has a general circuit fault, detected by the output stage. The flap then stays open, so the EGR rate cannot be raised enough and filter regeneration may be blocked.
possible_causes: Connector at the flap corroded or loose, wire open [HIGH]
Flap actuator motor faulty (winding open) [MEDIUM]
Pneumatic version: vacuum converter faulty [LOW]
Driver in the engine module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 80€ - 500€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

Die AGR-Drosselklappe ist bei Dieseln eine Regelklappe vor dem Saugrohr: Halb geschlossen senkt sie den Saugrohrdruck unter den Abgasgegendruck, damit genug Abgas zurückgeführt wird; außerdem hilft sie bei der Filterregeneration und sperrt beim Abstellen die Luft. symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode possible
Shaking when the engine is switched off

description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. It is usually a DC motor with position sensor. GM and Ford report this flap under P02E0 ff; no manufacturer document available to us uses this code. P0488 is its function check: the actual position reported by the sensor deviates from the target for too long, or the position signal is implausible – typically a coked, stiff flap or a broken gear. The flap then goes to its rest position or the engine enters limp mode, and the EGR rate cannot be controlled.

Actuator gear or motor worn or broken [MEDIUM]

Corrosion on flap or housing [LOW]

symptoms: Rough idle or stalling if the valve stays open

description: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2. Documented uses are the flap behind the particulate filter of VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI, which raises back pressure for the low-pressure EGR, and the sound flaps of Audi and Bentley. P048A means valve A is commanded open but its position feedback stays closed. On VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI of 2009–13 water and road salt corrode the shaft of the low-pressure EGR flap so it sticks; the code appears with P047F, P0477, P048B/P048C and P0401. The bulletins advise removing the flap and checking it moves freely, otherwise replacing it; improved parts were introduced. A closed flap keeps back pressure high.
possible_causes: Flap or flap shaft corroded or coked (stiff) [HIGH]
Flap actuator (motor or gear) faulty or too weak [MEDIUM]
Linkage between actuator and flap broken or misadjusted [LOW]
Position sensor reports wrongly [LOW]

description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0490 means the drive circuit of EGR valve A is shorted to battery voltage, or its output stage sees overcurrent. GM's Duramax LML sets it at 0.5 Ω or less to the supply for 3 s, GM's 2017 diesels at an H-bridge current above 8 A (160 of 200 samples), Ford diesels after 0.35 s – MIL after two trips. The output stage switches off for protection and the valve falls into its spring position, closed; EGR is off.

EGR valve with shorted turns (low resistance, overcurrent) [MEDIUM]
Moisture in the connector [MEDIUM]
Driver in the engine module [LOW]

description: After a cold start the secondary air pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; CARB requires the air flow to be monitored per bank. P0491 means too little air reaches bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1). VW and Audi calculate the injected air mass per bank from the front oxygen sensor's reaction during the cold-start phase; an Audi bulletin names values of 0.4–0.7 on both banks as too little together, often from coked air passages in the cylinder head. On VW/Audi V engines each bank has its own combination valve with a shared pump. Ford assigns the code to the bank 1 secondary air monitor; GM uses P0411 instead.
possible_causes: Secondary air passages in the cylinder head coked [HIGH]
Combination valve stuck or stiff [HIGH]
Vacuum supply or changeover valve leaking, valve closes too early [MEDIUM]
Secondary air pump weak or water in the pump [MEDIUM]
Hose between pump and valve leaking or off [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 100€ - 900€ (0.5h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: Two kinds of cooling fan carry these codes: electric fans switched by relays or driven by a PWM/LIN fan module with speed feedback, and engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch, whose speed a Hall sensor reports – GM calls them EV fans, meaning electro-viscous, not electric vehicle. P0493 is documented only on GM petrol engines of 2004–06 with a viscous fan: the measured fan speed exceeds a limit that is hardly physically possible (about 6400 rpm), so it is effectively a plausibility check of the speed signal or a seized clutch at high engine speed. Two counts set it, with the warning lamp on the first trip – unlike P0495, which needs two trips. Ford, FCA and GM from 2014 were not found to use it.
possible_causes: Viscous clutch seized – fan runs rigidly with the belt drive [HIGH]
Interference or faulty signal from the fan speed sensor [MEDIUM]
Clutch solenoid or its control stuck at fully engaged [MEDIUM]
Engine module or software [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 150€ - 600€ (1h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0496 means vapour flows into the intake although the module is not purging – usually a purge valve that leaks or sticks open. GM and Saab seal the system after a cold start with the engine running; if tank vacuum exceeds 2491 Pa for 5 s, the code sets (fuel 10–90 %, MIL after two trips). Ford, which replaced its old code P1450 with P0496, also sets it for excessive vacuum during the leak test, for example with a vent valve stuck closed. Hard starting right after refuelling is typical.

bilingual_title.en: EVAP System High Purge Flow

bilingual_description.en: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0496 means vapour flows into the intake although the module is not purging – usually a purge valve that leaks or sticks open. GM and Saab seal the system after a cold start with the engine running; if tank vacuum exceeds 2491 Pa for 5 s, the code sets (fuel 10–90 %, MIL after two trips). Ford, which replaced its old code P1450 with P0496, also sets it for excessive vacuum during the leak test, for example with a vent valve stuck closed. Hard starting right after refuelling is typical.
bilingual_description.de: Die Tankentlüftung (EVAP) speichert Kraftstoffdampf aus dem Tank in einem Aktivkohlebehälter; ein Spülventil lässt den Motor ihn absaugen, und ein Belüftungsventil öffnet den Behälter zur Frischluft. P0496 heißt, Dampf strömt in den Ansaugtrakt, obwohl das Steuergerät nicht spült – meist ein undichtes oder offen klemmendes Spülventil. GM und Saab dichten das System nach einem Kaltstart bei laufendem Motor ab; steigt der Tankunterdruck 5 s lang über 2491 Pa, setzt der Code (Füllstand 10–90 %, Kontrollleuchte nach zwei Fahrten). Ford, das seinen alten Code P1450 durch P0496 ersetzt hat, setzt ihn auch bei zu starkem Unterdruck im Lecktest, etwa bei zuhängendem Belüftungsventil. Typisch ist ein schwerer Start direkt nach dem Tanken.

description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The vent valve is normally open and switched to ground by the module; P0449 (open), P0498 and P0499 form the newer code scheme for its circuit, used mainly by GM and Saab models with GM engines, while Ford uses P0446. Corrosion or water in the connector [MEDIUM]
Driver in the engine module [LOW]

description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Circuit B is the second EGR path; on diesels with two circuits it is the low-pressure EGR, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor (GM diesels 2016–18, FCA's 2.2 and 3.0 diesels). P049A is the general flow fault of circuit B, used where the module does not separate too little from too much; CARB requires low and high flow to be detected, mostly by comparing air mass, manifold pressure or lambda with a model. No manufacturer document available to us uses P049A – GM has only position and actuator codes for its low-pressure EGR, FCA uses P049B. Low-pressure EGR is then switched off.
possible_causes: Low-pressure EGR valve sooted or sticking [HIGH]
Low-pressure EGR cooler or line blocked or leaking [MEDIUM]
Flap creating the pressure difference faulty [MEDIUM]
Sensors (air mass, pressure difference, position sensor B) implausible [MEDIUM]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 150€ - 1500€ (1h - 5h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_description.de: Die Abgasrückführung (AGR) leitet einen Teil des Abgases zurück in den Ansaugtrakt, um Verbrennungstemperatur und Stickoxide zu senken. Kreis B ist der zweite AGR-Weg; bei Dieseln mit zwei Kreisen die Niederdruck-AGR, die Abgas hinter dem Partikelfilter entnimmt und vor dem Turbo-Verdichter einleitet (GM-Diesel 2016–18, FCAs 2,2- und 3,0-Liter-Diesel). P049A ist der allgemeine Durchflussfehler von Kreis B, genutzt, wenn das Steuergerät nicht zwischen zu wenig und zu viel trennt; CARB verlangt, zu geringen und zu hohen Durchfluss zu erkennen, meist durch Vergleich von Luftmasse, Saugrohrdruck oder Lambda mit einem Modell. Keine uns vorliegende Herstellerunterlage nutzt P049A – GM hat für seine Niederdruck-AGR nur Lage- und Stellercodes, FCA nutzt P049B. Die Niederdruck-AGR wird dann abgeschaltet.

description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P049B means too little flow in circuit B: with the low-pressure valve open the module expects a change in fresh air mass or manifold pressure, or a modelled EGR volume, and the actual flow stays below the threshold. FCA documents it on the 3.0-litre EcoDiesel third generation in the 2020 Ram 1500, partly as a false trigger fixed by a software update; thresholds are not published.

Implausible sensors (air mass, pressure difference) [LOW]

description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P049D checks the learned zero point – the fully closed position – of EGR valve A. The module learns the position sensor voltage with the valve closed, at GM during the after-run following ignition off; if the learned value lies outside a window (GM 2018: 83.5–93.5 % of 5 V, GM 2016: 16.4–25.1 %) or the values scatter too much (GM Duramax LML above 30 %), the code sets – MIL after two trips at GM, immediately after learning at Ford. Usually soot at the seat keeps the valve from closing, or a new valve was not taught in.
possible_causes: Soot or deposits at the valve seat, valve does not close fully [HIGH]
Position sensor A faulty or characteristic shifted [MEDIUM]
New or cleaned valve not taught in, or wrong part [MEDIUM]
Position sensor circuit fault as the primary cause [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 0€ - 800€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve B is the second such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2. Documented uses are the flap behind the particulate filter of VW's and Audi's 2.0 TDI, which raises back pressure for the low-pressure EGR, and the sound flaps of Audi and Bentley. P049F is the general electrical fault of valve B. Audi uses it for sound flap 2 (2017–21, mostly sporadic, with P0475/P0477); on Bentley's Bentayga a commutator short in the flap motor caused by sludge triggers it – if the flap moves freely by hand, the actuator is replaced, otherwise the silencer or pipe.
possible_causes: Flap actuator faulty (commutator short) [HIGH]
Wire or connector at the actuator damaged [MEDIUM]
Control wire open [MEDIUM]
Driver in the engine module [LOW]

description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Purge valve B is a second electric purge valve, usually for the high-load purge line of a turbo engine, which purges to the compressor inlet when there is boost in the manifold (Ford patent). Many makers solve this path with one purge valve and passive check valves instead – Ford tests it as P04F0 – and then have no valve B. CARB requires every purge path to be checked. P04AB means the control circuit of purge valve B is open; the high-load path then does not purge. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB and the comparable purge valve A checks (for GM P0443/P0458/P0459).

Coil of purge valve B open [MEDIUM]
Supply (fuse, main relay) or control wire open [MEDIUM]
Driver in the engine module [LOW]

description: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Plug-in hybrids and range extenders with a sealed, pressurised tank have an electric valve in the vapour line between tank and canister. It is normally closed and opens before refuelling, so that the tank is depressurised – the filler flap is only released then – and refuelling vapour reaches the canister (Ford patent). P04B0 means the valve's control circuit is open. The valve then does not open, the tank cannot be depressurised and the filler flap may not open or only after a delay. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – Ford reports its tank isolation valve as P2418/P2450 – so the description follows CARB and the component patent.
possible_causes: Connector at the tank valve (tank, underbody) loose or corroded [HIGH]
Valve coil open [MEDIUM]
Supply or control wire open [MEDIUM]
Driver in the control module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 400€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_description.de: Die Tankentlüftung (EVAP) speichert Kraftstoffdampf aus dem Tank in einem Aktivkohlebehälter; ein Spülventil lässt den Motor ihn absaugen, und ein Belüftungsventil öffnet den Behälter zur Frischluft. Plug-in-Hybride und Range-Extender mit abgedichtetem Drucktank haben ein elektrisches Ventil in der Dampfleitung zwischen Tank und Aktivkohlebehälter. Es ist normal geschlossen und öffnet vor dem Tanken, damit der Tank drucklos wird – erst dann wird die Tankklappe freigegeben – und die Betankungsdämpfe in den Behälter gelangen (Ford-Patent). P04B3 ist die Funktionsprüfung: Bei geschlossen befohlenem Ventil dürfen Tank und Behälter ihren Druck nicht ausgleichen; folgt der Tankdruck dem Behälter, etwa beim Spülen oder im Lecktest, klemmt das Ventil offen. Ford prüft sein vergleichbares Tank-Absperrventil unter P2450 über das Druckverhältnis zwischen Tank und Behälter. Die Tagesverdunstung belastet dann den Behälter, den Hybride mit wenig Motorlaufzeit nicht genug spülen können. Keine uns vorliegende Herstellerunterlage nutzt diesen Code – Ford meldet sein Tank-Absperrventil als P2418/P2450 –, die Beschreibung folgt deshalb CARB und dem Bauteilpatent.

description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. The code standard allows up to four EGR temperature sensors, A to D – for example before and after the cooler, or in the high- and low-pressure circuits; which is which depends on the maker. Sensor C is the third of them, usually an NTC whose low voltage means hot. P04CE is its general circuit fault, without separating low and high. FCA lists sensor C codes for its part 68142905A (Ram 2014 6.4 and 3.0 litre, Jeep and Dodge 3.6 Pentastar 2016) together with P040B, P0401 and P2457. Thresholds are not published. Without a valid temperature the EGR flow model is wrong, so the module uses a substitute value or switches EGR off.
possible_causes: Open or poor contact in signal or ground line [HIGH]
Connector or wire at the sensor corroded or worn by heat and vibration [HIGH]
Sensor faulty (element broken or sooted) [MEDIUM]
Engine module input [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 60€ - 300€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_description.de: Die Abgasrückführung (AGR) leitet einen Teil des Abgases zurück in den Ansaugtrakt, um Verbrennungstemperatur und Stickoxide zu senken. Die Code-Norm sieht bis zu vier AGR-Temperatursensoren A bis D vor – etwa vor und nach dem Kühler oder im Hoch- und Niederdruckkreis; welcher welcher ist, legt der Hersteller fest. Sensor C ist der dritte davon, meist ein NTC, dessen niedrige Spannung heiß bedeutet. P04CE ist sein allgemeiner Kreisfehler, ohne Trennung nach zu niedrig und zu hoch. FCA führt Codes zu Sensor C für sein Teil 68142905A (Ram 2014 6,4 und 3,0 Liter, Jeep und Dodge 3.6 Pentastar 2016), zusammen mit P040B, P0401 und P2457. Schwellen werden nicht veröffentlicht. Ohne gültige Temperatur stimmt das AGR-Durchflussmodell nicht, das Steuergerät nutzt dann einen Ersatzwert oder schaltet die AGR ab.

symptoms: Usually no change in driving (EGR on a substitute value or off)
Possibly EGR flow or cooler codes (P0401, P2457)

description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. The code standard allows up to four EGR temperature sensors, A to D – for example before and after the cooler, or in the high- and low-pressure circuits; which is which depends on the maker. Sensor C is the third of them, usually an NTC whose low voltage means hot. P04CF is its plausibility check: the signal is electrically valid but does not fit the model or other temperatures. Comparable checks on sensors A and B compare it after a long stop with coolant and intake air, or look for a temperature change during EGR operation (Ford diesels, GM diesels above 10 °C). No manufacturer document available to us uses P04CF; FCA lists P040B as the range code for its sensor C part.
possible_causes: Sensor drifting or sluggish (soot, ageing) [HIGH]
Contact resistance at the connector [MEDIUM]
EGR cooler or valve problem changes the real temperature [MEDIUM]
Comparison sensor (coolant, intake air, exhaust) faulty [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 60€ - 300€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: The exhaust brake input is the driver's request for the exhaust or engine brake – a button or stalk on diesel pick-ups and trucks. On GM's 6.6-litre L5P, for example, the button must be pressed again after every start. GM uses the exhaust brake status as an enable condition for other emission monitors, which is why CARB requires the input to be checked. No manufacturer table available to us lists P04D3–P04D7; Hino's J08E truck engine checks P04D5 before its exhaust brake function test. P04D3 is the general circuit fault of the request input, used where the module cannot resolve the fault type further – an open circuit or, on bus-connected buttons, an invalid message.
possible_causes: Exhaust brake button faulty (contact, lighting board) [HIGH]
Open wire or connector between button and module [MEDIUM]

description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Where EGR is closed-loop controlled – on flow, valve position or pressure difference – CARB requires the control to start within a time set by the maker after starting; otherwise a fault is due, and P04D8 is that code. Typical prerequisites are coolant or cooler temperature, valid sensors and an operating range; Ford diesels, for example, run their EGR monitors only with EGR in closed loop. No manufacturer document available to us uses P04D8 – many monitor the inputs individually instead, as CARB permits.
possible_causes: Engine reaches release temperature too late (thermostat stuck open, very short trips, cold weather) [HIGH]
Faulty input sensor blocks the release (EGR temperature, air mass, position) [MEDIUM]
EGR valve or actuator not ready (stuck, learned value missing) [MEDIUM]
Software or calibration [LOW]

bilingual_description.de: Die Abgasrückführung (AGR) leitet einen Teil des Abgases zurück in den Ansaugtrakt, um Verbrennungstemperatur und Stickoxide zu senken. description: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P04D9 means the EGR control has used up its authority and still gets too little flow – CARB requires this to be detected. Ford's 6.7-litre diesel sets it when the desired minus the measured EGR rate stays above 50 points for 20 s. Volvo cars from 2022 also set it after long low-load driving and fix it with a software update and an activation drive; a Mack/Volvo truck bulletin traces it to wrong EGR temperature readings from worn connector contacts.

description: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) system routes blow-by gas from the crankcase into the intake; CARB requires a disconnection between crankcase and intake to be detected. GM's 2.0-litre LSY has a pressure sensor in the PCV hose: with the hose connected it must see a pressure drop that grows with air flow, plus pressure pulses from the pistons. Ford reports the same sensor type as crankcase pressure sensor A (P051A ff). P04DB means a disconnection: without the pressure drop the clean-air side is off, without the pulses the crankcase side. GM's LSY uses the product of normalised offset and noise (below 0.63 kPa², MIL after two trips); Ford's EcoBoost checks the dirty side at cranking and the clean side above 5 lb/min of air. Engines without such a sensor may report a disconnection through mixture or load codes, as CARB allows. FCA bulletins cover it on the Alfa Romeo 2.0 turbo and the Ram 3.0 EcoDiesel.
possible_causes: Ventilation hose off or quick connector not latched (often after intake work) [HIGH]
Hose cracked or porous, or nipple broken [HIGH]
PCV valve stuck closed or oil separator blocked or frozen (simulates a disconnection) [MEDIUM]
Pressure sensor in the hose giving a wrong signal [LOW]

GMs 2,0-Liter-LSY hat einen Drucksensor im Entlüftungsschlauch: Bei angeschlossenem Schlauch muss er einen mit dem Luftdurchsatz wachsenden Druckabfall sehen und dazu Druckpulse der Kolben. Ford meldet denselben Sensortyp als Kurbelgehäusedrucksensor A (P051A ff). P04DB heißt, es gibt eine Trennung: Fehlt der Druckabfall, ist die Reinluftseite ab, fehlen die Pulse, die Kurbelgehäuseseite. GMs LSY nutzt das Produkt aus normiertem Versatz und Rauschen (unter 0,63 kPa², Kontrollleuchte nach zwei Fahrten); Fords EcoBoost prüft die Schmutzseite beim Anlassen und die Reinluftseite ab 5 lb/min Luftdurchsatz. description: Plug-in and some full hybrids keep the fuel tank sealed while driving, separated from the charcoal canister by a valve. When the driver presses the fuel button, the system opens the valve, lets the pressure escape into the canister and only then unlocks the filler door. A switch reports whether the door is open or closed, so that the tank can be sealed again afterwards. P04DC means the door switch signal is electrically valid but implausible. A GM patent detects refuelling from a rising fuel level at standstill with low tank pressure; if the switch reported open for less than about 20 s, or closed for too long, it is faulty. A Ford patent sets a fault if the fuel level rose and the car drove off without the switch ever reporting open – the valve then stays open and the driver is warned. If the door state is unknown, the system leaves the tank open to the canister as a precaution and suspends the leak tests. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules and patents for the door switch.
possible_causes: Switch mechanically jammed or misadjusted (reports one state permanently) [HIGH]
Door or actuator damaged or missing [MEDIUM]
Signal or connector fault with a valid but wrong level [MEDIUM]
Fuel level sensor faulty (refuelling misdetected) [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 30€ - 250€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.
