bilingual_description.de: Moderne Diesel-Glühanlagen schalten jede Glühkerze über einen eigenen Leistungshalbleiter (im Glüh- oder Motorsteuergerät), sodass Strom und Fehler je Kerze messbar sind; ein fehlerhafter Kanal wird abgeschaltet. CARB verlangt, Glühkerzen auf korrekten Strom und Spannungsabfall zu prüfen und seit Modelljahr 2010 schon eine einzelne Kerze außerhalb der Spezifikation zu erkennen und zu benennen. P069A heißt: Der Kreis zur Glühkerze von Zylinder 9 hat Masseschluss oder zieht Überstrom. GMs Endstufen im Motorsteuergerät melden eine Impedanz gegen Masse unter 0,11 Ω (10 von 20 Proben) mit Motorkontroll- und Vorglühleuchte nach zwei Fahrten; Fords Power Stroke 2023 prüft beim Glühen auf mehr als 22 A für 0,3 s oder 20–22 A für 2 s. Der Kanal wird abgeschaltet, Kerze 9 glüht nicht mehr – schwerere Kaltstarts und weißer Rauch folgen. Keine uns vorliegende Herstellerunterlage nutzt diesen Code für Zylinder ab 9; die Beschreibung folgt den Zylindern 1–8.

description: P069E is not a component fault but a notice in the engine module: the separate fuel pump control module has detected and stored an emission-related fault of its own and requests the check engine light – over serial data or, on older systems, a request line. GM uses it (2014–2019 tables) and lists P069E itself as 'type A, no MIL': the lamp is lit because of the fault in the pump module, not because of P069E. The actual cause must therefore be read from the fuel pump module's own memory – typically pump circuit, fuel pressure sensor, module overheating or supply. On GM diesels (2014) this module also controls the active grille shutters. Clear the code only after repairing the module's fault.
possible_causes: Fault in the fuel pump circuit (pump, wiring, ground) stored in the pump module [HIGH]
Fuel pressure sensor or its wiring or 5 V reference [MEDIUM]
Pump module faulty internally or overheated (corrosion, moisture) [MEDIUM]
Insufficient supply or ground of the pump module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 800€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_description.de: P069E ist kein Bauteilfehler, sondern ein Hinweis im Motorsteuergerät: Das eigene Kraftstoffpumpen-Steuergerät hat selbst einen abgasrelevanten Fehler erkannt, gespeichert und fordert die Motorkontrollleuchte an – über serielle Daten oder bei älteren Systemen über eine Anforderungsleitung. GM nutzt ihn (Tabellen 2014–2019) und führt P069E selbst als „Typ A, ohne MIL“: Die Leuchte brennt wegen des Fehlers im Pumpen-Steuergerät, nicht wegen P069E. Die eigentliche Ursache steht daher im Fehlerspeicher des Pumpen-Steuergeräts – typisch Pumpenkreis, Kraftstoffdrucksensor, Überhitzung des Moduls oder Versorgung. Bei GM-Dieseln (2014) steuert dieses Modul auch die aktive Kühlerjalousie. Den Code erst nach Behebung des Modulfehlers löschen.

description: P069F concerns the hard-wired control circuit of the electronic throttle warning lamp (called 'reduced power', wrench or EPC lamp depending on the maker), which lights when the throttle control detects a fault and limits power. Das Steuergerät überwacht diesen Ausgang elektrisch auf Unterbrechung und Kurzschluss; ob die Leuchte brennt, sieht es nicht. description: Variable-displacement A/C compressors change their swash-plate stroke via an electric control valve: a PWM current sets the crankcase pressure and thus the output. Where the engine module drives this valve (Ford's 'EVDC' compressors 2013–2019), it monitors the circuit; where the climate control module drives it (Hyundai, VW/Audi, GM), faults appear in that module instead. CARB requires monitoring only where the A/C affects engine control. P06A0 is the general circuit fault of the compressor control valve. Ford's service messages for its EVDC compressors (2013–2019) describe it with weak or no cooling, typically from a valve with an open coil or a corroded connector at the compressor; low refrigerant can also mislead the diagnosis. The compressor then runs at minimum stroke or does not cool. Not emission relevant in most cases.
possible_causes: Compressor control valve faulty (coil open) [HIGH]
Connector at the compressor corroded or loose, wire open [HIGH]
Low or incorrect refrigerant charge misleading the diagnosis [MEDIUM]
Engine module driver faulty [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 30€ - 900€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: The engine module feeds sensors from several regulated 5 V reference circuits; a short at one sensor pulls the whole circuit down, so all its sensors report at once – unplug them one by one to find the culprit. On GM engines (2016–2025) circuit D feeds pedal sensor 1 and both throttle position sensors, on the Saab 9-4X the throttle and pedal sensor 1 – a fault therefore usually means electronic throttle limp mode. P06A3 is the general code for circuit D. GM's petrol engines (2016–2025) and 2018 diesels use it as the only code for this circuit (4.875–5.125 V, lamp in the first trip); the 2014 6.6 L LML used 4.6 V or less for 1 s with two trips. Saab's 9-3 (2012) also reports it.
possible_causes: Short in the wire or sensor of a connected sensor [HIGH]
Chafing or water in harness or connector [MEDIUM]
A connected sensor faulty internally [MEDIUM]
Module internal voltage regulator [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 80€ - 600€ (1h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: GM uses P06AF for a cross-check between two control modules: the monitored module (engine or transmission module, each with main and secondary processor) sends a fixed answer sequence over CAN only if both its processors work together correctly; the monitoring module (engine, transmission or hybrid control module) sets P06AF if the pattern is wrong or missing. In all GM tables from 2016 to 2025 it is type A – lamp in the first trip – and the torque management may shut the engine down for safety. Typical causes are processor or software faults in one of the modules, communication problems or supply interruptions. Look for further processor codes (P0606, P060A, P060B) and software bulletins. No other manufacturer document available to us uses P06AF.
possible_causes: Software fault in engine, transmission or hybrid module [HIGH]
Processor fault in one of the modules [MEDIUM]
CAN communication disturbance between the modules [MEDIUM]
Supply interruption or poor ground of a module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 100€ - 1500€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: Despite the similar name, 'sensor power supply' is not the 5 V sensor reference (P0641 ff). It is documented in GM hybrid drive motor control modules: a 15 V supply that excites the motor position sensor (resolver) and powers the gate drivers of the inverter transistors, kept separate from the 5 V reference and the 12 V supply. In GM's 2008 Two-Mode hybrid, A and B are the two motor control modules. P06B0 is the general or open-circuit code of supply A. Only Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander bulletin lists this code (as a main code with low/high sub-codes), without thresholds or sensor assignment. Low and high are P06B1/P06B2; GM documents those with thresholds. Check fuses and feeds of the motor control module first.

Internal supply circuit of the motor control module faulty [MEDIUM]
Connector or wiring fault [MEDIUM]
Short in a supplied component (resolver, gate driver) [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 100€ - 1500€ (1h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

It is documented in GM hybrid drive motor control modules: a 15 V supply that excites the motor position sensor (resolver) and powers the gate drivers of the inverter transistors, kept separate from the 5 V reference and the 12 V supply. In GM's 2008 Two-Mode hybrid, A and B are the two motor control modules. P06B4 means supply B, in the second motor control module, is too low: GM's 2008 Two-Mode hybrid flags below 12.0 V for 365 ms after two trips. Blown fuses, shorts in supplied components or an internal fault are typical. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander lists it as a sub-code.
bilingual_description.de: Trotz des ähnlichen Namens ist „Sensor Power Supply“ nicht die 5-V-Sensorreferenz (P0641 ff). Belegt ist sie in den E-Motor-Steuergeräten von GM-Hybriden: eine 15-V-Versorgung, die den Lagegeber des E-Motors (Resolver) erregt und die Gate-Treiber der Wechselrichter-Transistoren speist, getrennt von 5-V-Referenz und 12-V-Versorgung. Im Two-Mode-Hybrid von GM (2008) sind A und B die beiden Motorsteuergeräte. P06B4 heißt: Versorgung B im zweiten Motorsteuergerät ist zu niedrig. GMs Two-Mode-Hybrid von 2008 meldet unter 12,0 V für 365 ms nach zwei Fahrten. Typisch sind durchgebrannte Sicherungen, Kurzschlüsse in versorgten Bauteilen oder ein interner Fehler. Mitsubishis Outlander 2022 führt ihn als Untercode.

description: To detect an open knock sensor circuit, GM's engine modules feed a 20 kHz test signal into the sensor circuit and check whether it returns. P06B6 checks the internal test circuit or knock signal processor for sensor 1: it sets when the returned 20 kHz component lies between the open-circuit thresholds, so the module cannot decide 'connected' or 'open'. GM rates it type B (two trips), type A in some 2025 modules; Saab retards ignition timing as a reaction. GM bulletin 22-NA-229 calls for reprogramming only, not part replacement. Ford uses P06B6 for lost communication with its knock chip (more than 200 cylinder events). Knock sensor circuit codes are P0325–P0328.
possible_causes: Engine module software (GM bulletin) [HIGH]
Internal knock processor or test circuit faulty [MEDIUM]
Knock sensor wiring with high resistance or intermittent contact [MEDIUM]
Knock sensor faulty [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 0€ - 1200€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_title.en: Internal Control Module Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Processor 1 Performance

bilingual_description.en: To detect an open knock sensor circuit, GM's engine modules feed a 20 kHz test signal into the sensor circuit and check whether it returns. P06B6 checks the internal test circuit or knock signal processor for sensor 1: it sets when the returned 20 kHz component lies between the open-circuit thresholds, so the module cannot decide 'connected' or 'open'. GM rates it type B (two trips), type A in some 2025 modules; Saab retards ignition timing as a reaction. GM bulletin 22-NA-229 calls for reprogramming only, not part replacement. Ford uses P06B6 for lost communication with its knock chip (more than 200 cylinder events). Knock sensor circuit codes are P0325–P0328.
bilingual_description.de: Um eine Unterbrechung im Klopfsensorkreis zu erkennen, speisen GMs Motorsteuergeräte ein 20-kHz-Testsignal in den Sensorkreis ein und prüfen, ob es zurückkommt. P06B6 prüft den internen Testkreis bzw. den Klopfsignal-Prozessor für Sensor 1: Er setzt, wenn der zurückgekommene 20-kHz-Anteil zwischen den Schwellen für „verbunden“ und „offen“ liegt, das Steuergerät also nicht entscheiden kann. GM stuft ihn als Typ B (zwei Fahrten) ein, in manchen Steuergeräten von 2025 als Typ A; Saab nimmt als Reaktion den Zündzeitpunkt zurück. Das GM-Bulletin 22-NA-229 verlangt nur Neuprogrammieren, keinen Teiletausch. Ford nutzt P06B6 für verlorene Kommunikation mit seinem Klopfbaustein (mehr als 200 Zylinderereignisse). Kreiscodes der Klopfsensoren sind P0325–P0328.

symptoms: Retarded ignition, less power and higher consumption

description: Non-volatile RAM keeps its content without power; among other things it stores the permanent fault codes CARB requires, which cannot be cleared with a scan tool. Ford sets P06B8 when the checksum of this permanent-code memory is wrong; a common companion is P068A (main relay dropped out too early, memory write incomplete). Ford's commercial and propane variants list it with or without the check engine light depending on the vehicle; Ford's 2023 diesel table misprints it as 'P068B'. GM and Saab do not use P06B8. Typical causes are interrupted shutdowns (battery disconnected, voltage dips), software faults and, rarely, a memory defect. After a software check, clearing and an ignition cycle with normal shutdown often resolve it.
possible_causes: Interrupted shutdown (battery disconnected, voltage dip, main relay too early) [HIGH]
Engine module software [MEDIUM]
Weak battery or poor ground [MEDIUM]
Memory defect in the module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 0€ - 1200€ (0.3h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_title.en: Internal Control Module Non-Volatile Random Access Memory (NVRAM) Error

bilingual_description.en: Non-volatile RAM keeps its content without power; among other things it stores the permanent fault codes CARB requires, which cannot be cleared with a scan tool. Ford sets P06B8 when the checksum of this permanent-code memory is wrong; a common companion is P068A (main relay dropped out too early, memory write incomplete). Ford's commercial and propane variants list it with or without the check engine light depending on the vehicle; Ford's 2023 diesel table misprints it as 'P068B'. GM and Saab do not use P06B8. Typical causes are interrupted shutdowns (battery disconnected, voltage dips), software faults and, rarely, a memory defect. After a software check, clearing and an ignition cycle with normal shutdown often resolve it.
bilingual_description.de: Nichtflüchtiger Arbeitsspeicher (NVRAM) behält seinen Inhalt ohne Spannung; darin liegen unter anderem die von CARB verlangten permanenten Fehlercodes, die sich per Diagnosegerät nicht löschen lassen. Ford setzt P06B8, wenn die Prüfsumme dieses Speichers für permanente Codes nicht stimmt; häufiger Begleiter ist P068A (Hauptrelais zu früh abgefallen, Speichern unvollständig). Fords Nutzfahrzeug- und Propanvarianten führen ihn je nach Fahrzeug mit oder ohne Motorkontrollleuchte; die Diesel-Tabelle 2023 verschreibt ihn als „P068B“. GM und Saab nutzen P06B8 nicht. Typische Ursachen sind unterbrochenes Abschalten (Batterie abgeklemmt, Spannungseinbrüche), Softwarefehler und selten ein Speicherdefekt. Nach einer Softwareprüfung helfen oft Löschen und ein Zündzyklus mit normalem Abschalten.

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the vehicle)

description: The glow module calculates each plug's resistance from voltage and current while glowing. 'Range/performance' means the circuit is electrically intact but the resistance or current lies outside the specified window – typically an aged, high-resistance or wrong plug or contact resistance at the connector. CARB requires a single plug outside specification to be detected from model year 2010. Ford's 2023 6.7 L/3.0 L Power Stroke runs this check during heating after the open and short checks and flags a circuit above 2 Ω after about 3 s. GM does not use this code family. Ram's 6.7 L Cummins (from model year 2025, with glow plugs instead of the grid heater) set these codes falsely; the fix was reprogramming the engine module. On the 2014–15 Ram ProMaster 3.0 L diesel, plugs without an inner O-ring caused it; all plugs were replaced.
possible_causes: Glow plug cylinder 1 aged or high-resistance [HIGH]
Contact resistance at plug connector or terminal nut [MEDIUM]
Wrong plug type or a plug with a manufacturing fault [MEDIUM]
Engine or glow module software (Ram 6.7 L from 2025) [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 500€ (0.5h - 3h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

bilingual_title.en: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Circuit Range/Performance

bilingual_description.en: The glow module calculates each plug's resistance from voltage and current while glowing. 'Range/performance' means the circuit is electrically intact but the resistance or current lies outside the specified window – typically an aged, high-resistance or wrong plug or contact resistance at the connector. CARB requires a single plug outside specification to be detected from model year 2010. Ford's 2023 6.7 L/3.0 L Power Stroke runs this check during heating after the open and short checks and flags a circuit above 2 Ω after about 3 s. GM does not use this code family. Ram's 6.7 L Cummins (from model year 2025, with glow plugs instead of the grid heater) set these codes falsely; the fix was reprogramming the engine module. On the 2014–15 Ram ProMaster 3.0 L diesel, plugs without an inner O-ring caused it; all plugs were replaced.
bilingual_description.de: Das Glühsteuergerät berechnet beim Glühen aus Spannung und Strom den Widerstand jeder Kerze. „Bereich/Funktion“ heißt: Der Kreis ist elektrisch intakt, aber Widerstand oder Strom liegen außerhalb des Sollfensters – typisch eine gealterte, hochohmige oder falsche Kerze oder ein Übergangswiderstand am Stecker. CARB verlangt ab Modelljahr 2010, schon eine einzelne Kerze außerhalb der Spezifikation zu erkennen. Fords Power Stroke 6,7 l/3,0 l von 2023 prüft das beim Glühen nach den Unterbrechungs- und Kurzschlussprüfungen und meldet einen Kreis über 2 Ω nach etwa 3 s. GM nutzt diese Codefamilie nicht. Rams 6,7-l-Cummins (ab Modelljahr 2025, mit Glühkerzen statt Heizgitter) setzte diese Codes fälschlich; Abhilfe war das Neuprogrammieren des Motorsteuergeräts. Beim Ram ProMaster 3.0 l Diesel 2014–15 waren Kerzen ohne inneren O-Ring die Ursache; alle Kerzen wurden getauscht.

symptoms: Check engine and glow plug lamp
Rough running and white smoke after a cold start

description: A glow plug has no identification; the control unit recognises its type only from its electrical behaviour – cold resistance at switch-on and how resistance rises during heating (R = U/I). A Beru patent describes how steel and ceramic plugs are told apart this way so the right heating profile is used and a wrong or mixed type is reported. A low-voltage plug on an 11 V control burns out, an 11 V plug on a low-voltage control glows too weakly. GM uses 'incorrect' for any resistance outside the window: the 2025 diesels check 0.22–2.00 Ω (15 of 25 samples, two trips), the L5P glow module a ramp-dependent window. P06C5 reports this for cylinder 1. VW's 2.0 TDI (Jetta, Golf, Passat 2011–13) checks the type 2 s after ignition on – starting during that time caused false codes from the voltage dip, fixed with new glow module software.
possible_causes: Wrong glow plug type fitted in cylinder 1 (steel/ceramic, voltage rating) [HIGH]
Plug resistance drifted (ageing, damage) [MEDIUM]
Glow module software or check during cranking (false report) [MEDIUM]
Contact resistance at the plug connector [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 40€ - 500€ (0.5h - 3h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: On ignition systems where the coils are driven through a separate driver chip inside the engine module, P06D1 reports that this internal coil control does not work correctly. Ford checks the communication with the coil driver chip continuously and sets the code within 1 s at 200–3200 rpm, positive torque and 11–16 V. GM Europe's V6 (Saab 9-5 2.8 T) reports it as an internal engine module fault with the lamp after two trips. Misfires or rough running can follow if coils are no longer fired correctly. Primary circuit faults of individual coils are P0351–P0360, driver shorts P2300 ff. Check supply and ground, look for software updates; otherwise the module is the likely cause.
possible_causes: Coil driver chip or internal communication in the engine module faulty [HIGH]
Engine module software [MEDIUM]
Supply or ground problem at the module [MEDIUM]
Shorted coil overloading the driver [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 100€ - 1500€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_description.de: Bei Zündanlagen, deren Spulen über einen eigenen Treiberbaustein im Motorsteuergerät angesteuert werden, meldet P06D1, dass diese interne Spulenansteuerung nicht korrekt arbeitet. Ford prüft die Kommunikation mit dem Spulen-Treiberbaustein laufend und setzt den Code binnen 1 s bei 200–3200/min, positivem Moment und 11–16 V. GM-Europas V6 (Saab 9-5 2.8 T) meldet ihn als internen Fehler des Motorsteuergeräts mit Leuchte nach zwei Fahrten. Aussetzer oder unrunder Lauf können folgen, wenn Spulen nicht mehr richtig angesteuert werden. Primärkreisfehler einzelner Spulen sind P0351–P0360, Treiberkurzschlüsse P2300 ff. Versorgung und Masse prüfen, nach Software-Updates suchen; sonst ist das Steuergerät die wahrscheinliche Ursache.

description: The engine module feeds sensors from several regulated 5 V reference circuits; a short at one sensor pulls the whole circuit down and all its sensors report at once – unplug them one by one to find the culprit. description: A switchable or variable oil pump saves fuel by lowering its output at part load; a solenoid valve sets the stage. GM and Ford design it so the pump runs at full output, i.e. high pressure, when the valve is unpowered – the safe default – and at the low stage when powered. P06DA means the control circuit of this valve is open: it can no longer be powered, so the pump stays at high pressure. GM measures the voltage with the driver off and flags more than 200 kΩ after two trips; some GM modules set P06DB instead. GM checks the low-side driver at 11 V or more relay voltage over 40 of 50 samples (100 ms); Ford's smart driver reports output faults after 5 s with the battery at 11 V or more. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander uses the same code. The engine is not at risk, the pump just can no longer be regulated.
possible_causes: Connector at the control valve loose or corroded (often at the pump in the oil pan) [HIGH]
Valve coil open or valve broken [MEDIUM]
Supply (main relay) or control wire broken [MEDIUM]
Engine module software [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 60€ - 450€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: A switchable oil pump changes its output via a solenoid valve; unpowered it delivers high pressure. To test it, the module switches the pump between stages (GM up to 15 times, with oil at 50–110 °C and 1350–2500 rpm, expecting more than 100 kPa difference) and watches the oil pressure sensor; Ford checks each switch-over of a two-stage pump within 1 s, or a variable pump over 10 s, from 30 s after start. P06DD means the pressure does not react and stays above the threshold – the pump acts as if the valve were stuck off, at high pressure; GM sets it after two trips. Yet GM bulletins for V8 and 2.5 L engines list P06DD with low oil pressure, too: broken valve tips, unseated valves, a loose pump drive gear or worn tensioners also stop the pressure from changing. Check oil level and pressure before replacing parts.
possible_causes: Control valve stuck or broken, screen clogged [HIGH]
Oil level too low, wrong viscosity or sludge [MEDIUM]
Mechanical pump or drive damage (tensioner, drive gear, pump face) [MEDIUM]
Valve not seated correctly (retaining clip) [LOW]
Oil pressure sensor inaccurate [LOW]

description: A switchable oil pump changes its output via a solenoid valve; powered it runs at the low stage. To test it, the module switches the pump between stages (GM up to 15 times, with oil at 50–110 °C and 1350–2500 rpm, expecting more than 100 kPa difference) and watches the oil pressure sensor; Ford checks each switch-over of a two-stage pump within 1 s, or a variable pump over 10 s, from 30 s after start. P06DE is the counterpart of P06DD: the commanded high stage is not reached and the pressure stays below the threshold, as if the valve were stuck on. Too little oil pressure at high load endangers the engine, so GM sets it after just one trip; a Ford patent raises idle speed in this case. A short to ground on the control wire (P06DB) has the same effect electrically. An FCA bulletin for the 3.6 L V6 fixes false codes by software.
possible_causes: Control valve stuck in the powered position [HIGH]
Low oil level, diluted or sludged oil, aeration [MEDIUM]
Pump wear or internal leakage [MEDIUM]
Engine module software (FCA 3.6 L) [LOW]
Oil pressure sensor [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 100€ - 3500€ (1h - 12h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: A diesel glow plug control module has its own microcontroller. On power-up it forms a checksum over its memory and compares it with the stored value; P06DF means they differ, so the module's program or data cannot be trusted. Ford's 2023 6.7 L and 3.0 L Power Stroke list P06DF among the glow module checks, run at power-up and flagged on a RAM checksum mismatch after about 1 s. GM's L5P performs the same check on ROM (4.5 s, two trips) but reports it as P064C. CARB treats the module as a 'smart device' whose internal faults need not be pinpointed, so this is extra diagnosis by the manufacturer. The usual remedy is reprogramming or replacing the module; until then preheating may be missing.
possible_causes: Glow plug control module faulty internally (memory, controller) [HIGH]
Failed or interrupted programming of the module [MEDIUM]
Voltage dip or spike at power-up (weak battery, poor ground) [LOW]
Moisture or corrosion in module or connector [LOW]

description: Diesel glow systems switch each plug through its own power semiconductor and switch off a faulty channel; CARB requires single-plug detection from model year 2010. P06E0 means the circuit to the cylinder 11 glow plug is shorted to ground or draws overcurrent. For cylinders 1–8, GM's engine-module drivers flag below 0.11 Ω to ground after two trips, and Ford's 2023 Power Stroke more than 22 A for 0.3 s or 20–22 A for 2 s while heating. The channel is switched off and the plug stays cold; the other plugs keep working. An internally shorted plug or a chafed wire is the usual cause. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – it needs at least 11 cylinders, and the only US OBD II diesel above eight, VW's Touareg V10 TDI, has ten; the description follows cylinders 1–8.
possible_causes: Cylinder 11 glow plug shorted internally [HIGH]
Plug wire chafed through to ground [MEDIUM]
Burnt connector or terminal nut, tracking through oil or moisture [MEDIUM]
Driver stage in the glow module defective [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 80€ - 800€ (1h - 4h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: Control modules are woken by a dedicated wake-up line or a network wake-up – at ignition on, when a charging cable is plugged in, or on a timer for engine-off diagnostics and battery management. P06E4 means this wake-up signal is implausible: the module wakes too late or not at all, stays awake, or the line state does not match the network status. In practice the code appears mainly on hybrids: FCA fixes it on the Pacifica plug-in hybrid and the Wrangler 4xe with module software, where it remained as a permanent code that blocked emission inspections; GM's hybrid integration module lists it as a fault bundle. No manufacturer publishes thresholds or timing.
possible_causes: Module software (false setting, permanent code does not clear) [HIGH]
Wake-up line or connector open or shorted [MEDIUM]
Weak 12 V battery, voltage dips at wake-up [MEDIUM]
Engine or hybrid control module faulty [LOW]

P06E4 heißt: Dieses Aufwecksignal ist unplausibel – das Modul wacht zu spät oder gar nicht auf, bleibt wach, oder der Leitungszustand passt nicht zum Netzwerkstatus. In der Praxis tritt der Code vor allem bei Hybriden auf: FCA behebt ihn beim Pacifica Plug-in-Hybrid und beim Wrangler 4xe per Modulsoftware, wo er als Permanent-Code die Abgasuntersuchung blockierte; GMs Hybrid-Integrationsmodul führt ihn als Fehlerbündel. Schwellen oder Zeiten veröffentlicht kein Hersteller.

description: P06E5 means glow plug control module 1 does not respond correctly to the glow command: its outputs do not switch or its internal drivers report faults or overheating. Ford's 2023 6.7 L and 3.0 L Power Stroke list P06E5 among the glow module checks, run continuously, with a fault after about 1 s when internal drivers for glow plugs, DEF heaters or relays fail to switch or overheat for more than 1 s – Ford does not assign each threshold to a single code. GM files the same check under P064C: on the L5P a plug commanded on but drawing under 3.2 A with 0 V at the plug for 3.5 s, on the LML a total current under 6.6 A; both after two trips. The plugs then heat partly or not at all, with hard cold starts and white smoke. There is no limp mode.
possible_causes: Glow plug control module faulty internally (drivers do not switch) [HIGH]
Poor supply or ground of the module (main feed, fuse, ground) [MEDIUM]
Module overheating (mounting location, short at a plug) [MEDIUM]
Module software [LOW]

description: 'Sensor power supply' is a separate J2012 family next to the 5 V sensor reference (P0697 ff): an additional supply from the module for sensors or drivers – in GM hybrids a 15 V supply for resolvers and inverter gate drivers, there as supplies A and B. Supply C is a third such circuit. P06E6 is the general or open-circuit code of supply C: the module measures the output of its supply regulator and finds the voltage missing. Low and high are P06E7/P06E8. Only Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander lists P06E6 as a main code with sub-codes for low and high, called internal control module, without thresholds or the sensors fed. All sensors on the circuit then deliver invalid values, so several follow-up codes and limp mode are possible.

description: On cars with stop-start or keyless start the engine module operates the starter relay itself and watches the start: if cranking is commanded but the engine does not turn, turns too slowly or the start is aborted, it sets P06E9. description: A modern NOx sensor is a smart sensor: a ceramic sensing element with pump cells and heater plus its own control unit with a microcontroller, which regulates the pump currents, calculates NOx and oxygen and sends them to the engine module over CAN. P06EA means this control unit of sensor 1 (before the SCR catalyst) reports an internal fault – its self-tests of RAM and ROM or EEPROM checksums fail – so the electronics, not the sensing element, are at fault. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code: Ford's 2023 diesels run exactly these checks continuously, with a fault after 5 s, but report them as P2200; GM uses the P2200 family and U029D/U029E. The NOx value is then invalid, so SCR dosing runs on a model or stops, a warning appears and, depending on market, a countdown to a start lock.
possible_causes: Faulty electronics in the NOx sensor control unit [HIGH]
Moisture or corrosion in control unit or connector (underbody location) [MEDIUM]
Under- or overvoltage or dips in the sensor supply [MEDIUM]
Unsuitable replacement sensor or software [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 250€ - 900€ (0.5h - 1.5h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: P06EC is a notice code like P0700: a separate fuel injector control module has stored an emission-related fault of its own and asks the engine module over CAN to switch on the check engine light. The actual fault is stored in that module and must be read there; simple OBD readers show only P06EC. GM uses it on the 2019 Corvette ZR1, whose LT5 engine adds port injection driven by its own module with its own crank and cam inputs; the code runs continuously from key on and is listed as type A without its own MIL – the lamp comes from the module's fault. Older separate injector modules (Ford 6.0 L Power Stroke, GM bi-fuel CNG trucks) report through P0611 or U codes instead. Any limp mode follows the module's fault.
possible_causes: Emission-related fault in the injector control module or its injectors/sensors (code stored there) [HIGH]
Supply, ground or relay problem of the module [MEDIUM]
Internal module fault (memory, processor) [MEDIUM]
Software level of engine or injector module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 100€ - 1500€ (0.5h - 3h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: The engine module turns the crankshaft signal into a cleaned-up square wave for the tachometer, transmission or body-builder modules – Saab's 1999 9-3, for example, sends two pulses per revolution, about 30 Hz at idle. P06ED means this output is too low, typically shorted to ground, so it can no longer switch high. It is the counterpart of P0654 (open circuit) and P06EE (high). CARB requires output circuits to be checked; the signal is emission-relevant only if a receiving module uses it for emission functions. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB, the component and P0654. The tachometer then reads zero or jumps, and modules using the signal lose it, while the engine runs normally.
possible_causes: Speed output wire chafing against ground [HIGH]
Receiver (instrument, add-on device) shorted internally [MEDIUM]
Aftermarket tachometer or accessory wired wrongly [MEDIUM]
Engine module driver stage [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 40€ - 300€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: P06EF concerns the automatic restart after the system itself has stopped the engine – stop-start or hybrid. The restart, by starter, reinforced stop-start starter or belt starter-generator, takes too long or fails. CARB does not count such a commanded shutdown as a stall. description: Some SCR diesels have a separate reductant control module that drives the DEF pump, heaters and dosing valve – Ford calls it the pump motor controller (fault above 130 °C under P20FF), GM's L5P an SCR power module. It measures its own board temperature with an internal sensor to protect itself from heat. P06F0 is the general circuit fault of this internal sensor: the signal is missing, open or cannot be evaluated. Range, low and high are P06F1–P06F3; the DEF tank temperature sensor is a different part. No manufacturer document available to us uses P06F0–P06F3; Ford and GM report related faults under P20FF or own codes. Without a valid temperature the module limits or stops heaters and pump, so dosing is restricted and an SCR warning, up to a start lock countdown, may follow.
possible_causes: Reductant control module or pump unit faulty (sensor is on the board) [HIGH]
Water ingress or corrosion in the module (DEF crystals, underbody location) [MEDIUM]
Supply or ground problems at the module [MEDIUM]
Module software or calibration [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 400€ - 1800€ (1h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: When the engine module switches a lamp through its own wire, it checks the output driver electrically like other lamp outputs: with the lamp off the line must carry supply voltage, with it on nearly 0 V – GM's MIL driver, for example, flags an open circuit at 200 kΩ or more. It cannot see whether the bulb lights, and on cars that send the lamp command over CAN such faults appear as U codes. P06F4 concerns the indicator showing that stop-start is active or disabled; the code reports a fault in its control circuit. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; the description follows CARB's output check and other lamp circuits. Only the display is affected – the stop-start function itself has its own codes (P06E9, P06EF).

Engine module driver stage [LOW]

description: SAE J2012 provides a complete code family for a second glow plug control module, mirroring module 1 code for code. The description follows module 1 (P064C). The plugs fed by module 2 then heat poorly or not at all.

Module software or configuration [LOW]

description: 'Diesel intake air flow control' is the diesel's electric intake throttle with position sensor (P02E0 ff). During cold start many diesels close it partly: the extra load raises exhaust temperature so the catalysts light off sooner. CARB requires such cold start elements to be monitored, with their own codes separate from normal operation. P06FE means the throttle does not reach its target position while the cold start strategy is active – it is not the intake air heater. No manufacturer document available to us uses P06FE: GM's 2025 diesels run this check under P2957 (deviation above 16 % or 10 %, two trips), Ford's 2023 diesels under P02E4 in cold start mode. Cold start emissions rise; driveability usually stays normal.
possible_causes: Intake throttle coked with soot and oil (EGR, crankcase ventilation) [HIGH]
Throttle motor or gear stiff, position sensor faulty [MEDIUM]
Ice or condensate in the intake in frost [LOW]
Contact resistance in connector or wiring, low voltage [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 80€ - 700€ (0.5h - 2.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

symptoms: Check engine light, usually after two trips

description: When the engine module switches a lamp through its own wire, it checks the output driver electrically like other lamp outputs: with the lamp off the line must carry supply voltage, with it on nearly 0 V – GM's MIL driver, for example, flags an open circuit at 200 kΩ or more. It cannot see whether the bulb lights, and on cars that send the lamp command over CAN such faults appear as U codes. P06FF concerns an economy indicator such as an ECO lamp that the engine module switches directly; the code reports a fault in its control circuit. It should not be confused with a body electrics 'economy mode' that saves battery energy. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's output check and other lamp circuits. Driving is not affected.
possible_causes: Wire or connector to the lamp open or shorted [HIGH]
Lamp or instrument cluster faulty [MEDIUM]
Engine module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 30€ - 250€ (0.3h - 1.5h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: P0700 is a notice code: the separate transmission control module has stored an emission-related fault of its own and asks the engine module to switch on the check engine light. The actual fault – a sensor, solenoid, ratio or speed sensor code – is stored in the transmission module and must be read with a tool that can address it; simple OBD readers often show only P0700. GM's engine module reads the request message from 3 s after start; Subaru-based systems (Saab 9-2X) light the MIL at once and clear it after three fault-free cycles. Ford's engine modules with integrated transmission control do not use P0700. Any limp mode comes from the transmission fault, not from P0700.

possible_causes: Actual fault stored in the transmission module (sensor, solenoid, ratio, speed sensor) [HIGH]
Wrong transmission fluid level or condition causing slip or ratio codes [MEDIUM]
Harness or connector at the transmission corroded or damaged [MEDIUM]
Low system voltage or weak battery [LOW]
Transmission module or software faulty [LOW]

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly transmission warning
Depending on the transmission fault: limp mode, harsh or delayed shifts
Often no symptoms if the fault was intermittent
Simple OBD reader shows only P0700

description: P0701 means the transmission control system works outside its expected range or its function is implausible – without a circuit fault. What exactly is checked is up to the manufacturer; no GM, Ford, Saab or bulletin document available to us describes the strategy. The only manufacturer evidence is Ford's engine module list for 6.8 L E- and F-Series trucks, where P0701 is stored without the check engine light. Typically the control cannot plausibly achieve the requested gear, pressure or torque, and the transmission goes into limp mode. Individual components have their own codes (P0705 ff range sensor, P0715 ff speed sensors, P0750 ff solenoids).
possible_causes: Transmission control faulty internally or software [MEDIUM]
Implausible input signals (speed or range sensor) without own circuit fault [MEDIUM]
Wrong fluid level or quality – hydraulics do not respond [MEDIUM]
Harness or connector with contact resistance [LOW]

description: P0702 reports an electrical fault in the transmission control system as a whole – typically the supply of the transmission actuators (solenoid supply, transmission relay, supply switch in the module) or a circuit fault not assigned to a single component. No manufacturer document available to us describes it in detail; Ford's engine module list for 6.8 L E- and F-Series trucks stores it without the check engine light. If the solenoid supply is lost, transmissions usually fall back to a hydraulic limp gear. Individual solenoids have their own codes (P0750 ff); actuator supply is P0657 ff.

Harness or connector at transmission or module damaged, corroded or oil-soaked [MEDIUM]

Low or fluctuating system voltage [LOW]

description: Brake switch A is usually the brake light switch, B a second, redundant contact or signal used to cancel cruise control, release the converter clutch, check 'brake before throttle' and for stop-start. Since about 2014 GM receives it as a CAN message from the body module and checks its integrity (rolling counter, protection value: 3 of 10 faulty in 2014, 9 of 17 in 2025) without the check engine light; cruise control is disabled. Subaru-based systems (Saab 9-2X) check the circuit electrically during stops and starts and light the MIL after two trips. An NHTSA investigation of Hyundai and Kia brake light switches lists P0703 with a brake light that stays on. Brake switch A codes are P0571–P0573, disagreement between A and B is P0504.
possible_causes: Brake light or double switch worn, corroded or misadjusted [HIGH]
Wiring or connector at the pedal damaged, fuse blown [MEDIUM]
CAN message from the body module disturbed (GM: software, bus fault) [MEDIUM]
Aftermarket LED lamps or trailer module distorting the circuit [LOW]

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be engaged or drops out
Brake light stays on or does not work
Selector cannot be moved out of P (shift lock)
Check engine light depending on the maker

description: Only on cars with a clutch pedal: the clutch switch tells the engine module that the clutch is depressed, used to cancel cruise control, smooth load changes when shifting and for stop-start. The check is a plausibility test over driving events rather than a voltage check: Saab's Trionic T8 expects a change of state every time the car pulls away from 3 to 50 km/h (four misses in a row), the EDC16 diesel at gear changes (25 in a row, above 35 km/h and 1500 rpm), and Ford compares its two clutch switches continuously. None of them lights the check engine light; cruise control is disabled. Separate clutch pedal switch codes are P0830–P0835.

Connector or wiring at the pedal box damaged or corroded [MEDIUM]
Floor mat or pedal stop shifted, switch bracket broken [MEDIUM]
Driving style (pulling away or shifting without fully depressing the clutch) [LOW]

symptoms: Cruise control not working or not cancelling when declutching

description: The transmission range sensor (selector or multifunction switch, PRNDL) reports the selected range; it may be a multi-contact switch with a bit pattern per position, an analog sensor with two opposing voltages adding up to 5 V, or a contactless PWM sensor. Its second channel has its own codes (P2801–P2805). P0705 is the circuit or pattern fault: the module receives a combination that matches no valid position. Ford flags an invalid pattern after 5 s (digital sensor) or 200 ms (4-bit sensor), checking continuously with the check engine light; Saab's 9-5 (9600) detects an impossible combination of its four contacts and goes into limp mode with the gearbox warning. The transmission no longer knows the range reliably – limp mode, start interlock or reversing light may be affected. Check the harness for shorts to ground before replacing the sensor.

specific_definitions.AUDI: Defective Transmission Range Sensor (PRNDL input), Defective Transmission Range Sensor (PRNDL input) wiring or connector, Defective Valve Body, Defective manual shift valve linkage, Dirty transmission fluid that restricts the hydraulic passages

possible_causes: Range sensor worn, dirty or with oil or water ingress [HIGH]
Sensor misadjusted or selector cable out of adjustment [MEDIUM]
Harness or connector at the transmission damaged, short to ground [MEDIUM]
Transmission or engine module input faulty [LOW]

description: Fluid level sensors in the transmission sump (capacitive or voltage-based) report the oil level to the transmission module; measurements are only valid under defined conditions – an Allison patent names fluid temperature, vehicle at rest, low input speed and a tilt correction. Such sensors are mainly found in heavy automatic transmissions. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. P070A is the general circuit fault of this sensor (open or fault in the signal circuit). Because the oil level does not usually affect emissions directly, a rating without the check engine light is likely; expect a transmission warning or a missing level display. An actually low oil level is not a P070A fault. Range, low, high and intermittent are P070B–P070E; fluid temperature has its own codes (P0710 ff).

Transmission module input faulty [LOW]

Leaks at the pan gasket, seals or cooler lines and wrong filling after service are the usual causes.

description: The transmission fluid temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor whose resistance falls as the fluid warms; the module feeds it with 5 V through a resistor. description: P0711 means the fluid temperature signal is electrically valid but implausible. Manufacturers check three things: the fluid does not warm up as expected (GM 2025 still below 15 °C after the calibrated warm-up time, Saab's AF40 below 20 °C after 10 minutes of driving), the value is stuck (Ford: within ±2 °F for about 2.5 minutes below 70 or above 225 °F), or it jumps unrealistically. description: The input or turbine shaft speed sensor – a Hall sensor with square-wave output or an inductive sensor with sine output – reports the speed behind the torque converter. With output and engine speed it gives the actual gear ratio, converter slip and shift timing. P0715 is the general circuit code. Ford uses it for 'no signal' too: the vehicle is moving under power (engine above converter stall speed, output speed plausible) but the sensor reports under 200 rpm for 5–30 s; Ford's DPS6 dual-clutch sets it for a hardware-detected fault of input shaft sensor 1. Connector or harness corroded, chafed or loose pins (with internal sensors also the pass-through connector) [HIGH]

description: Brake switch B is the brake signal to the transmission module or a second brake switch channel, used to release the converter clutch, adapt shift strategy on grades and cancel cruise control. Low and high describe the signal voltage, and what that means depends on polarity: GM's converter clutch brake switch is closed at rest (12 V), while Saab's Trionic 8 sees 12 V when braking. Detection is always a plausibility check against driving: the brake reads applied during accelerations or never applied during decelerations. P0719 means the signal stays low. For GM that reads as brake applied: 2006 transmission modules flag it after eight accelerations without the brake releasing, without MIL. Saab's Trionic 8 flags the brake light signal not changing during four decelerations from 40 to 3 km/h and disables cruise control. The opposite is P0724.

bilingual_title.en: Brake Switch B Circuit Low

bilingual_description.en: Brake switch B is the brake signal to the transmission module or a second brake switch channel, used to release the converter clutch, adapt shift strategy on grades and cancel cruise control. Low and high describe the signal voltage, and what that means depends on polarity: GM's converter clutch brake switch is closed at rest (12 V), while Saab's Trionic 8 sees 12 V when braking. Detection is always a plausibility check against driving: the brake reads applied during accelerations or never applied during decelerations. P0719 means the signal stays low. For GM that reads as brake applied: 2006 transmission modules flag it after eight accelerations without the brake releasing, without MIL. Saab's Trionic 8 flags the brake light signal not changing during four decelerations from 40 to 3 km/h and disables cruise control. The opposite is P0724.

Erkannt wird immer über Plausibilität mit dem Fahrzustand: Bremse „an“ beim Beschleunigen oder nie „an“ beim Verzögern. P0719 heißt: Das Signal bleibt niedrig. Für GM heißt das Bremse betätigt: Getriebesteuergeräte von 2006 melden es nach acht Beschleunigungen ohne gelöste Bremse, ohne MIL. Saabs Trionic 8 meldet, wenn sich das Bremslichtsignal bei vier Verzögerungen von 40 auf 3 km/h nicht ändert, und schaltet den Tempomat ab. Das Gegenstück ist P0724.

description: The output shaft speed sensor (Hall or inductive) reports the speed of the transmission output; it gives the gear ratio together with input speed and on many vehicles also the road speed for speedometer and cruise control. P0720 is the general circuit code. Ford also uses it for 'no signal': while engine and turbine speed show the vehicle moving, the sensor reports under 100–200 rpm for 5–30 s; ZF's 6HP26 in Ford vehicles flags an open or short after 0.6 s. Subaru-based systems (Saab 9-2X) flag an impossible 255 km/h or 0 km/h while driving and light the MIL after two trips, substituting the other sensor. GM does not use P0720 but P0722. Speedometer and cruise control may fail, often with a vehicle speed code as well.

description: The output shaft speed sensor (Hall or inductive) reports the speed of the transmission output; it gives the gear ratio together with input speed and on many vehicles also the road speed for speedometer and cruise control. P0721 means the output speed is present but implausible: too high (Ford 6R80 above 7450 rpm), not matching wheel or input speed in the engaged gear (ZF 6HP26 more than 200 or 250 rpm apart, Ford's F21 more than 15 % for 10 s), or jumping (Allison 1000: 500 rpm within 0.15 s). Wrong tyre sizes or a faulty wheel speed sensor can also falsify the comparison.

bilingual_title.en: Brake Switch B Circuit High

bilingual_description.en: Brake switch B is the brake signal to the transmission module or a second brake switch channel, used to release the converter clutch, adapt shift strategy on grades and cancel cruise control. Low and high describe the signal voltage, and what that means depends on polarity: GM's converter clutch brake switch is closed at rest (12 V), while Saab's Trionic 8 sees 12 V when braking. Detection is always a plausibility check against driving: the brake reads applied during accelerations or never applied during decelerations. P0724 means the signal stays high. For GM that reads as brake never applied: 2006 transmission modules flag it after eight decelerations without a brake signal of at least 2 s, without MIL. Saab's Trionic 8 flags a brake light signal that reads on while accelerating from 3 to 40 km/h, four times, and disables cruise control. The opposite is P0719.
bilingual_description.de: Bremsschalter B ist das Bremssignal zum Getriebesteuergerät bzw. ein zweiter Bremsschalterkanal; er löst die Wandlerkupplung, passt die Schaltstrategie an Steigungen an und schaltet den Tempomat ab. Low und High beschreiben die Signalspannung, deren Bedeutung von der Polarität abhängt: GMs Bremsschalter für die Wandlerkupplung ist in Ruhe geschlossen (12 V), Saabs Trionic 8 sieht dagegen 12 V beim Bremsen. Erkannt wird immer über Plausibilität mit dem Fahrzustand: Bremse „an“ beim Beschleunigen oder nie „an“ beim Verzögern. P0724 heißt: Das Signal bleibt hoch. Für GM heißt das Bremse nie betätigt: Getriebesteuergeräte von 2006 melden es nach acht Verzögerungen ohne mindestens 2 s Bremssignal, ohne MIL. Saabs Trionic 8 meldet ein Bremslichtsignal, das beim Beschleunigen von 3 auf 40 km/h viermal „an“ zeigt, und schaltet den Tempomat ab. Das Gegenstück ist P0719.

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be activated or switches off
Unusual shifting, converter clutch behaviour changed
Brake lights stay off or on

description: The transmission module needs engine speed for converter slip, shift quality and to check the turbine speed. Today it almost always arrives over CAN from the engine module with a validity flag; only GM's 2007 Allison 1000 tables show a separate engine speed sensor read by the transmission module. P0725 is the general fault of this input; with CAN it means the engine module marks its speed value as invalid. Saab's Aisin transmissions and a 2006 GM table set it after about 4 s, the GM table with immediate MIL. A Saab bulletin notes that behind P0725 there is always a crankshaft or camshaft sensor code in the engine module (P0016, P0335–P0339) – so read the engine module first. Limp mode follows; a completely missing CAN message is U0100.
possible_causes: Crankshaft or camshaft sensor fault in the engine module (speed invalid there) [HIGH]
CAN fault between engine and transmission module (wiring, termination, connector) [MEDIUM]
Engine module software or fault [LOW]
Transmission module faulty [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 400€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: The transmission module needs engine speed for converter slip, shift quality and to check the turbine speed. description: The transmission module divides input (turbine) speed by output speed and compares the result with the ratio of the commanded gear; a deviation means slip – a clutch or brake not holding, too little pressure – or a wrong gear. Thresholds: Ford more than 30 rpm off for 1.8 s three times (diesel 2023: over 20 % for 12 s), GM's 2006 tables and the Allison 1000 converter slip of 200–230 rpm for 2.25 s after one trip, Saab's Aisin boxes over 20 % twelve times without MIL. P0729 concerns sixth gear. Saab's Aisin six-speed also checks whether the actual ratio matches fourth or fifth – the sixth gear clutch is not holding and the box drops into another gear. Ford stores it only if the fault does not fit a particular solenoid (otherwise P0751 ff). On GM manual transmissions (LT4) it checks the gear position sensor instead.
possible_causes: Fluid level too low or fluid worn or contaminated [HIGH]
Clutch for sixth gear worn (linings, piston seal) [HIGH]
Sticking shift or pressure valve, leaking valve body gasket, blocked passages [MEDIUM]
GM manual transmissions only: gear position sensor faulty or not learned [MEDIUM]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 150€ - 3500€ (1h - 14h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

Schwellen: Ford über 30/min Abweichung für 1,8 s dreimal (Diesel 2023: über 20 % für 12 s), GMs Tabellen von 2006 und das Allison 1000 Wandlerschlupf von 200–230/min für 2,25 s nach einer Fahrt, Saabs Aisin-Getriebe über 20 % zwölfmal ohne MIL. Gangs hält nicht, das Getriebe fällt in einen anderen Gang. Ford speichert ihn nur, wenn der Fehler zu keinem bestimmten Magnetventil passt (sonst P0751 ff). Bei GM-Schaltgetrieben (LT4) prüft er stattdessen den Ganghebelsensor.

symptoms: Slipping or flare in sixth gear, engine speed higher than expected

description: Ford's DPS6 dry dual-clutch transmission moves its gears with two electrically driven shift drums whose position is read by Hall sensors: drum A shifts 1st, 3rd and 5th, drum B reverse, 2nd, 4th and 6th. Ford's 2012 summary lists 'stuck in gear' codes for each drum: the module commands the drum out of a gear, but the gear stays engaged. It gives no thresholds or MIL rating. P072A means the transmission stays in neutral although a gear is commanded – no drive. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the DPS6 reports drum position faults under its own codes. On dual-clutch or automated manuals a drum or fork would fail to engage a gear, on planetary automatics clutch pressure would be missing. The opposite is P073D.
possible_causes: Shift fork or synchronizer for this gear sticking [MEDIUM]
Shift drum A motor, Hall position sensing or driver faulty [MEDIUM]
Transmission module [LOW]
On planetary automatics: clutch or brake not releasing (sticking valve) [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 200€ - 3000€ (1h - 10h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: P0730 reports a wrong transmission ratio without assigning it to a gear. Two uses are documented. Older Aisin-type automatics (a 2006 GM table, Saab's 9-5 of 2002) set it when fourth or fifth gear shows the ratio of third – a shift solenoid (Saab: S3) is not switching; GM lights the MIL at once, Saab enters limp mode. GM's continuously variable transmissions of 2023 and 2025 use it when the pulleys do not reach the commanded variator ratio – the belt or chain slips or clamping pressure is too low – after one trip. Ford and newer GM step automatics use gear-specific or clutch valve codes instead. Check fluid level and condition first.

description: The transmission module divides input (turbine) speed by output speed and compares the result with the ratio of the commanded gear; a deviation means slip – a clutch or brake not holding, too little pressure – or a wrong gear. Thresholds: Ford more than 30 rpm off for 1.8 s three times (diesel 2023: over 20 % for 12 s), GM's 2006 tables and the Allison 1000 converter slip of 200–230 rpm for 2.25 s after one trip, Saab's Aisin boxes over 20 % twelve times without MIL. P0731 concerns first gear. A 2006 GM table uses a tighter 4 % limit here and caps output speed at 1260 rpm; Saab's 2002 9-5 flags 3 % with the brake released. With a one-way clutch in first, slip shows as slipping when pulling away. On GM manual transmissions it checks the gear position sensor instead.
possible_causes: Fluid level too low or fluid worn or contaminated [HIGH]
Clutch or brake for first gear worn (linings, piston seal) [HIGH]
Sticking shift or pressure valve, leaking valve body gasket, blocked passages [MEDIUM]
GM manual transmissions only: gear position sensor faulty or not learned [MEDIUM]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 100€ - 3500€ (0.5h - 14h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

description: Some transmission modules pass an engine speed signal on to other devices such as a tachometer over a wire of their own. CARB requires output circuits to be checked. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0737–P0739 – engine speed is shared over CAN today; the description follows CARB and the engine module's own speed output (P0654), which sends, for example, two pulses per revolution. P0737 is the general circuit fault of this output; low and high are P0738/P0739. Not to be confused with the engine speed input at the transmission module (P0725 ff). A tachometer or dependent display then reads wrong or nothing, while driving is usually unaffected.
possible_causes: Wire to the receiver open or shorted [HIGH]
Receiver (e.g. instrument cluster) shorted internally [MEDIUM]
Connector corroded [MEDIUM]
Driver stage in the transmission module faulty [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 300€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

Keine uns vorliegende Herstellerunterlage nutzt P0737–P0739 – die Drehzahl wird heute über CAN verteilt; die Beschreibung folgt CARB und dem Drehzahlausgang des Motorsteuergeräts (P0654), der etwa zwei Impulse je Umdrehung sendet. P0738 heißt: Dieser Ausgang ist zu niedrig, typisch Masseschluss, und kann nicht mehr auf High schalten. Der Gegenfehler ist P0739, der allgemeine Fehler P0737. Drehzahlmesser oder abhängige Anzeigen zeigen dann null oder springen, das Fahren ist meist nicht beeinträchtigt.

description: Some transmission modules pass an engine speed signal on to other devices such as a tachometer over a wire of their own. CARB requires output circuits to be checked. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0737–P0739 – engine speed is shared over CAN today; the description follows CARB and the engine module's own speed output (P0654), which sends, for example, two pulses per revolution. P0739 means this output is too high, typically shorted to positive or, depending on the driver, open, so it can no longer switch to ground. The opposite is P0738, the general fault P0737. A tachometer or dependent display then reads nothing or full scale, while driving is usually unaffected.
possible_causes: Output wire shorted to positive or open [HIGH]
Receiver faulty [MEDIUM]
Connector corroded [MEDIUM]
Driver stage in the transmission module faulty [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 300€ (0.5h - 2h labor). DIY feasible with standard tools.

description: Ford's DPS6 dry dual-clutch transmission moves its gears with two electrically driven shift drums whose position is read by Hall sensors: drum A shifts 1st, 3rd and 5th, drum B reverse, 2nd, 4th and 6th. Ford's 2012 summary lists 'stuck in gear' codes for each drum: the module commands the drum out of a gear, but the gear stays engaged. It gives no thresholds or MIL rating. P073A is the code for drum A: fifth gear cannot be disengaged. The car stays in fifth – very weak pulling away – or sub-gearbox A is locked out. Slip in fifth gear is P0735.
possible_causes: Shift fork or synchronizer for this gear sticking [MEDIUM]
Shift drum A motor, Hall position sensing or driver faulty [MEDIUM]
Transmission module [LOW]
On planetary automatics: clutch or brake not releasing (sticking valve) [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 200€ - 3000€ (1h - 10h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

symptoms: Transmission stays in one gear, no further shifts

description: P073D means neutral is commanded but not reached or not held. GM uses it on vehicles with electronic gear selection (shift-by-wire, e.g. Cadillac XT4): the selector or engine module compares commanded and actual range from the range sensor and flags it after 1.8–2 s in the selector module or 10 s in the engine module, after two trips. For Ford's 6F35 the supplier Sonnax describes a mechanical cause: a forward or direct clutch dragging in neutral, visible as turbine speed staying only 200–400 rpm below engine speed. The car may creep in N; range changes may be locked. The opposite, stuck in neutral, is P072A.
possible_causes: Ford 6F35: forward or direct clutch dragging (balance piston, plates, seal) [HIGH]
Shift-by-wire: range actuator or park module, range sensor or its calibration [MEDIUM]
Valve body (manual valve, missing check ball, sticking solenoid) [MEDIUM]
CAN communication or control module [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 150€ - 3500€ (1h - 12h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_title.en: Unable to Engage Neutral

bilingual_description.en: P073D means neutral is commanded but not reached or not held. GM uses it on vehicles with electronic gear selection (shift-by-wire, e.g. Cadillac XT4): the selector or engine module compares commanded and actual range from the range sensor and flags it after 1.8–2 s in the selector module or 10 s in the engine module, after two trips. For Ford's 6F35 the supplier Sonnax describes a mechanical cause: a forward or direct clutch dragging in neutral, visible as turbine speed staying only 200–400 rpm below engine speed. The car may creep in N; range changes may be locked. The opposite, stuck in neutral, is P072A.
bilingual_description.de: P073D heißt: Neutral ist befohlen, wird aber nicht erreicht oder nicht gehalten. GM nutzt ihn bei elektronischer Fahrstufenwahl (Shift-by-Wire, z. B. Cadillac XT4): Wählmodul bzw. Motorsteuergerät vergleichen die befohlene mit der tatsächlichen Fahrstufe vom Bereichssensor und melden nach 1,8–2 s im Wählmodul bzw. 10 s im Motorsteuergerät, nach zwei Fahrten. Für Fords 6F35 beschreibt der Zulieferer Sonnax eine mechanische Ursache: eine in Neutral schleppende Vorwärts- oder Direktkupplung, erkennbar daran, dass die Turbinendrehzahl nur 200–400/min unter der Motordrehzahl bleibt. Das Fahrzeug kann in N kriechen; Fahrstufenwechsel werden ggf. gesperrt. Das Gegenstück, Hängen in Neutral, ist P072A.

symptoms: Vehicle creeps in N or engine is loaded when shifting to N
N selection not accepted, warning message
Check engine light after two trips (GM)

description: P073E means reverse is commanded but not reached. Two uses are documented. With electronic gear selection (shift-by-wire) GM compares the commanded range with the actual range reported by the transmission and flags it if reverse is not reached within 1.8–3 s in the selector or diesel engine module, or 10 s in petrol engine modules, after two trips; GM bulletins name a range actuator centred wrongly (LaCrosse, XT5) and software after an over-the-air update (2025 Equinox/Terrain). On dual-clutch transmissions (2020–23 Corvette, Maserati MC20) it means the reverse gear cannot be engaged. Stuck in reverse is P072B, slip in reverse P0736.
possible_causes: Range actuator or park module centred wrongly or faulty (shift-by-wire) [HIGH]
Module software (e.g. after an over-the-air update) [MEDIUM]
Range sensor reports the wrong actual range [MEDIUM]
Reverse clutch or brake, valve or shift fork (DCT) [MEDIUM]
Fluid level or system pressure [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 50€ - 5000€ (0.3h - 12h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_title.en: Unable to Engage Reverse

bilingual_description.en: P073E means reverse is commanded but not reached. Two uses are documented. With electronic gear selection (shift-by-wire) GM compares the commanded range with the actual range reported by the transmission and flags it if reverse is not reached within 1.8–3 s in the selector or diesel engine module, or 10 s in petrol engine modules, after two trips; GM bulletins name a range actuator centred wrongly (LaCrosse, XT5) and software after an over-the-air update (2025 Equinox/Terrain). On dual-clutch transmissions (2020–23 Corvette, Maserati MC20) it means the reverse gear cannot be engaged. Stuck in reverse is P072B, slip in reverse P0736.
bilingual_description.de: P073E heißt: Der Rückwärtsgang ist befohlen, wird aber nicht erreicht. Zwei Nutzungen sind belegt. Bei elektronischer Fahrstufenwahl (Shift-by-Wire) vergleicht GM die befohlene mit der vom Getriebe gemeldeten Fahrstufe und meldet, wenn R nicht binnen 1,8–3 s im Wähl- bzw. Diesel-Motorsteuergerät oder 10 s in Benzin-Motorsteuergeräten erreicht wird, nach zwei Fahrten; GM-Bulletins nennen einen falsch zentrierten Fahrstufenaktor (LaCrosse, XT5) und Software nach einem Over-the-Air-Update (Equinox/Terrain 2025). Bei Doppelkupplungsgetrieben (Corvette 2020–23, Maserati MC20) heißt er, dass sich der Rückwärtsgang nicht einlegen lässt. Hängen im Rückwärtsgang ist P072B, Schlupf P0736.

symptoms: No reverse, or R not accepted
Transmission warning, check engine light after two trips (GM)
Display shows R but the vehicle does not reverse

description: 'Unable to engage' means the transmission does not reach the commanded gear – the opposite of 'stuck in gear', where a gear cannot be disengaged. Documented users are dual-clutch transmissions, whose shift forks are moved hydraulically and watched by travel sensors: GM's 8-speed in the 2020–23 Corvette, Maserati's MC20 and – for the odd gears only – Acura's RLX Sport Hybrid, whose 'odd gear monitor' is part of an emission recall with permanent codes. No manufacturer publishes thresholds. P073F means the first gear, on the odd sub-gearbox, cannot be engaged; a gear that will not disengage is P072C, slip in an engaged gear P0731. GM's bulletin first runs a learn procedure and cleans valves only if system pressure codes are present; Maserati checks system pressure (20–30 bar). If neither helps, the mechanics are at fault.
possible_causes: Shift fork valve or solenoid in the mechatronic unit sticking (dirt, wear) [HIGH]
System pressure unstable or too low (pressure valve, pump, fluid level) [MEDIUM]
Shift fork, sleeve, synchronizer or dogs damaged [MEDIUM]
Learned shift fork or clutch values lost or wrong [MEDIUM]
Module software or calibration [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 100€ - 6000€ (0.5h - 12h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_title.en: Unable to Engage Gear 1

bilingual_description.en: 'Unable to engage' means the transmission does not reach the commanded gear – the opposite of 'stuck in gear', where a gear cannot be disengaged. Documented users are dual-clutch transmissions, whose shift forks are moved hydraulically and watched by travel sensors: GM's 8-speed in the 2020–23 Corvette, Maserati's MC20 and – for the odd gears only – Acura's RLX Sport Hybrid, whose 'odd gear monitor' is part of an emission recall with permanent codes. No manufacturer publishes thresholds. P073F means the first gear, on the odd sub-gearbox, cannot be engaged; a gear that will not disengage is P072C, slip in an engaged gear P0731. GM's bulletin first runs a learn procedure and cleans valves only if system pressure codes are present; Maserati checks system pressure (20–30 bar). If neither helps, the mechanics are at fault.
bilingual_description.de: „Unable to Engage“ heißt: Das Getriebe erreicht den befohlenen Gang nicht – das Gegenstück zu „Stuck in Gear“, wo sich ein Gang nicht auslegen lässt. Belegte Nutzer sind Doppelkupplungsgetriebe, deren Schaltgabeln hydraulisch bewegt und von Wegsensoren überwacht werden: GMs Achtgang in der Corvette 2020–23, Maseratis MC20 und – nur für die ungeraden Gänge – Acuras RLX Sport Hybrid, dessen „Odd Gear Monitor“ Teil eines Abgasrückrufs mit permanenten Codes ist. Schwellen veröffentlicht kein Hersteller. P073F heißt: Der 1. Gang im ungeraden Teilgetriebe lässt sich nicht einlegen; ein Gang, der sich nicht auslegen lässt, ist P072C, Schlupf im eingelegten Gang P0731. GMs Bulletin lässt zuerst einen Lernlauf fahren und reinigt Ventile nur bei begleitenden Systemdruckcodes; Maserati prüft den Systemdruck (20–30 bar). Hilft beides nicht, ist die Mechanik defekt.

symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light, possibly limp mode with one sub-gearbox locked out
Jerking, delayed pulling away or shifting

description: The torque converter clutch (lock-up) connects pump and turbine mechanically; a solenoid – on/off, pulse-width modulated or proportional – moves a control valve in the valve body. Slip is engine speed minus turbine speed. Manufacturers do not use P0740–P0744 uniformly: Ford uses P0740 for open, P0742 for short to ground and P0744 for short to power, and reports stuck on as P2758. P0740 concerns the control circuit of the converter clutch solenoid. Ford flags an open circuit when the driver feedback line disagrees with the command for 0.5–5 s, with MIL; a 2006 GM table checks 0/12 V with more than 43 of 50 failed counts after two trips – newer GM units use P2761/P2763/P2764. FCA's Ram 6.7 reads P0740 as converter slip out of range and moved it to two trips by software in 2013. The clutch is then switched off: higher engine speed when cruising, more fuel, hotter fluid.
possible_causes: Open or corroded harness or transmission pass-through connector [HIGH]
Converter clutch solenoid coil open [MEDIUM]
Internal transmission harness or mechatronic unit [MEDIUM]
Driver stage in the module faulty [LOW]
FCA: actual converter slip (clutch wear, fluid) or software [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 80€ - 900€ (1h - 4h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_title.en: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit/Open

bilingual_description.en: The torque converter clutch (lock-up) connects pump and turbine mechanically; a solenoid – on/off, pulse-width modulated or proportional – moves a control valve in the valve body. Slip is engine speed minus turbine speed. Manufacturers do not use P0740–P0744 uniformly: Ford uses P0740 for open, P0742 for short to ground and P0744 for short to power, and reports stuck on as P2758. P0740 concerns the control circuit of the converter clutch solenoid. Ford flags an open circuit when the driver feedback line disagrees with the command for 0.5–5 s, with MIL; a 2006 GM table checks 0/12 V with more than 43 of 50 failed counts after two trips – newer GM units use P2761/P2763/P2764. FCA's Ram 6.7 reads P0740 as converter slip out of range and moved it to two trips by software in 2013. The clutch is then switched off: higher engine speed when cruising, more fuel, hotter fluid.
bilingual_description.de: Die Wandlerüberbrückungskupplung verbindet Pumpenrad und Turbine mechanisch; ein Magnetventil – Ein/Aus, getaktet oder proportional – verstellt ein Regelventil im Ventilkörper. Schlupf ist Motor- minus Turbinendrehzahl. Die Hersteller belegen P0740–P0744 nicht einheitlich: Ford nutzt P0740 für Unterbrechung, P0742 für Masseschluss und P0744 für Plusschluss und meldet „hängt ein“ als P2758. P0740 betrifft den Steuerkreis des Wandlerkupplungsventils. Ford meldet eine Unterbrechung, wenn die Rückmeldeleitung der Endstufe 0,5–5 s nicht zum Befehl passt, mit MIL; eine GM-Tabelle von 2006 prüft 0/12 V, über 43 von 50 Fehlzählungen, zwei Fahrten – neuere GM-Getriebe nutzen P2761/P2763/P2764. FCAs Ram 6.7 versteht P0740 als Wandlerschlupf außerhalb des Bereichs und stellte ihn 2013 per Software auf zwei Fahrten um. Die Kupplung wird dann abgeschaltet: höhere Drehzahl, Mehrverbrauch, heißeres Öl.

symptoms: Check engine light or transmission warning
No lock-up: engine speed about 100–300 rpm higher when cruising
Higher fuel consumption, hotter transmission fluid

description: P0741 means the converter clutch does not lock although commanded – slip stays too high while the circuit is electrically fine. Thresholds: GM's T43 at least 130 rpm for 5 s twice, the 6T70 50 rpm for 5 s three times, Saab's Aisin AF40 over 100 rpm for 2 s, all after two trips; Ford over 100–200 rpm or a speed ratio below 0.93 over five lock-up events; Subaru engine speed more than 9/8 of target for 10.2 s. The module then locks out the clutch, sometimes the top gear, and uses a hot-mode shift pattern. Low or burnt fluid, a worn control valve in the valve body and a glazed converter clutch are the usual causes; Hyundai's 8-speed bulletin calls for a new converter.
possible_causes: Fluid level too low, old or burnt fluid [HIGH]
Converter clutch control valve worn or sticking, bore worn [HIGH]
Lock-up clutch in the converter worn or glazed [MEDIUM]
Solenoid mechanically sluggish (electrically fine) [MEDIUM]
Leaking turbine shaft seals or pump [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 150€ - 3000€ (1h - 10h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_title.en: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Performance/Stuck Off

bilingual_description.en: P0741 means the converter clutch does not lock although commanded – slip stays too high while the circuit is electrically fine. Thresholds: GM's T43 at least 130 rpm for 5 s twice, the 6T70 50 rpm for 5 s three times, Saab's Aisin AF40 over 100 rpm for 2 s, all after two trips; Ford over 100–200 rpm or a speed ratio below 0.93 over five lock-up events; Subaru engine speed more than 9/8 of target for 10.2 s. The module then locks out the clutch, sometimes the top gear, and uses a hot-mode shift pattern. Low or burnt fluid, a worn control valve in the valve body and a glazed converter clutch are the usual causes; Hyundai's 8-speed bulletin calls for a new converter.
bilingual_description.de: P0741 heißt: Die Wandlerkupplung schließt trotz Befehl nicht – der Schlupf bleibt zu hoch, obwohl der Kreis elektrisch in Ordnung ist. Schwellen: GMs T43 mindestens 130/min für 5 s zweimal, das 6T70 50/min für 5 s dreimal, Saabs Aisin AF40 über 100/min für 2 s, alle nach zwei Fahrten; Ford über 100–200/min oder ein Drehzahlverhältnis unter 0,93 über fünf Überbrückungen; Subaru Motordrehzahl über 9/8 des Sollwerts für 10,2 s. Das Steuergerät sperrt dann die Kupplung, teils den höchsten Gang, und schaltet nach Heiß-Programm. Meist sind zu wenig oder verbranntes Öl, ein verschlissenes Regelventil im Ventilkörper oder eine verglaste Wandlerkupplung die Ursache; Hyundais Achtgang-Bulletin verlangt einen neuen Wandler.

symptoms: Check engine light or transmission warning
Higher engine speed when cruising, 'rubber band' feel
Possibly shudder when the clutch applies

description: P0742 means the converter clutch stays applied although commanded off – there is almost no slip. GM's T43 flags −50 to +13 rpm for 1.5 s six times and the 6T70 −20 to +30 rpm for 2.5 s, both after one trip; Allison and Saab's Aisin AF40 after two trips, the AF40 also when the engine stalls without slip. Typical is the engine stalling when stopping or when selecting D or R, plus jerking at low speed. Note the different uses: Ford's P0742 is a short to ground in the clutch solenoid circuit (stuck on is P2758 there), and Saab's 9-3 of 2003 uses it for a mechanical lock-up fault.
possible_causes: Converter clutch control valve sticking in the applied position [HIGH]
Solenoid stuck open (or short to ground with low-side control) [MEDIUM]
Lock-up clutch seized in the converter [MEDIUM]
Wrong fluid level or contaminated fluid [MEDIUM]
Engine or turbine speed signal implausible [LOW]
garage_advice: Estimated repair: 200€ - 3000€ (1.5h - 10h labor). Professional workshop recommended.

bilingual_title.en: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Stuck On

bilingual_description.en: P0742 means the converter clutch stays applied although commanded off – there is almost no slip. GM's T43 flags −50 to +13 rpm for 1.5 s six times and the 6T70 −20 to +30 rpm for 2.5 s, both after one trip; Allison and Saab's Aisin AF40 after two trips, the AF40 also when the engine stalls without slip. Typical is the engine stalling when stopping or when selecting D or R, plus jerking at low speed. Note the different uses: Ford's P0742 is a short to ground in the clutch solenoid circuit (stuck on is P2758 there), and Saab's 9-3 of 2003 uses it for a mechanical lock-up fault.
bilingual_description.de: P0742 heißt: Die Wandlerkupplung bleibt geschlossen, obwohl sie aus sein soll – es gibt fast keinen Schlupf. GMs T43 meldet −50 bis +13/min für 1,5 s sechsmal, das 6T70 −20 bis +30/min für 2,5 s, beide nach einer Fahrt; Allison und Saabs Aisin AF40 nach zwei Fahrten, das AF40 auch, wenn der Motor ohne Schlupf abwürgt. Typisch ist, dass der Motor beim Anhalten oder beim Einlegen von D oder R abstirbt, dazu Ruckeln bei niedriger Geschwindigkeit. Abweichende Belegung: Fords P0742 ist ein Masseschluss im Kreis des Kupplungsventils („hängt ein“ ist dort P2758), und Saabs 9-3 von 2003 nutzt ihn für einen mechanischen Überbrückungsfehler.

symptoms: Engine stalls when stopping or selecting D/R

description: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. description: 'Unable to engage' means the transmission does not reach the commanded gear – the opposite of 'stuck in gear', where a gear cannot be disengaged. Documented users are dual-clutch transmissions, whose shift forks are moved hydraulically and watched by travel sensors: GM's 8-speed in the 2020–23 Corvette, Maserati's MC20 and – for the odd gears only – Acura's RLX Sport Hybrid, whose 'odd gear monitor' is part of an emission recall with permanent codes. No manufacturer publishes thresholds. P074A means the second gear, on the even sub-gearbox, cannot be engaged; a gear that will not disengage is P072D, slip in an engaged gear P0732. GM's bulletin first runs a learn procedure and cleans valves only if system pressure codes are present; Maserati checks system pressure (20–30 bar). If neither helps, the mechanics are at fault.
possible_causes: Shift fork valve or solenoid in the mechatronic unit sticking (dirt, wear) [HIGH]
System pressure unstable or too low (pressure valve, pump, fluid level) [MEDIUM]
Shift fork, sleeve, synchronizer or dogs damaged [MEDIUM]
Learned shift fork or clutch values lost or wrong [MEDIUM]
Module software or calibration [LOW]
